15.6.8.a.m: There is no preparation for this, says another [view].

15.6.9.a.m: Here he puts the curd on [the fire].

15.6.10.a.m: Then, taking this sovereign-seat and carrying it along the front of the āhavanīya, he sets it down in front of the king's seat.

15.6.11.a.s: tasyāṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīrya tasminnapracaraṇīyau mahāvīrāvupāvaharati deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tveti
15.6.11.a.d: तस्यां कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्नप्रचरणीयौ महावीरावुपावहरति देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वेति
15.6.11.a.m: Having spread a black-antelope skin upon it with the neck pointing east and the hair facing up, he brings down the two mahāvīra pots not used for the proceeding upon it with: "O god, going in front, may I be equal to you!"

15.6.12.a.m: This mantra is [used] at a later time, says another [view].

15.6.13.a.s: athaitāṃ methīṃ mayūkhānviśākhadāmānītyādāyāgreṇa hotāraṃ jaghanena gārhapatyaṃ dakṣiṇayā dvāropanirhṛtya dakṣiṇena dakṣiṇaṃ dvāraṃ methīṃ nihanti hotuḥ samīkṣāyai
15.6.13.a.d: अथैतां मेथीं मयूखान्विशाखदामानीत्यादायाग्रेण होतारं जघनेन गार्हपत्यं दक्षिणया द्वारोपनिर्हृत्य दक्षिणेन दक्षिणं द्वारं मेथीं निहन्ति होतुः समीक्षायै
15.6.13.a.m: Then, taking this peg, the pegs, and the branching tethers, having carried [them] out in front of the hotṛ, behind the gārhapatya, by the southern door, he drives in the peg south of the southern door for the hotṛ's view.

15.6.14.a.s: etasyaiva dvārasya pūrvasyai dvāryāyai dakṣiṇato vatsāya śaṅkum
15.6.14.a.d: एतस्यैव द्वारस्य पूर्वस्यै द्वार्यायै दक्षिणतो वत्साय शङ्कुम्
15.6.14.a.m: To the south of the eastern door-post of this very door, a peg for the calf.

15.6.15.a.m: To the south of the western door-post of this very [door], [a peg] on the inside for the goat.

15.6.17.a.m: He fastens the branching tethers to them.

15.6.18.a.m: They remain fastened until the final disposal.

15.6.19.a.m: With them they tie these [animals] at the proper time.

15.6.20.a.m: Then he scatters the mounds [of sand]:

15.6.21.a.m: One to the north of the gārhapatya;

15.6.21.b.m: One to the north of the āhavanīya.

15.6.22.a.s: uttarapūrvaṃ dvāraṃ pratyucchiṣṭakharaṃ karoti bāhyato niḥṣecanavantam
15.6.22.a.d: उत्तरपूर्वं द्वारं प्रत्युच्छिष्टखरं करोति बाह्यतो निःषेचनवन्तम्
15.6.22.a.m: Facing the north-eastern door, he makes the remnant-mound with an outlet on the outside.

15.6.23.a.m: To the north of the āhavanīya he places the heated curd,

15.7.1.a.m: The splinters, and the thorny fuel-stick.

15.7.2.a.s: athaitaṃ pracaraṇīyaṃ mahāvīraṃ śaphābhyāṃ parigṛhyāpracchinnāgreṇa vedenopariṣṭātsaṃmārṣṭi deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tveti
15.7.2.a.d: अथैतं प्रचरणीयं महावीरं शफाभ्यां परिगृह्याप्रच्छिन्नाग्रेण वेदेनोपरिष्टात्संमार्ष्टि देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वेति
15.7.2.a.m: Then, grasping this mahāvīra [pot] to be used for the proceeding with the two pairs of tongs, he wipes it from above with the grass broom whose tips are uncut, with: "O god, going in front, may I be equal to you!"

15.7.3.a.s: prāṇāya svāha vyānāya svāheti sruveṇāhavanīye saptaikādaśa vā prāṇāhutīrhutvā devastvā savitā madhvānaktviti sruveṇoparyāhavanīye mahāvīramaktvā pṛthivīṃ tapasastrāyasvetyaparasminkhare rājataṃ rukmaṃ nidhāya pratiṣṭhāpya mahāvīramanyasmai vā pradāya dvayānmuñjapralavānādāya dakṣiṇeṣāmagrāṇi gārhapatye pradīpayatyarciṣe tveti /
15.7.3.a.d: प्राणाय स्वाह व्यानाय स्वाहेति स्रुवेणाहवनीये सप्तैकादश वा प्राणाहुतीर्हुत्वा देवस्त्वा सविता मध्वानक्त्विति स्रुवेणोपर्याहवनीये महावीरमक्त्वा पृथिवीं तपसस्त्रायस्वेत्यपरस्मिन्खरे राजतं रुक्मं निधाय प्रतिष्ठाप्य महावीरमन्यस्मै वा प्रदाय द्वयान्मुञ्जप्रलवानादाय दक्षिणेषामग्राणि गार्हपत्ये प्रदीपयत्यर्चिषे त्वेति ।
15.7.3.a.m: Having offered seven or eleven life-breath offerings in the āhavanīya with the dipping spoon, with: "To the out-breath, svāhā! To the all-pervading breath, svāhā!" and having anointed the mahāvīra over the āhavanīya with the dipping spoon, with: "May god Savitṛ anoint you with honey!", having laid down the silver plate on the western mound with: "Protect the earth from heat!", having firmly set the mahāvīra [there] or handed [it] over to someone else, having taken two tufts of muñja grass, he sets alight the tips of the southern ones in the gārhapatya with: "To the flame, you!";

15.7.3.b.m: With their tips, the bases of the northern ones with: "To the blaze, you!";

15.7.3.c.m: With their bases, the bases of the southern ones with: "To the light, you!";

15.7.3.d.m: With their bases, the tips of the northern ones with: "To the heat, you!"

15.7.4.a.s: tānvyatyastānupari rukme nidadhātyarcirasi śocirasi jyotirasi tapo 'sīti
15.7.4.a.d: तान्व्यत्यस्तानुपरि रुक्मे निदधात्यर्चिरसि शोचिरसि ज्योतिरसि तपो ऽसीति
15.7.4.a.m: He places them crosswise upon the gold plate with: "Flame you are, blaze you are, light you are, heat you are!"

15.7.5.a.s: saṃsīdasva mahām̐ asīti teṣu mahāvīraṃ pratiṣṭhāpyāñjanti yaṃ prathayanta iti sruveṇa mahāvīramanakti /
15.7.5.a.d: संसीदस्व महाम्̐ असीति तेषु महावीरं प्रतिष्ठाप्याञ्जन्ति यं प्रथयन्त इति स्रुवेण महावीरमनक्ति ।
15.7.5.a.m: Having firmly placed the mahāvīra pot upon them with: "Sit down, great are you!", he anoints the mahāvīra pot with the dipping spoon with: "They anoint [the steed], whom they spread out...";

15.7.6.a.s: adhyadhi mahāvīramasaṃspṛśanyajamānaḥ prāñcaṃ prādeśaṃ dhārayamāṇo japatyanādhṛṣyā purastādityetairyathāliṅgam
15.7.6.a.d: अध्यधि महावीरमसंस्पृशन्यजमानः प्राञ्चं प्रादेशं धारयमाणो जपत्यनाधृष्या पुरस्तादित्येतैर्यथालिङ्गम्
15.7.6.a.m: Above the mahāvīra, without touching it, holding his span pointing east, the sacrificer mutters according to their characteristic markers with these [formulas]: "Unassailable from the east...".

15.7.7.a.m: With: "You are Manu's mare, rich in offspring," he touches the earth to the north.

15.7.8.a.s: siddhyai tveti dhṛṣṭī ādatto 'dhvaryuḥ pratiprasthātā ca
15.7.8.a.d: सिद्ध्यै त्वेति धृष्टी आदत्तो ऽध्वर्युः प्रतिप्रस्थाता च
15.7.8.a.m: With: "For accomplishment, you!" the adhvaryu and the pratiprasthātṛ take up the two fire-pokers.

15.7.9.a.s: tapo ṣvagne antarām̐ amitrāniti gārhapatyādudīco 'ṅgārānnirūhya citaḥ stha paricita iti pradakṣiṇamaṅgāraiḥ paryūhya
15.7.9.a.d: तपो ष्वग्ने अन्तराम्̐ अमित्रानिति गार्हपत्यादुदीचो ऽङ्गारान्निरूह्य चितः स्थ परिचित इति प्रदक्षिणमङ्गारैः पर्यूह्य
15.7.9.a.m: Having scraped out embers from the gārhapatya towards the north with: "Burn down, O Agni, the enemies within!", having surrounded [the mahāvīra] with embers clockwise with: "Piled up are you, piled around [are you]!",

15.8.1.a.m: They enclose [it] with the enclosing sticks of vikankata wood.

15.8.2.a.m: The adhvaryu lays down two pointing east with: "Measure you are!"

15.8.2.b.m: The pratiprasthātṛ [sets down] two towards the north with: "Thou art the measure."

15.8.3.a.m: Thus, of the remaining [spoons], the adhvaryu [sets down each] with the preceding formula;

15.8.4.a.m: The adhvaryu alone puts down the thirteenth to the south with: "Thou art the concealment of the midspace."

15.8.5.a.s: divaṃ tapasastrāyasveti sauvarṇena rukmeṇāpidhāyābhirgīrbhiriti tisṛbhirabhimantrya dhavitrāṇyādatte /
15.8.5.a.d: दिवं तपसस्त्रायस्वेति सौवर्णेन रुक्मेणापिधायाभिर्गीर्भिरिति तिसृभिरभिमन्त्र्य धवित्राण्यादत्ते ।
15.8.5.a.m: Having covered [the mahāvīra] with the golden plate with [the formula], "Protect the sky from heat," and having consecrated it with the three [verses], "With these songs...", he takes the fans.

15.8.5.b.m: [He takes] the first [fan] with, "You are of the gāyatrī."

15.8.5.c.m: The second with, "You are of the triṣṭubh."

15.8.6.a.m: With them he fans it upwards three times with, "Sweet, sweet!"

15.8.7.a.m: He hands one of them to the pratiprasthātṛ,

15.8.8.a.m: With the agnīdh first, fanning upwards, they go around clockwise three times.

15.8.9.a.m: Facing it, they sit around it:

15.8.10.a.s: avyatiṣaṅgamūrdhvaṃ dhūnvantaḥ praṇavaiḥ saṃrādhayanta indhānāḥ samañjanto vāgyatā āsate
15.8.10.a.d: अव्यतिषङ्गमूर्ध्वं धून्वन्तः प्रणवैः संराधयन्त इन्धानाः समञ्जन्तो वाग्यता आसते
15.8.10.a.m: Fanning upwards without intercrossing, propitiating with om-calls, kindling [the fire], anointing [it with clarified butter], they sit, restraining their speech.

15.8.11.a.m: It is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: "When it is blazing up, he removes the plate."

15.8.12.a.s: yatrābhijānāti yābhir vartikāṃ grasitām amuñcatam iti tad adhvaryur mahāvīram abhimantrayate daśa prācīr daśa bhāsi dakṣiṇety anuvākena
15.8.12.a.d: यत्राभिजानाति याभिर् वर्तिकां ग्रसिताम् अमुञ्चतम् इति तद् अध्वर्युर् महावीरम् अभिमन्त्रयते दश प्राचीर् दश भासि दक्षिणेत्य् अनुवाकेन
15.8.12.a.m: When he recognises [the verse], "With which you released the swallowed quail...", then the adhvaryu consecrates the mahāvīra with the section, "Ten eastward, ten you shine to the south..."

15.8.13.a.s: yatrābhijānāty apnasvatīm aśvinā vācam asme iti tad upottiṣṭhann adhvaryur āha rucito gharma iti
15.8.13.a.d: यत्राभिजानात्य् अप्नस्वतीम् अश्विना वाचम् अस्मे इति तद् उपोत्तिष्ठन्न् अध्वर्युर् आह रुचितो घर्म इति
15.8.13.a.m: When he recognises [the verse], "Bestowing property, Aśvins, [may] speech [be] in us...", then rising up, the adhvaryu says: "The gharma has shone!"

15.8.14.a.m: With the adhvaryu first, not fanning it, they go around it three times in reverse.

15.8.15.a.m: Taking the fans, the adhvaryu gives them to the pratiprasthātṛ.

15.8.15.b.m: Bringing them around in front of the āhavanīya, the pratiprasthātṛ places them on the sovereign's throne.

15.8.16.a.s: yathālokamavasthāya sarva ṛtvijo yajamānaścādhīyanto mahāvīramavekṣante 'paśyaṃ gopāmiti
15.8.16.a.d: यथालोकमवस्थाय सर्व ऋत्विजो यजमानश्चाधीयन्तो महावीरमवेक्षन्ते ऽपश्यं गोपामिति
15.8.16.a.m: Standing in their respective places, all the officiating priests and the sacrificer, reciting, look at the mahāvīra with, "I saw the herdsman..."

15.8.17.a.s: anuvākaśeṣaṃ tu pariśrite pratiprasthātā patnīṃ vācayati tvaṣṭīmatī te sapeyeti
15.8.17.a.d: अनुवाकशेषं तु परिश्रिते प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्नीं वाचयति त्वष्टीमती ते सपेयेति
15.8.17.a.m: With the remainder of the section, however, inside the enclosed space, the pratiprasthātṛ makes the wife recite, "Accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ, may I serve you..."

15.9.1.a.m: Then he issues the call: "Agnīdh, set down the two rauhiṇa cakes!"

15.9.2.a.m: On two ladles that are not tied, he sets down the two cakes after spreading [clarified butter beneath] and pouring [clarified butter over them]:

15.9.2.b.m: one along the southern junction of the enclosing sticks,

15.9.2.c.m: the other along the northern junction of the enclosing sticks.

15.9.3.a.s: sāvitreṇa raśanāmādāyādityai rāsnāsītyabhimantrya pūrvayā dvāropaniṣkramya trirupāṃśu gharmadughamāhvayatīḍa ehyadita ehi sarasvatyehīti
15.9.3.a.d: सावित्रेण रशनामादायादित्यै रास्नासीत्यभिमन्त्र्य पूर्वया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्य त्रिरुपांशु घर्मदुघमाह्वयतीड एह्यदित एहि सरस्वत्येहीति
15.9.3.a.m: Taking the cord with [the verse addressed] to Savitṛ, consecrating it with, "You are the girdle of Aditi," and stepping out by the eastern door, he calls the gharma-cow three times in a low voice: "Iḍā, come! Aditi, come! Sarasvatī, come!"

15.9.4.a.s: pratyetya dogdhre nidāne ityādāya dakṣiṇayā dvāropaniṣkramya triruccairasāvehyasāvehīti yathānāmā bhavati
15.9.4.a.d: प्रत्येत्य दोग्ध्रे निदाने इत्यादाय दक्षिणया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्य त्रिरुच्चैरसावेह्यसावेहीति यथानामा भवति
15.9.4.a.m: Returning and taking the milking pail and the tether, and stepping out by the southern door, he calls three times aloud, "N.N., come! N.N., come!", using whatever name she has.

15.9.5.a.m: With the cord, he ties the gharma-cow with, "You are the turban of Aditi,"

15.9.5.b.m: and the calf with, "You are Vāyu, offspring of Iḍā."

15.9.6.a.s: pūṣā tvopāvasṛjatvityupāvasṛjya yaste stanaḥ śaśaya iti gharmadughamabhimantrayate
15.9.6.a.d: पूषा त्वोपावसृजत्वित्युपावसृज्य यस्ते स्तनः शशय इति घर्मदुघमभिमन्त्रयते
15.9.6.a.m: Having released [the calf] with, "May Pūṣan release you to [her]!", he addresses the gharma-cow with, "That teat of yours which is swelling..."

15.9.7.a.s: usra gharmaṃ śiṃṣosra gharmaṃ pāhi gharmāya śiṃṣeti nidāya vatsaṃ bṛhaspatistvopasīdatvityupasīdati
15.9.7.a.d: उस्र घर्मं शिंषोस्र घर्मं पाहि घर्माय शिंषेति निदाय वत्सं बृहस्पतिस्त्वोपसीदत्वित्युपसीदति
15.9.7.a.m: Tethering the calf with, "O bright cow, leave a remainder for the gharma; O bright cow, protect the gharma; leave a remainder for the gharma!", he sits down by her with, "May Bṛhaspati sit beside you!"

15.9.8.a.s: dānavaḥ stha perava iti stanānasaṃmṛśyāśvibhyāṃ pinvasva sarasvatyai pinvasva pūṣṇe pinvasva bṛhaspataye pinvasvendrāya pinvasvendrāya pinvasveti varṣīyasi dogdhre dogdhi
15.9.8.a.d: दानवः स्थ पेरव इति स्तनानसंमृश्याश्विभ्यां पिन्वस्व सरस्वत्यै पिन्वस्व पूष्णे पिन्वस्व बृहस्पतये पिन्वस्वेन्द्राय पिन्वस्वेन्द्राय पिन्वस्वेति वर्षीयसि दोग्ध्रे दोग्धि
15.9.8.a.m: Without rubbing the teats, with, "You are liberal, swelling," he milks into the larger milking pail with, "Swell for the two Aśvins! Swell for Sarasvatī! Swell for Pūṣan! Swell for Bṛhaspati! Swell for Indra! Swell for Indra!"

15.9.9.a.m: Silently the pratiprasthātṛ [milks] the goat into the smaller [milking vessel].

15.9.10.a.s: yatrābhijānātyuttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata iti tadupottiṣṭhantāvagnīdhe payasī pradāya pūrvāvatidutya śaphopayamānādadāte /
15.9.10.a.d: यत्राभिजानात्युत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पत इति तदुपोत्तिष्ठन्तावग्नीधे पयसी प्रदाय पूर्वावतिदुत्य शफोपयमानाददाते ।
15.9.10.a.m: When he recognises [the verse], "Arise, Brahmaṇaspati!", then the two, rising up and handing the two milks to the agnīdh, having run past as before, take the tongs and the supportive ladle.

15.9.10.b.m: [The adhvaryu takes] the first [tong] with, "You are of the gāyatrī."

15.9.10.c.m: The second with, "You are of the triṣṭubh."

15.9.10.d.m: The pratiprasthātṛ [takes] the supportive ladle with, "You are of the jagatī."

15.9.11.a.m: When he recognises [the verse], "Run forward with the milk, cow-milker!", then the agnīdh enters.

15.9.12.a.s: sahorjo bhāgenopa mehīti paya āhriyamāṇaṃ pratīkṣate
15.9.12.a.d: सहोर्जो भागेनोप मेहीति पय आह्रियमाणं प्रतीक्षते
15.9.12.a.m: He looks at the milk as it is being brought with, "Come near to me with a share of vigor and strength!"

15.10.1.a.s: indrāśvinā madhunaḥ sāraghasyeti mahāvīre gopaya ānayati
15.10.1.a.d: इन्द्राश्विना मधुनः सारघस्येति महावीरे गोपय आनयति
15.10.1.a.m: With, "Indra and the two Aśvins, of the sweet bee-honey...", he pours the cow's milk into the mahāvīra.

15.10.2.a.s: svāhā tvā sūryasya raśmaye vṛṣṭivanaye juhomītyudyantamūṣmāṇamanumantrayate
15.10.2.a.d: स्वाहा त्वा सूर्यस्य रश्मये वृष्टिवनये जुहोमीत्युद्यन्तमूष्माणमनुमन्त्रयते
15.10.2.a.m: He addresses the rising vapor with, "Svāhā! I sacrifice you to the ray of the sun, the winner of rain!"

15.10.3.a.m: [He pours in] the goat's milk with, "You are the sweet oblation."

15.10.4.a.m: Some teach the pouring in of the goat's milk first.

15.10.5.a.m: [He addresses] the vapor with, "Burn with the heat of the sun!"

15.10.6.a.s: dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ tvā parigṛhṇāmīti śaphābhyāṃ mahāvīraṃ parigṛhya pracchinnāgreṇa vedena bhasma pramṛjyāntarikṣeṇa tvopayacchāmītyupayamanena pratiprasthātopayacchati
15.10.6.a.d: द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां त्वा परिगृह्णामीति शफाभ्यां महावीरं परिगृह्य प्रच्छिन्नाग्रेण वेदेन भस्म प्रमृज्यान्तरिक्षेण त्वोपयच्छामीत्युपयमनेन प्रतिप्रस्थातोपयच्छति
15.10.6.a.m: Grasping the mahāvīra with the two tongs with, "I grasp you with heaven and earth," and brushing off the ashes with the brush having trimmed ends, the pratiprasthātṛ supports it with the supportive ladle with, "I support you with the intermediate space."

15.10.7.a.s: devānāṃ tvā pitṝṇāmanumato bhartuṃ śakeyamityādāyotthāya tejo 'si tejo 'nuprehīti harati
15.10.7.a.d: देवानां त्वा पितॄणामनुमतो भर्तुं शकेयमित्यादायोत्थाय तेजो ऽसि तेजो ऽनुप्रेहीति हरति
15.10.7.a.m: Lifting it with, "Permitted by the gods and ancestors, may I be able to bear you," and having risen, he carries it with, "You are splendor; go along with splendor!"

15.10.8.a.s: vrajannanavānaṃ pañca vātanāmāni vyācaṣṭe samudrāya tvā vātāya svāheti
15.10.8.a.d: व्रजन्ननवानं पञ्च वातनामानि व्याचष्टे समुद्राय त्वा वाताय स्वाहेति
15.10.8.a.m: Walking without taking a breath, he pronounces the five names of the wind: "Svāhā to you, the ocean-wind!"

15.10.9.a.m: Having exhaled, [he pronounces] the five subsequent ones: "Svāhā to you, Agni accompanied by the Vasus!"

15.10.10.a.s: etasminkāle pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇaṃ rauhiṇaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ juhotyaharjyotiḥ ketunā juṣatāṃ sujyotirjyotiṣāṃ svāheti
15.10.10.a.d: एतस्मिन्काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणं रौहिणं प्रतिष्ठितं जुहोत्यहर्ज्योतिः केतुना जुषतां सुज्योतिर्ज्योतिषां स्वाहेति
15.10.10.a.m: At this time the pratiprasthātṛ offers the southern rauhiṇa [cake] while it rests [in the ladle], with, "May the day-light enjoy with its banner, well-light of lights, svāhā!"

15.10.11.a.m: Stepping across to the south behind the āhavanīya, he looks at the brahman with, "All the quarters, sitting to the south..."

15.10.11.b.m: He looks at the hotṛ with, "He has sacrificed to all the gods here."

15.10.11.c.s: svāhākṛtasya gharmasyeti gharmamabhimantryāśrāvya pratyāśrāvite saṃpreṣyati gharmasya yajeti /
15.10.11.c.d: स्वाहाकृतस्य घर्मस्येति घर्ममभिमन्त्र्याश्राव्य प्रत्याश्राविते संप्रेष्यति घर्मस्य यजेति ।
15.10.11.c.m: Addressing the gharma with, "Of the gharma consecrated with svāhā...", calling for recitation and when the response has been made, he issues the call: "Recite the consecratory verse for the gharma!"

15.10.11.d.m: When the vaṣaṭ-call is uttered, he offers with, "Aśvins, drink the gharma!"

15.10.11.e.m: When the secondary vaṣaṭ-call is uttered, [he offers] with, "Svāhā! To Indra vaṭ!"

15.10.12.a.m: Having paid reverence with the remainder of the section, "You two drank the gharma, Aśvins...", while it is held above the āhavanīya, the pratiprasthātṛ fills it up with boiled curds.

15.10.13.a.m: He addresses it as it overflows with, "Swell for food, swell for strength!"

15.11.1.a.s: athainaṃ diśo 'nu prahāvayati tviṣyai tvā dyumnāya tvendriyāya tvā bhūtyai tveti
15.11.1.a.d: अथैनं दिशो ऽनु प्रहावयति त्विष्यै त्वा द्युम्नाय त्वेन्द्रियाय त्वा भूत्यै त्वेति
15.11.1.a.m: Then he makes it move along toward the directions with, "For splendor to you, for glory to you, for vigor to you, for prosperity to you!"

15.11.2.a.s: pratyākramyopayamane śeṣamānīyāntarvedyupayamanaṃ nidhāya pūrvasminkhare rājataṃ rukmaṃ nidhāya tasminmahāvīraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati dharmāsi sudharmāmenyasme brahmāṇi dhārayeti /
15.11.2.a.d: प्रत्याक्रम्योपयमने शेषमानीयान्तर्वेद्युपयमनं निधाय पूर्वस्मिन्खरे राजतं रुक्मं निधाय तस्मिन्महावीरं प्रतिष्ठापयति धर्मासि सुधर्मामेन्यस्मे ब्रह्माणि धारयेति ।
15.11.2.a.m: Having stepped back and poured the remainder into the supportive ladle, having set down the supportive ladle inside the altar ground, and having placed the silver plate on the eastern mound, he sets down the mahāvīra firmly on it with, "You are order, possessing good order; hold firmly in us priestly powers!"

15.11.2.b.m: "Hold firmly royal powers!" for a nobleman.

15.11.2.c.m: "Hold firmly the common people!" for a vaiśya.

15.11.4.a.m: If he would practice sorcery, he should set it down with: 'I set thee down upon the breath of so-and-so.'

15.11.5.a.m: Thereupon the pratiprasthātṛ offers the second rauhiṇa [cake] as before.

15.11.6.a.d: अथैताञ्छकलानुपयमने ऽञ्जञ्जुहोति पूष्णे शरसे स्वाहेत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
15.11.6.a.m: Then, anointing these chips on the upayamana, he offers them, each with its respective mantra, with: 'To Pūṣan of the cream, svāhā!'

15.11.7.a.s: ṣaṣṭhaṃ śakalaṃ sarveṣu lepeṣvaktvānanvīkṣamāṇa udañcaṃ nirasyati rudrāya rudrahotre svāheti
15.11.7.a.d: षष्ठं शकलं सर्वेषु लेपेष्वक्त्वानन्वीक्षमाण उदञ्चं निरस्यति रुद्राय रुद्रहोत्रे स्वाहेति
15.11.7.a.m: Having anointed the sixth chip in all the remainders, not looking back, he casts it to the north with: 'To Rudra, the Rudra-hotṛ, svāhā!'

15.11.8.a.m: Some teach [the offering of] the chips before the rauhiṇa offering.

15.11.9.a.s: athāpa upaspṛśya tūṣṇīṃ kāṇṭakīṃ samidhamādhāyaitasmādeva śeṣādupayamanenāgnihotraṃ juhoti bhūḥ svāheti /
15.11.9.a.d: अथाप उपस्पृश्य तूष्णीं काण्टकीं समिधमाधायैतस्मादेव शेषादुपयमनेनाग्निहोत्रं जुहोति भूः स्वाहेति ।
15.11.9.a.m: Then, having touched water and silently put on a thorny kindling-stick, he offers the agnihotra with the upayamana from this very remainder with: 'Bhūḥ svāhā!'

15.11.10.a.m: Having brought together the remainder on the upayamana, they all partake of it.

15.11.11.a.m: He addresses each with their liturgical title: 'So-and-so, do thou invite!'

15.11.12.a.m: The hotṛ, the adhvaryu, the brahman, the pratiprasthātṛ, the agnīdh, and the sacrificer.

15.11.14.a.m: Or rather, only the sacrificer [partakes] visibly,

15.11.15.a.s: hutaṃ havirmadhu haviriti bhakṣayitvopayamanaṃ pratiprasthātre prayacchati
15.11.15.a.d: हुतं हविर्मधु हविरिति भक्षयित्वोपयमनं प्रतिप्रस्थात्रे प्रयच्छति
15.11.15.a.m: Having partaken with: 'The oblation is offered, the oblation is honey,' he hands over the upayamana to the pratiprasthātṛ.

15.11.16.a.s: taducchiṣṭakhare prakṣālyāntarvedyupayamanaṃ nidhāya tasminrukmāvavadhāya madnatīrānīyāpohiṣṭhīyābhirmārjayitvā ninīyāpo 'traiva sarvaṃ parigharmyaṃ samavadhāya
15.11.16.a.d: तदुच्छिष्टखरे प्रक्षाल्यान्तर्वेद्युपयमनं निधाय तस्मिन्रुक्माववधाय मद्नतीरानीयापोहिष्ठीयाभिर्मार्जयित्वा निनीयापो ऽत्रैव सर्वं परिघर्म्यं समवधाय
15.11.16.a.m: Having washed it on the mound for remnants, placed the upayamana inside the altar ground, put the two gold plates upon it, poured boiling water over it, wiped [the utensils] with the Apo-hiṣṭhā verses, poured out the water, and put together all the accessories of the pravargya right there,

15.12.1.a.m: he issues the ritual call: 'Recite for the gharma being set down!'

15.12.1.b.m: or: 'Recite for the one being set down!'

15.12.2.a.s: ā yasminsapta vāsavā ityabhijñāyāgreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya samrāḍāsandyāṃ sādayati svāhā tvā sūryasya raśmibhya iti prātaḥ /
15.12.2.a.d: आ यस्मिन्सप्त वासवा इत्यभिज्ञायाग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य सम्राडासन्द्यां सादयति स्वाहा त्वा सूर्यस्य रश्मिभ्य इति प्रातः ।
15.12.2.a.m: Having recognized [the beginning of the verse]: 'In whom the seven Vasus...', he carries it around to the east of the āhavanīya and sets it down on the sovereign's throne with: 'Svāhā to thee, to the rays of the sun!' in the morning,

15.12.2.b.m: with: 'Svāhā to thee, to the constellations!' in the evening.

15.12.3.a.s: yatrābhijānātyaddhi tṛṇamaghnye viśvadānīmiti tadgāmavasṛjya madantīrupaspṛśyottamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kurvanti
15.12.3.a.d: यत्राभिजानात्यद्धि तृणमघ्न्ये विश्वदानीमिति तद्गामवसृज्य मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्योत्तमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कुर्वन्ति
15.12.3.a.m: When he recognizes [the words]: 'Eat the grass, O unslayable cow, at all times,' having let the cow loose at that point and touched boiling water, they perform the expiation with the last anuvāka.

15.12.4.a.m: Thus they perform the Pravargya and the Upasad in the evening and in the morning.

15.12.5.a.m: At a rite with three Upasads, six times;

15.12.5.b.m: at one with six Upasads, twelve times;

15.12.5.c.m: at one with twelve Upasads, twenty-four times.

15.12.7.a.m: In the evening he offers the rauhiṇa [cake] with the subsequent mantra.

15.12.7.b.m: 'Thou hast brought me across the day; protect me from the night.

15.12.7.c.m: This is thy kindling-stick, O Agni; blaze up therewith.

15.12.7.d.s: āyurme dā varcasā māñjīriti sāyaṃ samidhamādadhāti /
15.12.7.d.d: आयुर्मे दा वर्चसा माञ्जीरिति सायं समिधमादधाति ।
15.12.7.d.m: Grant me life; anoint me with splendour!'—with this he puts on a kindling-stick in the evening.

15.12.7.e.s: apīparo mā rātriyā ahno mā pāhīti prātaḥ
15.12.7.e.d: अपीपरो मा रात्रिया अह्नो मा पाहीति प्रातः
15.12.7.e.m: 'Thou hast brought me across the night; protect me from the day'—in the morning.

15.12.8.a.m: He offers the agnihotra in the evening with: 'Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā!'

15.12.8.b.m: In the morning with: 'Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā!'

15.12.12.a.m: He performs the Pravargya at a Viśvajit with all the Pṛṣṭhas.

15.12.13.a.m: Having performed the Pravargya with it, he should not eat meat for a year;

15.12.13.d.m: a Śūdra should not drink his leftover.

15.12.13.e.m: 'It is fiery splendour indeed that he thereby whets'—so it is known.

15.13.1.a.m: About to conclude the Pravargya, he gives a she-goat to the agnīdh,

15.13.2.a.s: aparaṃ kharaṃ pūrvasminkhare nyupyocchiṣṭakharaṃ saṃkṛṣyottareṇāhavanīyaṃ samrāḍāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tasyāṃ sarvaṃ parigharmyaṃ samavadhāyaudumbaryāṃ sruci caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā gharma yā te divi śugityetairyathāliṅgaṃ juhoti
15.13.2.a.d: अपरं खरं पूर्वस्मिन्खरे न्युप्योच्छिष्टखरं संकृष्योत्तरेणाहवनीयं सम्राडासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य तस्यां सर्वं परिघर्म्यं समवधायौदुम्बर्यां स्रुचि चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा घर्म या ते दिवि शुगित्येतैर्यथालिङ्गं जुहोति
15.13.2.a.m: Having poured the western mound onto the eastern mound, scraped up the mound for remnants, set up the sovereign's throne to the north of the āhavanīya, placed all the accessories of the pravargya upon it, and taken four ladlings of clarified butter in the spoon of udumbara wood, he offers them according to their characteristics with: 'O Gharma, whatever heat of thine is in heaven...'

15.13.3.a.s: api vā pratiprasthātā trīnsaṃnakhāñchalākāmuṣṭīnādāya teṣāmekamāhavanīye pradīpyāsyadaghne dhārayati /
15.13.3.a.d: अपि वा प्रतिप्रस्थाता त्रीन्संनखाञ्छलाकामुष्टीनादाय तेषामेकमाहवनीये प्रदीप्यास्यदघ्ने धारयति ।
15.13.3.a.m: Or rather, the pratiprasthātṛ, having taken three fistfuls of splints trimmed even to the nails and ignited one of them in the āhavanīya, holds it at mouth-level.

15.13.3.b.s: tamadhvaryurabhijuhoti gharma yā te divi śugiti /
15.13.3.b.d: तमध्वर्युरभिजुहोति घर्म या ते दिवि शुगिति ।
15.13.3.b.m: Over it the adhvaryu makes an offering with: 'O Gharma, whatever heat of thine is in heaven...'

15.13.3.c.s: tasminnaparaṃ pradīpyāhavanīye pūrvaṃ prahṛtya nābhidaghne dhārayati /
15.13.3.c.d: तस्मिन्नपरं प्रदीप्याहवनीये पूर्वं प्रहृत्य नाभिदघ्ने धारयति ।
15.13.3.c.m: Having ignited another upon it and cast the first into the āhavanīya, he holds it at navel-level.

15.13.3.d.d: तमध्वर्युरभिजुहोति घर्म या ते ऽन्तरिक्षे शुगिति ।
15.13.3.d.m: Over it the adhvaryu makes an offering with: 'O Gharma, whatever heat of thine is in the intermediate space...'

15.13.3.e.s: tasminnaparaṃ pradīpyāhavanīye pūrvaṃ prahṛtya jānudaghne dhārayati /
15.13.3.e.d: तस्मिन्नपरं प्रदीप्याहवनीये पूर्वं प्रहृत्य जानुदघ्ने धारयति ।
15.13.3.e.m: Having ignited another upon it and cast the first into the āhavanīya, he holds it at knee-level.

15.13.3.f.s: tamadhvaryurabhijuhoti gharma yā te pṛthivyāṃ śugiti
15.13.3.f.d: तमध्वर्युरभिजुहोति घर्म या ते पृथिव्यां शुगिति
15.13.3.f.m: Over it the adhvaryu makes an offering with: 'O Gharma, whatever heat of thine is on earth...'

15.13.4.a.m: He throws it along into the āhavanīya itself.

15.13.5.a.d: अनु नो ऽद्यानुमतिरिति परिश्रिते प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्नीमुदानयति
15.13.5.a.m: With: 'May Anumati [approve] us today,' the pratiprasthātṛ leads the wife out into the enclosed space.

15.13.6.a.m: They step out after with: 'Followed by Anumati...'

15.13.7.a.m: They carry after [them]: the post, the shovel, the pegs, the branching pegs, the cords, and the two mounds.

15.13.8.a.m: He carries the mound for remnants around to the south.

15.13.9.a.s: samrāḍāsandyā dvāvantarvedi pādau dvau bahirvedi pratiṣṭhāpya saṃpreṣyati prastotaḥ sāma gāyeti
15.13.9.a.d: सम्राडासन्द्या द्वावन्तर्वेदि पादौ द्वौ बहिर्वेदि प्रतिष्ठाप्य संप्रेष्यति प्रस्तोतः साम गायेति
15.13.9.a.m: Having set up two feet of the sovereign's throne inside the altar ground and two outside the altar ground, he issues the ritual call: 'O prastotṛ, sing the saman!'

15.13.10.a.m: All, together with the wife [of the sacrificer], join in the finale of the sāman three times.

15.13.10.c.m: Having arrived to the west of the high altar, a third time.

15.14.1.a.m: With "From the sky, as far-protector..." they step forward at the first [call];

15.14.1.b.m: with "From the sacred word, as far-protector..." at the second;

15.14.1.c.m: with "From the breath, as far-protector..." at the third.

15.14.2.a.s: uttareṇottaravediṃ samrāḍāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya saṃpreṣyati prastotarvārṣāharaṃ sāma gāyeṣṭāhotrīyaṃ sāma gāyeti /
15.14.2.a.d: उत्तरेणोत्तरवेदिं सम्राडासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य संप्रेष्यति प्रस्तोतर्वार्षाहरं साम गायेष्टाहोत्रीयं साम गायेति ।
15.14.2.a.m: Having set down the emperor-stool north of the high altar, he gives the call: "Prastotṛ, sing the Vārṣāhara sāman; sing the Iṣṭāhotrīya sāman!"

15.14.2.b.m: They join in the finale of the Iṣṭāhotrīya sāman;

15.14.3.a.m: If he sprinkles water afterwards, then he should enjoin the Vārṣāhara.

15.14.4.a.s: udakumbhamādāyādhvaryurvalgurasi śaṃyudhāyā iti triḥ pradakṣiṇamuttaravediṃ pariṣiñcanparyeti /
15.14.4.a.d: उदकुम्भमादायाध्वर्युर्वल्गुरसि शंयुधाया इति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमुत्तरवेदिं परिषिञ्चन्पर्येति ।
15.14.4.a.m: Taking a water jar, the adhvaryu circumambulates the high altar sunwise three times, sprinkling [water] with "Pleasing art thou, for well-being..."

15.14.4.b.s: nidhāya kumbhaṃ śaṃ ca vakṣi pari ca vakṣīti trirapariṣiñcanpratiparyeti
15.14.4.b.d: निधाय कुम्भं शं च वक्षि परि च वक्षीति त्रिरपरिषिञ्चन्प्रतिपर्येति
15.14.4.b.m: Having set down the jar, he circumambulates [it] counter-sunwise three times without sprinkling, with "Mayest thou bring well-being, mayest thou carry [it] all around..."

15.14.5.a.m: Having touched the high altar with "Four-cornered is the navel of the cosmic order...", he scatters and spreads two mounds north of the high navel with "A seat of all life..."

15.14.6.a.s: apa dveṣo apa hṛra iti mārjālīyadeś ucchiṣṭakharam
15.14.6.a.d: अप द्वेषो अप हृर इति मार्जालीयदेश् उच्छिष्टखरम्
15.14.6.a.m: With "Away hatred, away crookedness!" [he scatters] the mound for the remnants in the place of the mārjālīya.

15.14.7.a.s: uttareṇottaranābhiṃ khare hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya tasmin pracaraṇīyaṃ mahāvīramupāvaharati
15.14.7.a.d: उत्तरेणोत्तरनाभिं खरे हिरण्यं निधाय तस्मिन् प्रचरणीयं महावीरमुपावहरति
15.14.7.a.m: Having placed gold upon the mound north of the high navel, he brings down upon it the Mahāvīra used in the rite.

15.14.8.a.m: Right here [he places] the other two, east and west, or south and north.

15.14.9.a.s: atraiva sarvaṃ parigharmyaṃ sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalamādityasya rūpaṃ karoti
15.14.9.a.d: अत्रैव सर्वं परिघर्म्यं सर्वतः परिमण्डलमादित्यस्य रूपं करोति
15.14.9.a.m: Right here he forms everything belonging to the cauldron circular on all sides, as the form of the sun.

15.14.10.a.d: महीनां पयो ऽसीति महावीरे गोपय आनयति ।
15.14.10.a.m: With "Thou art the milk of the great ones," he pours cow's milk into the Mahāvīra;

15.14.10.b.s: jyotirbhā asi vanaspatīnāmoṣadhīnāṃ rasa iti madhu /
15.14.10.b.d: ज्योतिर्भा असि वनस्पतीनामोषधीनां रस इति मधु ।
15.14.10.b.m: with "Thou art the light, thou art the sap of trees and plants," honey;

15.14.10.c.d: वाजिनं त्वा वाजिनो ऽवनयाम इति दधि
15.14.10.c.m: with "Speedy one, we pour thee down, who art vigorous," curds.

15.14.11.a.m: In this way he fills the second and the third [vessels].

15.14.12.a.m: Or he should pour clarified butter into the first;

15.14.13.a.s: gharmaitatte 'nnametatpurīṣamiti dadhnā madhumiśreṇa pātrāṇi pūrayati yānyāsecanavanti /
15.14.13.a.d: घर्मैतत्ते ऽन्नमेतत्पुरीषमिति दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण पात्राणि पूरयति यान्यासेचनवन्ति ।
15.14.13.a.m: With "O cauldron, this is thy food, this thy rubble," he fills with curds mixed with honey whichever vessels are meant to receive poured liquid;

15.14.13.c.m: "For non-emptiness," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

15.15.1.a.m: Now if he should intend to make [it] in the shape of a man, the procedure is the same up to bringing down the first [Mahāvīra].

15.15.1.b.m: Having brought down the other two right here, he forms the shape of the head.

15.15.1.c.m: He places a veda with unbroken ends on top, as the form of the topknot;

15.15.1.d.m: on both sides, the two milking-pails as the form of the ears;

15.15.1.e.m: on both sides, two gold pieces, or the two butter spoons, as the form of the eyes;

15.15.1.f.m: on both sides, the two sruva spoons as the form of the nostrils;

15.15.1.g.m: the vessel for sprinkling water as the form of the mouth;

15.15.1.h.m: the pot for clarified butter as the form of the neck;

15.15.1.i.m: on both sides, the two tongs as the form of the collarbones;

15.15.1.j.m: on both sides, the two pincers as the form of the shoulders;

15.15.1.k.m: on both sides, the two Rauhiṇa offering ladles as the form of the arms;

15.15.1.l.m: pointing east, the peg as the form of the spine;

15.15.1.m.m: on both sides, the two fanning-fans as the form of the ribs;

15.15.1.n.m: in the middle, the third [fan] as the form of the chest;

15.15.1.o.m: in the middle, the support shovel as the form of the belly;

15.15.1.p.m: into it he places all the cord material, as the form of the entrails;

15.15.1.q.m: pointing north, the wooden shovel as the form of the hips;

15.15.1.r.m: on both sides, the two pegs as the form of the thighs;

15.15.1.s.m: in the middle, a third [peg] as the form of the penis;

15.15.1.t.m: on both sides, the two potsherds for the Rauhiṇa cakes as the form of the heels;

15.15.1.u.m: with the remainder of the Rauhiṇa flour he scatters [it], as the form of the marrow;

15.15.1.v.m: having untied the veda, he strews it along, as the form of the sinews;

15.15.1.w.m: he covers [it] with avakā plants and scented grass, as the form of the flesh;

15.15.1.x.m: he sprinkles [it] with curds mixed with honey, as the form of the blood;

15.15.1.y.m: he covers [it] with a black antelope skin with the hair turned upward, as the form of the skin and hair;

15.15.1.z.m: having dismantled the emperor-stool, he places it on top, as the form of sovereignty.

15.16.1.a.m: He should dispose of [the Pravargya equipment] on the high altar for one who desires splendor;

15.16.1.b.m: on the high altar for one who desires proper nourishment.

15.16.2.a.m: Or he should dispose of it in front, or behind;

15.16.3.a.m: If he disposes of it on an island in a river, he should not sprinkle [water] all around.

15.16.4.a.s: yaṃ dviṣyādyatra sa syāttasyāṃ diśyaudumbaryāṃ śākhāyāmudvāsayet /
15.16.4.a.d: यं द्विष्याद्यत्र स स्यात्तस्यां दिश्यौदुम्बर्यां शाखायामुद्वासयेत् ।
15.16.4.a.m: Whomever he hates, in whichever direction he may be, in that direction he should set it out upon an udumbara branch.

15.16.4.b.m: The udumbara is indeed sap, food is breath, [and] the gharma is pain.

15.16.4.c.m: With the formula, 'Here do I close up the breath of so-and-so, descendant of so-and-so, with pain,' he closes up his breath with pain.

15.16.4.d.m: 'Instantly he meets with ruin,' so it is taught.

15.16.5.a.m: Where darbha grass is swarming with termites, there he should set it out for one desiring rain.

15.16.6.a.m: They declare the constant rule [to be] on the uttaravedī.

15.16.7.a.m: Birds should not alight around it once it is set out until the carrying forward of the fire.

15.16.8.a.m: Here some prescribe pouring water around [it].

15.16.9.a.m: Then they revere it with, 'Ranti by name are you, the heavenly Gandharva...'

15.16.10.a.s: etattvaṃ deva gharma devo devānupāgā ityabhimantryedamahaṃ namuṣyo manuṣyāniti pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya sumitrā na āpa oṣadhaya iti mārjālīyadeśa ucchiṣṭakhare mārjayitvodvayaṃ tamasasparītyādityamupasthāyodu tyaṃ citramiti dvābhyāṃ gārhapatye juhoti /
15.16.10.a.d: एतत्त्वं देव घर्म देवो देवानुपागा इत्यभिमन्त्र्येदमहं नमुष्यो मनुष्यानिति प्रदक्षिणमावृत्य सुमित्रा न आप ओषधय इति मार्जालीयदेश उच्छिष्टखरे मार्जयित्वोद्वयं तमसस्परीत्यादित्यमुपस्थायोदु त्यं चित्रमिति द्वाभ्यां गार्हपत्ये जुहोति ।
15.16.10.a.m: Having addressed it with, 'Thus, O divine gharma, a god, have you approached the gods,' [and then saying,] 'Here do I, a man, [approach] men,' having turned clockwise, having cleansed themselves with 'Friendly to us be waters and plants' in the place of the mārjālīya on the refuse-mound, having revered the sun with 'Looking upon the higher light beyond darkness,' he offers into the gārhapatya with the two [verses], 'Up that All-knower...' and 'The brilliant front of the gods...'

15.16.10.c.m: He offers into the āhavanīya with, 'This very [drink] for us...'

15.17.1.a.m: If the gharma spills, he should address it with the two [verses], 'The earth has leaped...'

15.17.2.a.s: yadi ghrameṇa caratsu vidyudāpatedyā purastādvidyudāpatadityetairyathāliṅgaṃ juhuyāt
15.17.2.a.d: यदि घ्रमेण चरत्सु विद्युदापतेद्या पुरस्ताद्विद्युदापतदित्येतैर्यथालिङ्गं जुहुयात्
15.17.2.a.m: If lightning strikes while they are proceeding with the gharma, he should make an offering with these verses according to their characteristic marks: 'The lightning which struck from the east...'

15.17.3.a.m: If from all sides, he should offer all [of them].

15.17.4.a.m: The two sections, 'To Prāṇa svāhā, to Pūṣan svāhā,' are the expiations for the gharma.

15.17.5.a.m: He places the gharma-brick with the section, 'Its light did not perish from its heat...'

15.17.5.b.s: kulāyinīṃ yāste agna ārdrā yonaya ityanuvākena /
15.17.5.b.d: कुलायिनीं यास्ते अग्न आर्द्रा योनय इत्यनुवाकेन ।
15.17.5.b.m: [He places] the nest-like [brick] with the section, 'Those moist wombs of yours, O Agni...'

15.17.5.c.m: The adhvaryu touches the fire with the iḍā-piling with the section, 'You are Agni, you are Vaiśvānara...'

15.17.6.a.m: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar' are the universal expiations.

15.17.7.a.s: yadi mahāvīraḥ padyetordhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaya iti dvābhyāmenamucchrayīta
15.17.7.a.d: यदि महावीरः पद्येतोर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतय इति द्वाभ्यामेनमुच्छ्रयीत
15.17.7.a.m: If the mahāvīra falls over, he should set it upright with the two verses, 'Upright for our aid...'

15.17.8.a.m: If it breaks, he should join it together with 'The solitary runner...'

15.17.8.b.s: tato yāni dṛḍhārthe saṃśleṣaṇāni syustairenamabhidihyādyadanyanmāṃsānmāṣebhyaśca yadṛte cidabhiśriṣa iti
15.17.8.b.d: ततो यानि दृढार्थे संश्लेषणानि स्युस्तैरेनमभिदिह्याद्यदन्यन्मांसान्माषेभ्यश्च यदृते चिदभिश्रिष इति
15.17.8.b.m: Then, whatever binding substances there may be for making it firm, with those he should smear it over, other than meat and māṣa beans, with 'Even without bindings...'

15.17.9.a.s: yadi ghramamatiparīyurna vā pratiparīyuḥ punarūrjā saha rayyetyetābhyāmenaṃ pratiparīyuḥ
15.17.9.a.d: यदि घ्रममतिपरीयुर्न वा प्रतिपरीयुः पुनरूर्जा सह रय्येत्येताभ्यामेनं प्रतिपरीयुः
15.17.9.a.m: If they bypass the gharma or do not walk around it in return, they should walk back around it with these two verses, 'Again with sap, together with wealth...'

15.17.10.a.s: mā no gharma vyathita ityaṣṭau gharme vyathite prāyaścittāni
15.17.10.a.d: मा नो घर्म व्यथित इत्यष्टौ घर्मे व्यथिते प्रायश्चित्तानि
15.17.10.a.m: The eight [formulas], 'May the gharma not be troubled for us,' are the expiations when the gharma is troubled.

15.17.11.a.m: Or he should address the troubled gharma itself with four of these [verses].

15.17.12.a.s: yadi gharmeṇa caratsvādityo 'stamiyādaparasyāṃ dvāri darbheṇa hiraṇyaṃ prabadhyodvayaṃ tamasasparītyupasthāyodu tyaṃ citramiti dvābhyāṃ gārhapatye hutvā pravṛjya śvobhūte vayaḥ suparṇā ityādityamupatiṣṭhante
15.17.12.a.d: यदि घर्मेण चरत्स्वादित्यो ऽस्तमियादपरस्यां द्वारि दर्भेण हिरण्यं प्रबध्योद्वयं तमसस्परीत्युपस्थायोदु त्यं चित्रमिति द्वाभ्यां गार्हपत्ये हुत्वा प्रवृज्य श्वोभूते वयः सुपर्णा इत्यादित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ते
15.17.12.a.m: If the sun sets while they are proceeding with the gharma, having tied gold at the western door with a blade of darbha grass, having revered [the sun] with 'Looking upon the higher light beyond darkness,' having offered into the gārhapatya with the two verses, 'Up that All-knower...' and 'The brilliant front of the gods...', having performed the heating, on the next day they revere the sun with 'The fair-winged birds...'

15.18.1.a.s: yadi gharmadhugdohakāle nāgacchedanyāṃ dugdhvā pravṛjya tāṃ sutyāyāṃ brāhmaṇāya dadyādyamanabhyāgamiṣyansyāt
15.18.1.a.d: यदि घर्मधुग्दोहकाले नागच्छेदन्यां दुग्ध्वा प्रवृज्य तां सुत्यायां ब्राह्मणाय दद्याद्यमनभ्यागमिष्यन्स्यात्
15.18.1.a.m: If the gharma-milch-cow does not come at the time of milking, having milked another and having performed the heating, he should give her on the soma-pressing day to a brahmin whom he will not visit again.

15.18.2.a.s: yadi gharmadhugi payo na syāddṛteścaturthaṃ pādaṃ stanaṃ kṛtvā pinvayet
15.18.2.a.d: यदि घर्मधुगि पयो न स्याद्दृतेश्चतुर्थं पादं स्तनं कृत्वा पिन्वयेत्
15.18.2.a.m: If there is no milk in the gharma-milch-cow, having made the fourth foot of a leather bag into a teat, he should make it flow.

15.18.3.a.m: If she yields curds, he should recite [a verse] to Bṛhaspati.

15.18.4.a.m: If milk, [a verse] to the Aśvins with a conclusion.

15.18.5.a.s: yadyu vai lohitaṃ duhīta raudryarcā juhuyāt
15.18.5.a.d: यद्यु वै लोहितं दुहीत रौद्र्यर्चा जुहुयात्
15.18.5.a.m: And if she yields blood, he should offer with a verse to Rudra.

15.18.6.a.m: If she is lost, he should offer with two verses to Dhātṛ.

15.18.7.a.m: If her calf [is lost], he should offer with a verse to Vāyu with team.

15.18.8.a.m: If she sits down upon something unholy or unfit for sacrifice, he should offer with a verse to Agni.

15.18.9.a.m: If a bird flies against her, he should offer with a verse to the Aśvins.

15.18.10.a.s: yadyudvā patetsaṃ vā vijeta śārdūlo vā hanyādarkakṣīramajākṣīra āścotya tena precaret
15.18.10.a.d: यद्युद्वा पतेत्सं वा विजेत शार्दूलो वा हन्यादर्कक्षीरमजाक्षीर आश्चोत्य तेन प्रेचरेत्
15.18.10.a.m: If she bolts, or trembles, or a tiger strikes her down, having dripped calotropis milk into goat's milk, he should proceed with that.

15.18.11.a.m: Some prescribe the heating [of the gharma] on the soma-pressing day.

15.18.13.a.m: When it becomes reddish in the east, then it is to be heated;

15.18.13.b.s: upakāśa upavyuṣaṃ samayāviṣita uditānudita udite vā /
15.18.13.b.d: उपकाश उपव्युषं समयाविषित उदितानुदित उदिते वा ।
15.18.13.b.m: at dawn, at daybreak, when the sun is half-risen, when it has risen or not risen;

15.18.13.c.s: prātaḥ saṃgave mādhyaṃdine vā pavamāne stute
15.18.13.c.d: प्रातः संगवे माध्यंदिने वा पवमाने स्तुते
15.18.13.c.m: in the morning at grazing time, or at midday when the pavamāna chant has been sung.

15.18.14.a.m: It is to be heated in the house of the agnīdh.

15.18.15.a.m: 'It is to be heated only once,' so it is taught.

15.18.16.a.m: These options are to be alternated with the heatings belonging to the upasads.

15.18.17.a.m: They partake of the curd-gharma with the section, 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar.'

15.19.1.a.d: व्याख्याता घोरास्तन्वो ऽरण्येऽनुवाक्यो गण उत्तरौ चानुवाकौ
15.19.1.a.m: The terrifying bodies, the group to be recited in the forest, and the two subsequent sections have been explained.

15.19.2.a.s: yadi gharmeṇa caratsvekasṛka uttiṣṭhedvi gā indra vicaranspāśayasvetyetamabhimantryobhayata ādīpyolmukamasmai pratyasyedagne agninā saṃvadasveti
15.19.2.a.d: यदि घर्मेण चरत्स्वेकसृक उत्तिष्ठेद्वि गा इन्द्र विचरन्स्पाशयस्वेत्येतमभिमन्त्र्योभयत आदीप्योल्मुकमस्मै प्रत्यस्येदग्ने अग्निना संवदस्वेति
15.19.2.a.m: If a jackal rises while they are proceeding with the gharma, having addressed it with 'O Indra, roaming about, discover the cows,' having ignited a firebrand at both ends, he should throw it towards it with, 'O Agni, speak with Agni.'

15.19.3.a.m: Then they revere it with the remainder of the section, 'Once, O Agni, homage to you...'

15.19.4.a.s: atha yadi gṛdhraḥ salāvṛkī bhayeḍako dīrghamukhyulūko bhūtopasṛṣṭaḥ śakunirvā vadedasṛṅmukhaḥ /
15.19.4.a.d: अथ यदि गृध्रः सलावृकी भयेडको दीर्घमुख्युलूको भूतोपसृष्टः शकुनिर्वा वदेदसृङ्मुखः ।
15.19.4.a.m: Now if a vulture, a she-jackal, an omen-ram, a long-snouted animal, an owl, an animal possessed by an evil spirit, or a bird with a bloody mouth should cry out,

15.19.4.g.m: [and] 'Spreading both thighs...', having addressed it with these according to the characteristic marks, the throwing of the firebrand and the subsequent rites are the same.

15.19.5.a.s: yadi gharmadhukkrimiṇā syādatriṇā tvā krime hanmītyanuvākenāsyāḥ krimīnhanyāt
15.19.5.a.d: यदि घर्मधुक्क्रिमिणा स्यादत्रिणा त्वा क्रिमे हन्मीत्यनुवाकेनास्याः क्रिमीन्हन्यात्
15.19.5.a.m: If the gharma-milch-cow has worms, he should kill her worms with the section, 'With Atri I slay you, O worm.'

15.19.6.a.m: Or this expiation may be performed on all occasions.

15.19.7.a.m: If he practices sorcery against someone, he should make a portion out of his blood and offer it with the section: 'Bring out [the portion] cut off from the cooked [offering]...'

15.19.8.a.s: yamabhivyāhariṣyansyāttrirātrāvaraṃ brahmacaryaṃ caritvā gatvainamabhivyāharedbrahmaṇā tvā śapāmītyanuvākena
15.19.8.a.d: यमभिव्याहरिष्यन्स्यात्त्रिरात्रावरं ब्रह्मचर्यं चरित्वा गत्वैनमभिव्याहरेद्ब्रह्मणा त्वा शपामीत्यनुवाकेन
15.19.8.a.m: If he intends to curse someone, he should observe celibacy for at least three nights, go up to him, and curse him with the section: 'By the brahman I curse you...'

15.19.9.a.s: yaṃ dviṣyāttasy goṣṭhe svajamoṣadhīṃ nikhaneduttuda śimijāvarītyanuvākena
15.19.9.a.d: यं द्विष्यात्तस्य् गोष्ठे स्वजमोषधीं निखनेदुत्तुद शिमिजावरीत्यनुवाकेन
15.19.9.a.m: Against whom he feels hatred, he should bury a svajā-snake [or plant] in his cattle-pen with the section: 'Stir up, O Śimijāvarī...'

15.19.10.a.s: api vā goṣṭhasyaiva dakṣiṇāṃ dvārbāhumetenaiva vicālayet
15.19.10.a.d: अपि वा गोष्ठस्यैव दक्षिणां द्वार्बाहुमेतेनैव विचालयेत्
15.19.10.a.m: Or he may simply displace the right doorpost of his cattle-pen with this very [section].

15.19.11.a.s: yadyudgātā puruṣasāma na gāyedadhvaryurevaitena sāmnodgāyedbhurbhuvaḥ suvarityanuvākena
15.19.11.a.d: यद्युद्गाता पुरुषसाम न गायेदध्वर्युरेवैतेन साम्नोद्गायेद्भुर्भुवः सुवरित्यनुवाकेन
15.19.11.a.m: If the udgātṛ does not sing the Puruṣasāman, the adhvaryu himself should sing with that sāman by means of the section: 'Bhūḥ bhuvaḥ suvaḥ...'

15.20.1.a.m: Now we shall explain the intermediate initiation (avāntaradīkṣā).

15.20.2.a.s: parvaṇyudagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣasya vā puṇye nakṣatre keśaśmaśru vāpayitvāparāhṇe prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya khile 'cchadirdarśe 'gnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya pūrvavadupākṛtya madantīrupaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvā catasra audumbarīḥ samidho ghṛtānvaktā abhyādadhāti pṛthivī samidityetairmantraiḥ
15.20.2.a.d: पर्वण्युदगयन आपूर्यमाणपक्षस्य वा पुण्ये नक्षत्रे केशश्मश्रु वापयित्वापराह्णे प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्य खिले ऽच्छदिर्दर्शे ऽग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य पूर्ववदुपाकृत्य मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वा चतस्र औदुम्बरीः समिधो घृतान्वक्ता अभ्यादधाति पृथिवी समिदित्येतैर्मन्त्रैः
15.20.2.a.m: On a junction-day during the northern course of the sun, or during the waxing fortnight under an auspicious lunar mansion, having had his hair and beard shaved, having gone out in the afternoon toward the east or north, having set up the fire in an uncultivated plot where roofs are out of sight, having strewn around it, having brought [the ritual] into commencement as before, having touched hot water, and having performed the pacification rite with the first section, he puts on four firesticks of udumbara wood smeared with ghee with the mantras: 'Earth is the firestick...'

15.20.3.a.s: atha devatā upatiṣṭhate 'gne vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmīti
15.20.3.a.d: अथ देवता उपतिष्ठते ऽग्ने व्रतपते व्रतं चरिष्यामीति
15.20.3.a.m: Then he attends upon the deities with: 'O Agni, lord of vows, I will observe the vow...'

15.20.4.a.m: Then he makes him recite the beginnings of all the sections;

15.20.5.a.s: uttamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvā tataḥ saṃmīlayati vācaṃ ca yacchati
15.20.5.a.d: उत्तमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वा ततः संमीलयति वाचं च यच्छति
15.20.5.a.m: Having performed the pacification rite with the last section, he closes his eyes and restrains his speech.

15.20.6.a.s: athāsyāhatena vāsasā pradakṣiṇaṃ saṃmukhaṃ śiro veṣṭayitvāstamite grāmaṃ prapādayati
15.20.6.a.d: अथास्याहतेन वाससा प्रदक्षिणं संमुखं शिरो वेष्टयित्वास्तमिते ग्रामं प्रपादयति
15.20.6.a.m: Then, having wrapped his head around from left to right in front with an unwashed cloth, he brings him into the village after sunset.

15.20.7.a.m: With restrained speech, he stands or sits through this night.

15.20.8.a.d: श्वोभूते खिले ऽच्छदिर्दर्शे ऽग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्याथास्य षट्तयमभिविदर्शयति ।
15.20.8.a.m: On the next day, having set up the fire in an uncultivated plot where roofs are out of sight and having strewn around it, he causes him to look upon a group of six objects;

15.20.8.c.m: fire, the sun, a water-pot, a stone, a calf, and a naked woman;

15.20.9.a.m: Or, having shown the first three, [he shows] the others as they happen to be available.

15.20.10.a.s: atraitadvāso gurave dattvā vayaḥ suparṇā ityādityamupatiṣṭhate
15.20.10.a.d: अत्रैतद्वासो गुरवे दत्त्वा वयः सुपर्णा इत्यादित्यमुपतिष्ठते
15.20.10.a.m: At this point, having given this garment to his teacher, he attends upon the sun with: 'The winged birds...'

15.20.11.a.m: Now, with respect to his celibacy, [these rules are] permanent:

15.20.14.a.m: If he does eat, [it should be] while a fire is blazing.

15.20.15.a.m: He should not drink directly from an earthen vessel.

15.20.16.a.m: He should not converse with a woman or with a śūdra.

15.20.20.a.m: He should fast on eighth days and junction-days, with restrained speech.

15.21.1.a.m: He should observe this vow for a year;

15.21.1.b.m: he should study only during this year.

15.21.2.a.m: If he does not study within this year, he should observe this vow as long as the study lasts.

15.21.3.a.s: saṃvatsare paryavete khile 'cchadirdarśe 'gnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya pūrvavadvisṛjya madantīrupaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvāvṛttairmantraiḥ samidha ādhāyāvṛttairdevatā upasthāyottamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvā gurave varaṃ dattvā keśaśmaśru vāpayate
15.21.3.a.d: संवत्सरे पर्यवेते खिले ऽच्छदिर्दर्शे ऽग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य पूर्ववद्विसृज्य मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वावृत्तैर्मन्त्रैः समिध आधायावृत्तैर्देवता उपस्थायोत्तमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वा गुरवे वरं दत्त्वा केशश्मश्रु वापयते
15.21.3.a.m: When the year has elapsed, having set up the fire in an uncultivated plot where roofs are out of sight, having strewn around it, having released [the vow] as before, having touched hot water, having performed the pacification rite with the first section, having placed the firesticks with the mantras repeated, having attended upon the deities with [the mantras] repeated, having performed the pacification rite with the last section, and having given a choice gift to the teacher, he has his hair and beard shaved.

15.21.4.a.m: Now, with respect to his private recitation (svādhyāya), [these rules are] permanent:

15.21.5.a.m: He should not study if the study period has not been opened.

15.21.7.a.s: nātidoṣamabrahmacaryamāpadya na māṃsaṃ khāditvā na keśaśmaśrulomanakhāni vāpayitvā na keśānprasādhya na dataḥ prāksālya
15.21.7.a.d: नातिदोषमब्रह्मचर्यमापद्य न मांसं खादित्वा न केशश्मश्रुलोमनखानि वापयित्वा न केशान्प्रसाध्य न दतः प्राक्साल्य
15.21.7.a.m: not having transgressed celibacy too late [into the morning], not after eating meat, not after having hair, beard, body-hair, or nails shaved, not after combing his hair, not without having cleaned his teeth;

15.21.8.a.s: nākto nābhyakto nārdro nārdre nānavavṛṣṭe nābhre na chāyāyāṃ na paryāvṛtta āditye na haritayavānprekṣamāṇo na grāmyasya paśorante nāraṇyasya nāpāmante
15.21.8.a.d: नाक्तो नाभ्यक्तो नार्द्रो नार्द्रे नानववृष्टे नाभ्रे न छायायां न पर्यावृत्त आदित्ये न हरितयवान्प्रेक्षमाणो न ग्राम्यस्य पशोरन्ते नारण्यस्य नापामन्ते
15.21.8.a.m: not anointed, not smeared, not wet, not in wet clothes, not when it has not rained [during clear sky?], not under clouds, not in shade, not after the sun has turned, not looking at green barley, not near a domestic animal, not near a wild animal, not near water;

15.21.9.a.m: not after seeing something uncooked that has burst open, nor after seeing blood;

15.21.9.b.s: na harmyāṇi na śarīrāṇi na śavaṃ nāpapātram
15.21.9.b.d: न हर्म्याणि न शरीराणि न शवं नापपात्रम्
15.21.9.b.m: not [near] mansions, nor [unburied] bodies, nor a corpse, nor an outcaste.

15.21.10.a.s: adhyeṣyamāṇaḥ prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya khile 'cchadirdarśe 'gnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya madantīrupaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvāpareṇāgniṃ darbheṣvāsīno darbhāndūrvā vā dhārayamāṇaḥ parācīnamadhīyīta
15.21.10.a.d: अध्येष्यमाणः प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्य खिले ऽच्छदिर्दर्शे ऽग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वापरेणाग्निं दर्भेष्वासीनो दर्भान्दूर्वा वा धारयमाणः पराचीनमधीयीत
15.21.10.a.m: When about to study, having gone out toward the east or north, having set up the fire in an uncultivated plot where roofs are out of sight, having strewn around it, having touched hot water, having performed the pacification rite with the first section, seated to the west of the fire upon darbha grass, holding darbha grass or dūrvā grass, he should study the subsequent text.

15.21.12.a.m: When about to study, he should not utter other words.

15.21.13.a.m: Wherever he sees something unpacified, he should study only after performing the pacification rite again.

15.21.15.a.m: Having gone out for the Pravargya, he should not study anything else without having returned [to the village]; he should not study anything else.

16.1.1.a.d: अग्निं चेष्यमाणो ऽमावास्यायां पौर्णमास्यामेकाष्टकायां वोखां संभरति
16.1.1.a.m: Intending to pile the fire altar, he procures the materials for the boiler-pan (ukhā) on a new moon day, on a full moon day, or on the Ekāṣṭakā.

16.1.2.a.m: Some teach [this] with reference to the aṣāḍhā brick.

16.1.3.a.s: bṛhaspatipurohitā devā devānāṃ devā devāḥ prathamajā devā deveṣu parākramadhvaṃ prathamā dvitīyeṣu dvitīyāstṛtīyeṣu trirekādaśāstristrayastriṃśā anu va ārabha idaṃ śakeyaṃ yadidaṃ karomi te māvata te mā jinvatāsminbrahamannasminkṣatre 'syāmāśiṣyasyāṃ purodhāyāmasminkarmannasyāṃ devahūtyāmiti caturgṛhītaṃ juhoti
16.1.3.a.d: बृहस्पतिपुरोहिता देवा देवानां देवा देवाः प्रथमजा देवा देवेषु पराक्रमध्वं प्रथमा द्वितीयेषु द्वितीयास्तृतीयेषु त्रिरेकादशास्त्रिस्त्रयस्त्रिंशा अनु व आरभ इदं शकेयं यदिदं करोमि ते मावत ते मा जिन्वतास्मिन्ब्रहमन्नस्मिन्क्षत्रे ऽस्यामाशिष्यस्यां पुरोधायामस्मिन्कर्मन्नस्यां देवहूत्यामिति चतुर्गृहीतं जुहोति
16.1.3.a.m: With: 'The gods who have Bṛhaspati as their domestic priest, the gods of the gods, the first-born gods, make your effort among the gods, the first among the second, the second among the third, the thrice-eleven, the thrice-thirty-three; I take hold of you from behind; may I be able to do this which I do; protect me, invigorate me, in this sacred lore, in this royal power, in this wish, in this priestly office, in this work, in this invocation of the gods!'—he offers a fourfold ladleful.

16.1.4.a.s: juhūṃ sruvaṃ ca saṃmṛjya juhvāmaṣṭagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ mana iti yajuraṣṭamābhirṛgbhirekāmāhutiṃ juhotyantarvedyūrdhvastiṣṭhan
16.1.4.a.d: जुहूं स्रुवं च संमृज्य जुह्वामष्टगृहीतं गृहीत्वा युञ्जानः प्रथमं मन इति यजुरष्टमाभिरृग्भिरेकामाहुतिं जुहोत्यन्तर्वेद्यूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठन्
16.1.4.a.m: Having wiped the juhū and the sruva, having taken eight ladlefuls in the juhū, he offers a single oblation standing upright inside the altar ground with the eight verses [beginning with] the yajus: 'Yoking first the mind...'

16.1.5.a.m: One whom he desires should become worse off, for him he should offer each [verse] standing crooked.

16.1.6.a.m: If he desires: 'May I invest the meters with the sacrificial glory,' [the rule] has been stated.

16.1.7.a.s: ṛcā stomaṃ samardhayetyaparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti caturbhirabhrimādatte vaiṇavīṃ kalmāṣīṃ suṣirāmasuṣirāṃ vobhayataḥkṣṇūmanyatarataḥkṣṇūṃ vā prādeśamātrīmaratnimātrīṃ vyāyāmamātrīmaparimitāṃ vā /
16.1.7.a.d: ऋचा स्तोमं समर्धयेत्यपरं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति चतुर्भिरभ्रिमादत्ते वैणवीं कल्माषीं सुषिरामसुषिरां वोभयतःक्ष्णूमन्यतरतःक्ष्णूं वा प्रादेशमात्रीमरत्निमात्रीं व्यायाममात्रीमपरिमितां वा ।
16.1.7.a.m: Having taken another fourfold ladleful with: 'Swell the stoma with the ṛc...', he takes up the spade with the four [mantras beginning with]: 'At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ...'—[a spade] of bamboo, speckled, hollow or not hollow, sharpened at both ends or sharpened at one end, a span long, a cubit long, a fathom long, or of unlimited size;

16.1.7.b.s: khādirīṃ pālāśīmaudumbarīmarkamayīṃ kārṣmaryamayīṃ vaikaṅkatīṃ śamīmayīṃ vā yo vā yajñiyo vṛkṣaḥ phalagrahiḥ
16.1.7.b.d: खादिरीं पालाशीमौदुम्बरीमर्कमयीं कार्ष्मर्यमयीं वैकङ्कतीं शमीमयीं वा यो वा यज्ञियो वृक्षः फलग्रहिः
16.1.7.b.m: or made of khadira, of palāśa, of udumbara, of arka, of kārṣmarya, of vikankata, or of śamī, or whatever sacrificial tree bears fruit.

16.2.1.a.m: Taking the horse's halter with: 'They have grasped this halter of cosmic order...', he bridles the horse with: 'Run swiftly, O courser...'

16.2.2.a.s: tūṣṇīṃ gardabhasyādāya yuñjāthāṃ rāsabhaṃ yuvamiti gardabham
16.2.2.a.d: तूष्णीं गर्दभस्यादाय युञ्जाथां रासभं युवमिति गर्दभम्
16.2.2.a.m: Silently taking that of the donkey, [he bridles] the donkey with: 'Yoke the donkey, you two...'

16.2.3.a.s: yogeyoge tavastaramiti tisṛbhiraśvaprathamā abhipravrajanti yatra mṛdaṃ khaniṣyantaḥ syuḥ
16.2.3.a.d: योगेयोगे तवस्तरमिति तिसृभिरश्वप्रथमा अभिप्रव्रजन्ति यत्र मृदं खनिष्यन्तः स्युः
16.2.3.a.m: With the three [verses beginning with]: 'In every venture the most mighty...', they set out, with the horse first, to where they will dig the clay.

16.2.4.a.s: yadi kāmayeta pāpavasyasaṃ syāditi gardabhaprathamā gaccheyuḥ
16.2.4.a.d: यदि कामयेत पापवस्यसं स्यादिति गर्दभप्रथमा गच्छेयुः
16.2.4.a.m: If he should desire that things become worse instead of better, they should go with the donkey first.

16.2.5.a.m: He murmurs, 'Go to the earthly Agni as did the Aṅgirases.'

16.2.6.a.s: agniṃ purīṣyamaṅgirasvadacchema iti yena dveṣyeṇa saṃgacchate tamabhimantrayate /
16.2.6.a.d: अग्निं पुरीष्यमङ्गिरस्वदच्छेम इति येन द्वेष्येण संगच्छते तमभिमन्त्रयते ।
16.2.6.a.m: With 'We go to the earthly Agni as did the Aṅgirases,' he addresses any hateful person he encounters;

16.2.7.a.m: With 'We will bear the earthly Agni as did the Aṅgirases,' [he addresses] an anthill's crest.

16.2.7.b.m: Having dug it up, he attends upon it until the rising of the sun.

16.2.8.a.m: With 'Agni has looked after the front of the dawns,' he steps forth from the anthill's crest.

16.2.9.a.s: āgatya vājyadhvana ākramya vājinpṛthivīmiti dvābhyāṃ mṛtkhanamaśvamākramayya dyauste pṛṣṭhamityaśvasya pṛṣṭhaṃ saṃmārṣṭi
16.2.9.a.d: आगत्य वाज्यध्वन आक्रम्य वाजिन्पृथिवीमिति द्वाभ्यां मृत्खनमश्वमाक्रमय्य द्यौस्ते पृष्ठमित्यश्वस्य पृष्ठं संमार्ष्टि
16.2.9.a.m: Having made the horse step upon the clay-pit with the two [formulas], 'The courser having arrived from the road' and 'Stepping, O courser, upon the earth,' he strokes the back of the horse with 'The sky is your back.'

16.2.10.a.d: अभि तिष्ठ पृतन्यतो ऽधरे सन्तु शत्रवः ।
16.2.10.a.m: 'Tread upon those who fight [against us]; let the enemies be below!

16.2.10.b.s: indra iva vṛtrahā tiṣṭhāpaḥ kṣetrāṇi saṃjayan /
16.2.10.b.d: इन्द्र इव वृत्रहा तिष्ठापः क्षेत्राणि संजयन् ।
16.2.10.b.m: Stand like Indra the slayer of Vṛtra, conquering the waters and the fields!'

16.2.10.c.s: abhiṣṭhito 'sīti yaṃ dveṣṭi tamadhaspadamaśvasya manasā dhyāyati
16.2.10.c.d: अभिष्ठितो ऽसीति यं द्वेष्टि तमधस्पदमश्वस्य मनसा ध्यायति
16.2.10.c.m: With 'You are stepped upon,' he mentally focuses on whomever he hates under the horse's foot.

16.2.11.a.s: utkrāmodakrāmīditi dvābhyāṃ mṛtkhanādudañcamaśvamutkramayyāpo devīrupasṛjetyaśvasya pade 'pa upasṛjya pade hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya
16.2.11.a.d: उत्क्रामोदक्रामीदिति द्वाभ्यां मृत्खनादुदञ्चमश्वमुत्क्रमय्यापो देवीरुपसृजेत्यश्वस्य पदे ऽप उपसृज्य पदे हिरण्यं निधाय
16.2.11.a.m: Having made the horse step northward out of the clay-pit with the two [formulas], 'Step out' and 'It has stepped out,' having poured water into the horse's footprint with 'Divine waters, flow forth,' and having placed gold in the footprint,

16.3.1.a.s: jigharmy agnim ā tvā jigharmīti manasvatībhyām ekām āhutiṃ hiraṇye hutvāpādāya hiraṇyaṃ pari vājapatiḥ kavir agniriti tisṛbhirabhriyā mṛtkhanaṃ parilikhati /
16.3.1.a.d: जिघर्म्य् अग्निम् आ त्वा जिघर्मीति मनस्वतीभ्याम् एकाम् आहुतिं हिरण्ये हुत्वापादाय हिरण्यं परि वाजपतिः कविर् अग्निरिति तिसृभिरभ्रिया मृत्खनं परिलिखति ।
16.3.1.a.m: having offered a single oblation upon the gold with the two mind-formulas, 'I moisten Agni' and 'I moisten you,' and having taken up the gold, he traces around the clay-pit with the spade with the three [verses], 'Around, the lord of prize, the seer Agni…'

16.3.2.a.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti dvābhyāṃ khanati
16.3.2.a.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति द्वाभ्यां खनति
16.3.2.a.m: With the two [formulas], 'At the instigation of divine Savitṛ,' he digs.

16.3.3.a.s: apāṃ pṛṣṭham asīti puṣkaraparṇam āhṛtyaitayaiva viveṣṭya śarma ca stho varma ca stha iti dvābhyām uttareṇa mṛtkhanaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstṛṇāti /
16.3.3.a.d: अपां पृष्ठम् असीति पुष्करपर्णम् आहृत्यैतयैव विवेष्ट्य शर्म च स्थो वर्म च स्थ इति द्वाभ्याम् उत्तरेण मृत्खनं कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमास्तृणाति ।
16.3.3.a.m: Having fetched a lotus-leaf with 'You are the back of the waters,' and having wrapped it with this very [formula], he spreads a black antelope skin north of the clay-pit, with its neck pointing east and its hair facing upward, with the two [formulas], 'You two are protection, and you two are armour.'

16.3.3.b.m: Above it [he places] the lotus-leaf face upward.

16.3.4.a.s: purīṣyo 'si viśvabharā iti mṛtkhanam abhimantrya tvām agne puṣkarād adhīti kṛṣṇājine puṣkaraparṇe ca saṃbharati catasṛbhis tisṛbhir vā /
16.3.4.a.d: पुरीष्यो ऽसि विश्वभरा इति मृत्खनम् अभिमन्त्र्य त्वाम् अग्ने पुष्कराद् अधीति कृष्णाजिने पुष्करपर्णे च संभरति चतसृभिस् तिसृभिर् वा ।
16.3.4.a.m: Having addressed the clay-pit with 'You are earthly, all-bearing,' he collects [the clay] onto the black antelope skin and the lotus-leaf with 'You, O Agni, from the lotus…' using four or three [verses]:

16.3.4.b.m: with gāyatrī verses for a brāhmaṇa;

16.3.4.c.m: with triṣṭubh verses for a rājanya;

16.3.5.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta vasīyān syād ity ubhayībhis tasya saṃbharet
16.3.5.a.d: यं कामयेत वसीयान् स्याद् इत्य् उभयीभिस् तस्य संभरेत्
16.3.5.a.m: For one whom he wishes to become wealthier, he should collect with both.

16.3.7.a.s: janiṣvā hi jenya iti mṛdam abhimṛśya mṛtkhanaṃ saṃlobhya saṃ te vāyur iti mṛtkhane 'pa ānīya samudyamya kṛṣṇājinasyāntānsujāto jyotiṣā saheti kṣaumeṇa mauñjenārkamayeṇa vā dāmnopanahyati
16.3.7.a.d: जनिष्वा हि जेन्य इति मृदम् अभिमृश्य मृत्खनं संलोभ्य सं ते वायुर् इति मृत्खने ऽप आनीय समुद्यम्य कृष्णाजिनस्यान्तान्सुजातो ज्योतिषा सहेति क्षौमेण मौञ्जेनार्कमयेण वा दाम्नोपनह्यति
16.3.7.a.m: Having touched the clay with 'Be born, noble one,' having smoothed the clay-pit, having poured water into the clay-pit with 'May Vāyu unite you,' and having lifted the corners of the black antelope skin, he ties it up with 'Well-born with light' using a cord of linen, of muñja grass, or made of arka.

16.3.8.a.s: udu tiṣṭha svadhvarordhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaya iti sāvitrībhyāmuttiṣṭhati
16.3.8.a.d: उदु तिष्ठ स्वध्वरोर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतय इति सावित्रीभ्यामुत्तिष्ठति
16.3.8.a.m: He stands up with the two Savitṛ verses, 'Rise up, of good sacrifice' and 'Upright unto us for help.'

16.3.9.a.m: He carries [it] with 'Born, you are the embryo.'

16.3.10.a.s: sthiro bhava vīḍvaṅga iti gardabhasya pṛṣṭha ādadaḥti
16.3.10.a.d: स्थिरो भव वीड्वङ्ग इति गर्दभस्य पृष्ठ आददःति
16.3.10.a.m: With 'Be firm, strong-limbed,' he places it on the back of the donkey.

16.3.11.a.m: He addresses it once placed with 'Be for the welfare of creatures tomorrow.'

16.3.12.a.m: They return without haste with the three [verses], 'Let the courser advance neighing.'

16.3.13.a.s: agniṃ purīṣyamaṅgirasvadbharāma iti yena dveṣyeṇa saṃgacchate tamabhimantrayate /
16.3.13.a.d: अग्निं पुरीष्यमङ्गिरस्वद्भराम इति येन द्वेष्येण संगच्छते तमभिमन्त्रयते ।
16.3.13.a.m: With 'We bear the earthly Agni as did the Aṅgirases,' he addresses any hateful person he encounters;

16.3.14.a.s: uttareṇa vihāraṃ pariśrita oṣadhayaḥ prati gṛhṇītāgnimetamiti dvābhyāmoṣadhīṣu puṣpavatīṣu phalavatīṣūpāvaharati
16.3.14.a.d: उत्तरेण विहारं परिश्रित ओषधयः प्रति गृह्णीताग्निमेतमिति द्वाभ्यामोषधीषु पुष्पवतीषु फलवतीषूपावहरति
16.3.14.a.m: To the north of the sacrificial ground, inside an enclosure, he sets it down among flowering and fruit-bearing plants with the two [verses], 'O plants, receive this Agni.'

16.4.1.a.s: vi pājaseti visrasyāpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva iti tisṛbhirapa upasṛjya mitraḥ saṃsṛjya pṛthivīmiti dvābhyāṃ saṃsarjanīyaiḥ saṃsṛjati /
16.4.1.a.d: वि पाजसेति विस्रस्यापो हि ष्ठा मयोभुव इति तिसृभिरप उपसृज्य मित्रः संसृज्य पृथिवीमिति द्वाभ्यां संसर्जनीयैः संसृजति ।
16.4.1.a.m: Having untied [it] with 'With wide light,' having poured water with the three [verses], 'You, waters, are indeed refreshing,' he mixes it with the mixing ingredients with the two [formulas], 'Mitra, having united the earth…'—

16.4.1.b.s: armakapālaiḥ piṣṭairveṇvaṅgārairvrīhituṣaiḥ palāśakaṣāyeṇa śarkarābhiḥ piṣṭābhiḥ kṛṣṇājinalomabhirajalomabhiriti
16.4.1.b.d: अर्मकपालैः पिष्टैर्वेण्वङ्गारैर्व्रीहितुषैः पलाशकषायेण शर्कराभिः पिष्टाभिः कृष्णाजिनलोमभिरजलोमभिरिति
16.4.1.b.m: with crushed potsherds from an abandoned site, bamboo embers, rice husks, a decoction of palāśa bark, crushed gravel, hair of a black antelope, and hair of a goat—

16.4.2.a.m: and whatever else he considers useful for the purpose of making it firm.

16.4.3.a.s: rudrāḥ saṃbhṛtya pṛthivīmiti mṛdaṃ saṃkṣipya saṃsṛṣṭāṃ vasubhiriti tisṛbhiḥ kartre prayacchati
16.4.3.a.d: रुद्राः संभृत्य पृथिवीमिति मृदं संक्षिप्य संसृष्टां वसुभिरिति तिसृभिः कर्त्रे प्रयच्छति
16.4.3.a.m: Having gathered the clay with 'The Rudras, having assembled the earth,' he hands it over to the maker with the three [formulas], 'Mixed by the Vasus…'

16.4.4.a.s: makhasya śiro 'sīti piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā yajñasya pade stha iti kṛṣṇājinaṃ puṣkaraparṇaṃ cābhivṛśati mṛdi vāṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ nigṛhṇāti
16.4.4.a.d: मखस्य शिरो ऽसीति पिण्डं कृत्वा यज्ञस्य पदे स्थ इति कृष्णाजिनं पुष्करपर्णं चाभिवृशति मृदि वाङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां निगृह्णाति
16.4.4.a.m: Having made a lump with 'You are the head of Makha,' he touches the black antelope skin and the lotus-leaf with 'You two are the footprints of the sacrifice,' or presses down into the clay with his two thumbs.

16.4.5.a.s: vasavastvā kṛṇvantu gāyatreṇa cchandaseti caturbhirmahiṣyukhāṃ karoti bahubhāryasya /
16.4.5.a.d: वसवस्त्वा कृण्वन्तु गायत्रेण च्छन्दसेति चतुर्भिर्महिष्युखां करोति बहुभार्यस्य ।
16.4.5.a.m: With the four [formulas], 'May the Vasus make you with the gāyatrī metre,' the chief queen makes the ukhā-pot for one who has many wives;

16.4.5.b.m: the adhvaryu, for one who has one wife.

16.4.6.a.m: While it is being made, the sacrificer follows it with these same [formulas].

16.4.7.a.m: [It has] three layers, five layers, or an unmeasured number of layers;

16.4.7.c.m: a span in height, a cubit in width, a fathom in circumference;

16.4.8.a.s: pañcaprādeśāmiṣumātrīṃ vā yadi pañca paśvo bhavantīti vājasaneyakam
16.4.8.a.d: पञ्चप्रादेशामिषुमात्रीं वा यदि पञ्च पश्वो भवन्तीति वाजसनेयकम्
16.4.8.a.m: Five spans or an arrow-length [in size] if there are five sacrificial animals: so says the Vājasaneyaka.

16.4.9.a.m: In making it, he raises four corners towards the cardinal directions;

16.4.11.a.m: For one practicing sorcery, he should make it nine-cornered.

16.5.1.a.m: he makes a girdle with 'You are Aditi's girdle.'

16.5.2.a.s: aśrīṇāṃ rāsnāyāśca saṃdhau dvau caturaḥ ṣaḍaṣṭau vā stanānkaroti
16.5.2.a.d: अश्रीणां रास्नायाश्च संधौ द्वौ चतुरः षडष्टौ वा स्तनान्करोति
16.5.2.a.m: At the junction of the corners and the girdle, he makes two, four, six, or eight nipples.

16.5.3.a.m: Having fashioned the rim with 'May Aditi take your rim,'

16.5.4.a.s: ya ukhāṃ karoti so 'ṣāḍhāmetasyā eva mṛdastūṣṇīṃ caturaśrāṃ tryālikhitāmiṣṭakām
16.5.4.a.d: य उखां करोति सो ऽषाढामेतस्या एव मृदस्तूष्णीं चतुरश्रां त्र्यालिखितामिष्टकाम्
16.5.4.a.m: whoever makes the ukhā-pot makes the aṣāḍhā brick silently from this very clay, four-cornered, with three lines drawn upon it.

16.5.5.a.s: vasavastvā dhūpayantu gāyatreṇa cchandaseti saptabhiraśvaśakenokhāṃ dhūpayati
16.5.5.a.d: वसवस्त्वा धूपयन्तु गायत्रेण च्छन्दसेति सप्तभिरश्वशकेनोखां धूपयति
16.5.5.a.m: With the seven [formulas], 'May the Vasus fumigate you with the gāyatrī metre,' he fumigates the ukhā-pot with horse dung;

16.5.6.a.m: with the dung of a stallion, say some.

16.5.7.a.m: The fumigation and the baking are done with [fire] from the gārhapatya.

16.5.8.a.s: aditistvā devītyagreṇa gārhapatyamavaṭaṃ khātvā lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhārairavastīrya devānāṃ tvā patnīriti tasminnukhāmavadadhāti
16.5.8.a.d: अदितिस्त्वा देवीत्यग्रेण गार्हपत्यमवटं खात्वा लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैरवस्तीर्य देवानां त्वा पत्नीरिति तस्मिन्नुखामवदधाति
16.5.8.a.m: Having dug a pit in front of the gārhapatya with 'You, the goddess Aditi,' and having strewn it with materials for baking red, he places the ukhā-pot down into it with 'You, the wives of the gods.'

16.5.9.a.s: tūṣṇīmaṣāḍhāmanvavadhāya lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhāraiḥ pracchādya dhiṣaṇāstvā devīriti caturbhirukhāyāmagnimabhyādadhāti
16.5.9.a.d: तूष्णीमषाढामन्ववधाय लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैः प्रच्छाद्य धिषणास्त्वा देवीरिति चतुर्भिरुखायामग्निमभ्यादधाति
16.5.9.a.m: Silently putting in the aṣāḍhā [brick], covering [the whole] with materials for baking red, he places fire into the pan with the four [verses], 'May the divine Dhiṣaṇās...'

16.5.10.a.m: While it is being baked, he attends to it with the three [verses] addressed to Mitra, 'O Mitra, bake this pan...'

16.5.11.a.s: pakvāṃ devastvā savitodvapatvityudvāsyāpadyamānā pṛthivyāśā diśa ā pṛṇetyuttarataḥ sikatāsu pratiṣṭhāpya mitraitāṃ ta ukhāṃ paridadāmyabhitryā eṣā mā bhedīti mitrāya paridadāti
16.5.11.a.d: पक्वां देवस्त्वा सवितोद्वपत्वित्युद्वास्यापद्यमाना पृथिव्याशा दिश आ पृणेत्युत्तरतः सिकतासु प्रतिष्ठाप्य मित्रैतां त उखां परिददाम्यभित्र्या एषा मा भेदीति मित्राय परिददाति
16.5.11.a.m: When it is baked, he lifts it off with 'May divine Savitṛ lift you off...', places it to the north on sand with 'Not falling to earth, fill the quarters and directions!', and commits it to Mitra with 'O Mitra, I commit this pan to you for non-destruction, lest it break.'

16.5.12.a.m: Having silently lifted off the aṣāḍhā [brick],

16.6.1.a.m: he pours goat's milk into the pan with the four [formulas], 'May the Vasus unclose you with the Gāyatrī metre...'

16.6.2.a.s: saptaikaviṃśatiṃ vā māsānādāya puruṣaśiro 'cchaiti vaiśyasya rājanyasya veṣuhatasyāśanihatasya vā
16.6.2.a.d: सप्तैकविंशतिं वा मासानादाय पुरुषशिरो ऽच्छैति वैश्यस्य राजन्यस्य वेषुहतस्याशनिहतस्य वा
16.6.2.a.m: Having taken seven or twenty-one beans, he goes to fetch the head of a man—of a Vaiśya or a Rājanya, killed by an arrow or killed by lightning.

16.6.3.a.s: māṣānupanyupyāyaṃ yo 'si yasya ta idaṃ śira iti puruṣaśiraḥ pracchidyaitena tvamatra śīrṣaṇvānedhīti saptadhā vitṛṇāṃ valmīkavapāṃ śirasaḥ sthāne pratinidadhāti
16.6.3.a.d: माषानुपन्युप्यायं यो ऽसि यस्य त इदं शिर इति पुरुषशिरः प्रच्छिद्यैतेन त्वमत्र शीर्षण्वानेधीति सप्तधा वितृणां वल्मीकवपां शिरसः स्थाने प्रतिनिदधाति
16.6.3.a.m: Having scattered the beans, he severs the head of the man with 'This one who you are, whose head this is...', and in place of the head deposits an anthill mound pierced seven ways, with 'By means of this, be endowed with a head here!'

16.6.4.a.d: यो ऽस्य कौष्ठ्य जगतः पार्थिवस्यैक इद्वशी ।
16.6.4.a.m: 'Who, dwelling in the storehouse of this earthly world, is the sole ruler,

16.6.4.b.m: Sing of Yama, O Bhaṅgyaśravas, who is the unopposable king!

16.6.4.c.m: Sing of Yama, O Bhaṅgyaśravas, who is the unopposable king,

16.6.4.d.s: yenāpo nadyo dhanvāni yena dyauḥ pṛthivī dṛḍhā //
16.6.4.d.d: येनापो नद्यो धन्वानि येन द्यौः पृथिवी दृढा ॥
16.6.4.d.m: by whom the waters, the rivers, the deserts, by whom heaven and earth are made firm!

16.6.4.e.m: Golden-girthed, easy to harness, golden-eyed, iron-hoofed,

16.6.4.f.s: aśvānanaśyato dānaṃ yamo rājābhitiṣṭhatīti tisṛbhiryamagāthābhiḥ parigāyati
16.6.4.f.d: अश्वाननश्यतो दानं यमो राजाभितिष्ठतीति तिसृभिर्यमगाथाभिः परिगायति
16.6.4.f.m: undecaying horses—king Yama mounts this gift.' With these three Yama-gāthās he sings around [the head].

16.6.6.a.s: idamasmākaṃ bhuje bhogāya bhūyāditi puruṣaśira ādāyodehyagne adhi mātuḥ pṛthivyā ityāharati
16.6.6.a.d: इदमस्माकं भुजे भोगाय भूयादिति पुरुषशिर आदायोदेह्यग्ने अधि मातुः पृथिव्या इत्याहरति
16.6.6.a.m: Taking the head of the man with 'May this be for our enjoyment, for our pleasure!', he brings it with 'Rise up, O Agni, from mother earth!'

16.6.7.a.m: 'Agni goes round the sacrifice three times like a charioteer,

16.6.7.c.m: This [second verse is]: 'Round about, the lord of prize, the seer...'

16.6.7.d.m: 'The divine Agni has gone round, killer of rakṣases, expeller of sickness,

16.6.7.e.s: sedhanviśvā apa dviṣo dhanrakṣāṃsi viśvaheti tisṛbhiḥ paryagnikṛtvā mṛdā pralipya nidadhāti
16.6.7.e.d: सेधन्विश्वा अप द्विषो धन्रक्षांसि विश्वहेति तिसृभिः पर्यग्निकृत्वा मृदा प्रलिप्य निदधाति
16.6.7.e.m: driving away all foes, burning the rakṣases forever.' Having carried fire around [the head] with these three [verses], and having smeared it with clay, he deposits it.

16.7.1.a.m: He seizes uncastrated animals for the Agnis according to desire:

16.7.1.b.m: having assigned a hornless he-goat for Prajāpati, a horse, a bull, a ram, and a he-goat.

16.7.2.a.m: He recites twenty-one or twenty-four continuous sāmidhenī verses:

16.7.2.c.m: ten verses belonging to the fire ritual, [beginning with] 'May the years, O Agni...'

16.7.3.a.s: rāyo agne mahe tvā dānāya samidhīmahi /
16.7.3.a.d: रायो अग्ने महे त्वा दानाय समिधीमहि ।
16.7.3.a.m: 'For great wealth to be given, O Agni, we would kindle you;

16.7.3.b.s: īḍiṣvā hi mahī vṛṣandyāvā hotrāya pṛthivīmiti yadyekaviṃśatiḥ
16.7.3.b.d: ईडिष्वा हि मही वृषन्द्यावा होत्राय पृथिवीमिति यद्येकविंशतिः
16.7.3.b.m: implore, O bull, the great heaven and earth for the hotṛ's office'—[these are added] if there are twenty-one.

16.7.4.a.s: upemasṛkṣi vājayurvacasyāṃ cano dadhīta nādyo giro me /
16.7.4.a.d: उपेमसृक्षि वाजयुर्वचस्यां चनो दधीत नाद्यो गिरो मे ।
16.7.4.a.m: 'Desiring a prize, I have sent forth this well-spoken speech; may the river-god accept my hymns;

16.7.4.b.m: swiftly moving Apāṃ Napāt, may he make them well adorned, for he will be pleased.'

16.7.4.d.s: apāṃ napādā hyasthādupasthaṃ jihmānāmūrdhvaḥ svayaśā upasthe /
16.7.4.d.d: अपां नपादा ह्यस्थादुपस्थं जिह्मानामूर्ध्वः स्वयशा उपस्थे ।
16.7.4.d.m: 'Apāṃ Napāt has mounted the lap of the crooked [waters], upright, glorious in their lap;

16.7.4.e.s: ubhe abhi priyatame sadhasthe ā ca parā ca carati prajānanniti tisro 'psumatīryadi caturviṃśatiḥ
16.7.4.e.d: उभे अभि प्रियतमे सधस्थे आ च परा च चरति प्रजानन्निति तिस्रो ऽप्सुमतीर्यदि चतुर्विंशतिः
16.7.4.e.m: knowing well, he moves between both dearest common homes'—these three water-verses [are added] if there are twenty-four.

16.7.5.a.m: For a sick [sacrificer], he should say: 'May he be in that world.'

16.7.6.a.m: For one who is not sick: 'O Bṛhaspati, O Savitṛ, awaken him.'

16.7.7.a.m: They conclude with the verse containing 'light', 'Up from darkness...'

16.7.8.a.m: He performs the continuous offering from the ladle with 'The golden embryo evolved in the beginning...'

16.7.9.a.s: ūrdhvā asya samidho bhavantīti prayājānāmāpriyo bhavanti
16.7.9.a.d: ऊर्ध्वा अस्य समिधो भवन्तीति प्रयाजानामाप्रियो भवन्ति
16.7.9.a.m: The āprī verses of the fore-offerings are those beginning with 'Upward are his firebrands...'

16.7.10.a.m: Triṣṭubh verses addressed to Agni are the invitatory and consecratory verses for those [offerings] addressed to Agni.

16.7.11.a.s: yaḥ prāṇato ya ātmadā iti prājāpatyasya
16.7.11.a.d: यः प्राणतो य आत्मदा इति प्राजापत्यस्य
16.7.11.a.m: The two verses 'Who is the giver of breath, who is the giver of soul...' are for the [offering] dedicated to Prajāpati.

16.7.12.a.s: api vā saṃjñaptānāṃ śirāṃsi pracchidya mṛdā pralipya nidadhāti
16.7.12.a.d: अपि वा संज्ञप्तानां शिरांसि प्रच्छिद्य मृदा प्रलिप्य निदधाति
16.7.12.a.m: Or, having severed the heads of the suffocated [animals] and smeared them with clay, he deposits them.

16.8.1.a.m: They carry the headless trunks down to the water.

16.8.2.a.m: It is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: 'He concludes [the rite] with the one dedicated to Prajāpati.'

16.8.3.a.s: api vā sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ sthāne vāyave niyutvate śvetamajaṃ tūparamālabhate
16.8.3.a.d: अपि वा सर्वेषामेतेषां स्थाने वायवे नियुत्वते श्वेतमजं तूपरमालभते
16.8.3.a.m: Or rather, in place of all these, he seizes a white hornless he-goat for Vāyu accompanied by the Niyuts.

16.8.4.a.m: The invitatory and consecratory verses for the omentum contain the words 'vāyu' and 'śveta';

16.8.4.b.m: those for the offering of animal flesh contain the words 'vāyu' and 'niyut'.

16.8.5.a.s: tasya śiraḥ pracchidya mṛdā pralipya nidadhāti
16.8.5.a.d: तस्य शिरः प्रच्छिद्य मृदा प्रलिप्य निदधाति
16.8.5.a.m: Having severed its head and smeared it with clay, he deposits it.

16.8.6.a.m: It has been said: 'The actions relating to Vāyu should be performed.'

16.8.7.a.m: For it, he pours out a sacrificial animal-cake on twelve potsherds for Agni Vaiśvānara.

16.8.8.a.s: yaḥ kaścanāgnau paśurālabhyate vaiśvānara evāsya dvādaśakapālaḥ paśupuroḍāśo bhavatītyeke
16.8.8.a.d: यः कश्चनाग्नौ पशुरालभ्यते वैश्वानर एवास्य द्वादशकपालः पशुपुरोडाशो भवतीत्येके
16.8.8.a.m: Some say: 'Whatever animal is seized at the fire, its animal-cake is on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara alone.'

16.8.9.a.s: teneṣṭvā saṃvatsaraṃ na māṃsamaśnīyānna striyamupeyānnopari śyīta
16.8.9.a.d: तेनेष्ट्वा संवत्सरं न मांसमश्नीयान्न स्त्रियमुपेयान्नोपरि श्यीत
16.8.9.a.m: Having sacrificed with it, he should not eat meat, nor approach a woman, nor sleep on a raised couch for a year.

16.8.10.a.s: api vā māṃsamaśnīyādupari śayīta striyaṃ tveva nopeyāditi vājasneyakam
16.8.10.a.d: अपि वा मांसमश्नीयादुपरि शयीत स्त्रियं त्वेव नोपेयादिति वाजस्नेयकम्
16.8.10.a.m: Or rather, he may eat meat and sleep on a raised couch, but he should certainly not approach a woman: thus the Vājasaneyaka.

16.8.11.a.m: Having performed whatever comes prior to the consecration offering, he pours out the consecration offering consisting of three oblations.

16.8.12.a.m: For one who has not borne [the fire in the pan] for a year, the third is for Vaiśvānara on twelve potsherds, [offered] beforehand.

16.8.13.a.d: यत्प्राग्दीक्षाहुतीभ्यस्तत्कृत्वाकूत्यै प्रयुजे ऽग्नये स्वाहेति पञ्चाध्वरिकीर्हुत्वाकूतिमग्निमिति षडाग्निकीः ।
16.8.13.a.m: Having performed whatever comes prior to the consecration oblations, having offered the five oblations belonging to the basic sacrifice with 'To intention, to impulse, to Agni, svāhā!', and the six belonging to the fire ritual with 'Intention, Agni...';

16.8.13.b.m: he offers the seventh, the full oblation, with 'Of the divine guide, all...'

16.8.14.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta pramāyukaḥ syāditi tasya sakṛdanudrutya juhuyāt /
16.8.14.a.d: यं कामयेत प्रमायुकः स्यादिति तस्य सकृदनुद्रुत्य जुहुयात् ।
16.8.14.a.m: For one whom he would wish 'May he be liable to die!', he should offer by reciting continuously at one stretch;

16.8.14.c.m: he indeed becomes deaf, so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

16.9.1.a.m: The consecrated one carries the fire in the pan for a year,

16.9.1.b.m: or for three days, or for six days, or for twelve days.

16.9.2.a.m: 'Whoever [piles the fire] inside of a year, he is only a builder of pain,' say some.

16.9.3.a.m: It has already been said: 'By Agni's initiation indeed…'

16.9.4.a.s: yatprāṅmuṣṭikarmaṇastatkṛtvā śaṇakulāyane vokhāṃ pracchādya mā su bhitthā iti dvābhyāmāhavanīye pravṛṇakti
16.9.4.a.d: यत्प्राङ्मुष्टिकर्मणस्तत्कृत्वा शणकुलायने वोखां प्रच्छाद्य मा सु भित्था इति द्वाभ्यामाहवनीये प्रवृणक्ति
