16.9.4.a.m: Having performed whatever precedes the closing of the fists, or having covered the ukhā-pot with a nest of hemp, he places it upside down on the āhavanīya with the two [formulas], 'Do not break!'

16.9.5.a.m: With 'O Mitra, heat this ukhā-pot,' he surrounds it clockwise with burning embers.

16.9.6.a.s: dvarannaḥ sarpirāsutiriti tasyāṃ krumukamullikhitaṃ ghṛtenāktvāvadadhāti muñjāṃśca
16.9.6.a.d: द्वरन्नः सर्पिरासुतिरिति तस्यां क्रुमुकमुल्लिखितं घृतेनाक्त्वावदधाति मुञ्जांश्च
16.9.6.a.m: With the verse, 'Having ghee as drink, butter as food…' he puts into it a scraped piece of krumuka wood, having anointed it with ghee, and muñja grass.

16.9.7.a.m: The case of one who has attained prosperity has been stated.

16.9.8.a.s: pradāvyādāharedyaṃ kāmayeta prasyandinayāmasya rāṣṭraṃ jāyukaṃ syāditi /
16.9.8.a.d: प्रदाव्यादाहरेद्यं कामयेत प्रस्यन्दिनयामस्य राष्ट्रं जायुकं स्यादिति ।
16.9.8.a.m: He should bring it from a forest fire for him of whom he desires, 'May his realm become flowing with wealth.'

16.9.8.b.m: From the burning top of a tree for one who desires spiritual lustre;

16.9.8.c.m: from a parching pan for one who desires food.

16.9.9.a.m: When performing the fire for a specific wish, he should not turn [the pot] over on the āhavanīya.

16.9.10.a.m: When [the fire] is born in the pot, he allows the āhavanīya to expire.

16.9.11.a.s: parasyā adhi saṃvata iti vaikaṅkatīṃ samidhamādadhāti
16.9.11.a.d: परस्या अधि संवत इति वैकङ्कतीं समिधमादधाति
16.9.11.a.m: With the verse, 'From the further reach…' he puts on a firewood stick of vikankaṭa wood.

16.9.12.a.m: With the verse, 'From the farthest distance…' [he puts on] one made of śamī wood.

16.9.14.a.s: sīda tvaṃ mātur asyā upastha iti tisṛbhir jātamukhyam upatiṣṭhate
16.9.14.a.d: सीद त्वं मातुर् अस्या उपस्थ इति तिसृभिर् जातमुख्यम् उपतिष्ठते
16.9.14.a.m: With three verses beginning with 'Sit thou in the lap of this mother…' he attends upon the [fire] born in the pot.

16.10.1.a.s: yadagne yāni kāni ceti pañcabhiraudumbaramaparaśuvṛkṇamukhya idhmamabhyādadhāti
16.10.1.a.d: यदग्ने यानि कानि चेति पञ्चभिरौदुम्बरमपरशुवृक्णमुख्य इध्ममभ्यादधाति
16.10.1.a.m: With five verses beginning with 'Whatever, O Agni, whatsoever…' he places onto the [fire] in the pot firewood of udumbara wood, not cut down with an axe.

16.10.2.a.m: One of tilvaka wood for one practicing sorcery.

16.10.3.a.m: With the verse, 'With both fangs the robbers…' he puts on a firewood stick of aśvattha wood.

16.10.4.a.m: With 'Those thieves who are among people…' one of vikankaṭa wood.

16.10.5.a.m: With 'Whosoever would act with hostility against us…' one made of śamī wood.

16.10.6.a.s: tasmādagnicitaḥ pāpaṃ na kīrtayenno agniṃ bibhrato no agnividaḥ
16.10.6.a.d: तस्मादग्निचितः पापं न कीर्तयेन्नो अग्निं बिभ्रतो नो अग्निविदः
16.10.6.a.m: Therefore, one should not utter evil of one who has piled the fire, nor of one bearing the fire, nor of one who knows the fire.

16.10.7.a.s: saṃśitaṃ me brahmodeṣāṃ bāhū atiramityuttame yajamānaṃ vācayaṃstūṣṇīmaudumbaryau samidhāvādadhāti
16.10.7.a.d: संशितं मे ब्रह्मोदेषां बाहू अतिरमित्युत्तमे यजमानं वाचयंस्तूष्णीमौदुम्बर्यौ समिधावादधाति
16.10.7.a.m: Making the sacrificer recite the two verses, 'Sharpened is my prayer…' and 'I have raised their arms…', he silently puts on two firewood sticks of udumbara wood.

16.10.8.a.s: māteva putraṃ pṛthivī purīṣyamagniṃ sve yonau bhariṣyatyukhā /
16.10.8.a.d: मातेव पुत्रं पृथिवी पुरीष्यमग्निं स्वे योनौ भरिष्यत्युखा ।
16.10.8.a.m: 'Like a mother her son, the earth [shall bear] the fire belonging to the soil; the pot shall bear it in its own birthplace.

16.10.8.b.s: tāṃ viśvairdevairṛtubhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ prajāpatirviśvakarmā yunaktviti mauñje śikye ṣaḍudyāme dvādaśodyāme vokhāmavadadhāti
16.10.8.b.d: तां विश्वैर्देवैरृतुभिः संविदानः प्रजापतिर्विश्वकर्मा युनक्त्विति मौञ्जे शिक्ये षडुद्यामे द्वादशोद्यामे वोखामवदधाति
16.10.8.b.m: Agreement made with all the gods and the seasons, let Prajāpati Viśvakarman yoke it'—with this verse he places the pot into a sling made of muñja grass, six spans long or twelve spans long.

16.10.9.a.s: ekaviṃśatinirbodho yo rukmaḥ sūtroto dṛśāno rukma iti tamāsīno yajamāno 'ntarnirbādhaṃ pratimucya bahirnirbādhānkurute
16.10.9.a.d: एकविंशतिनिर्बोधो यो रुक्मः सूत्रोतो दृशानो रुक्म इति तमासीनो यजमानो ऽन्तर्निर्बाधं प्रतिमुच्य बहिर्निर्बाधान्कुरुते
16.10.9.a.m: A gold plate having twenty-one knobs, strung on a cord: with 'The visible gold plate…' the sacrificer, sitting down, fastens it on so that the knobs face inward, and makes the knobs face outward.

16.10.10.a.m: With 'All forms…' he fastens the noose of the sling [about his neck].

16.10.11.a.m: With 'Night and Dawn…' [he fastens] the black antelope skin above.

16.10.12.a.s: suparṇo 'si garutmānityukhyamavekṣya suparṇo 'si garutmānityādāyotthāyopari nābherdhārayamāṇo viṣṇoḥ kramo 'sīti caturo viṣṇukramānprācaḥ krāmati
16.10.12.a.d: सुपर्णो ऽसि गरुत्मानित्युख्यमवेक्ष्य सुपर्णो ऽसि गरुत्मानित्यादायोत्थायोपरि नाभेर्धारयमाणो विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति चतुरो विष्णुक्रमान्प्राचः क्रामति
16.10.12.a.m: Looking at the fire in the pot with 'A fair-winged eagle art thou…', taking it up with 'A fair-winged eagle art thou…', rising, and holding it above the navel, he steps the four Viṣṇu strides toward the east with 'Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu.'

16.10.13.a.m: Having recited the verse, 'Agni has cried out…', he turns around clockwise with the four verses beginning with 'O Agni, turn back…'.

16.10.14.a.d: उदुत्तममिति शिक्यपाशमुन्मुच्या त्वाहार्षमित्याहृत्योपतिष्ठते ऽग्रे बृहन्नुषसामूर्ध्वो अस्थादिति
16.10.14.a.m: With 'The highest…' he unfastens the noose of the sling; having brought it forward with 'I have brought thee…', he attends upon it with 'High, upright in front of the dawns, he has stood…'.

16.10.15.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta rāṣṭraṃ syāditi taṃ manasā dhyāyet
16.10.15.a.d: यं कामयेत राष्ट्रं स्यादिति तं मनसा ध्यायेत्
16.10.15.a.m: Him of whom he desires that he may obtain a realm, he should contemplate in mind.

16.10.16.a.s: audumbaryāsandyaratnimātraśīrṣaṇyānūcyā prādeśamātrapādā mauñjavivānā phalakāstīrṇā vā mṛḍā pradigdhā
16.10.16.a.d: औदुम्बर्यासन्द्यरत्निमात्रशीर्षण्यानूच्या प्रादेशमात्रपादा मौञ्जविवाना फलकास्तीर्णा वा मृडा प्रदिग्धा
16.10.16.a.m: There is a stool of udumbara wood, an aratni long in its head-pieces and side-pieces, a span high in its feet, woven with muñja grass or spread over with planks, smeared with clay.

16.10.17.a.s: sīda tvaṃ māturasyā upastha iti tasyāṃ catasṛbhirukhyaṃ sādayati
16.10.17.a.d: सीद त्वं मातुरस्या उपस्थ इति तस्यां चतसृभिरुख्यं सादयति
16.10.17.a.m: On it, with four verses beginning with 'Sit thou in the lap of this mother…', he sets down the [fire] in the pot.

16.10.18.a.m: Or he sets it down on gravel with three verses.

16.10.18.b.m: He attends upon it with the Haṃsavatī verse, say some.

16.11.1.a.s: yena devā jyotiṣordhvā udāyanniti prādeśamātraiḥ kāṣṭhairukhyamupasaminddhe
16.11.1.a.d: येन देवा ज्योतिषोर्ध्वा उदायन्निति प्रादेशमात्रैः काष्ठैरुख्यमुपसमिन्द्धे
16.11.1.a.m: With 'By which light the gods rose upward…' he fuels the [fire] in the pot with pieces of firewood a span long.

16.11.3.a.d: व्रतकाले ऽन्नपते ऽन्नस्य नो देहीत्यौदुम्बरीं समिधं व्रते ऽक्त्वाभ्यादधाति
16.11.3.a.m: At the time of the fast-food, with 'O lord of food, give us food…' he puts on a firewood stick of udumbara wood, having anointed it in the fast-food.

16.11.4.a.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ gāyatreṇa cchandasā rātrimiṣṭakāmupadadhe tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdeti sāyaṃ samidhamādadhāti
16.11.4.a.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर्बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यां गायत्रेण च्छन्दसा रात्रिमिष्टकामुपदधे तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेति सायं समिधमादधाति
16.11.4.a.m: With 'At the impulse of divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the gāyatrī metre I place the night-brick; with that deity sit firmly like Aṅgiras,' he puts on a firewood stick in the evening.

16.11.5.a.m: With this very formula [substituting] 'with the triṣṭubh metre I place the day-brick' in the morning.

16.11.6.a.m: With eleven, twelve, or thirteen verses beginning with 'From the sky…' he attends upon it with the Vātsapra hymn.

16.11.7.a.m: On the previous day he steps the Viṣṇu strides;

16.11.7.b.m: on the following day he attends upon [the fire].

16.11.9.a.m: On the day he purchases the soma, on that day he should combine both:

16.11.9.b.m: he should step [the Viṣṇu strides] and attend upon [the fire].

16.11.10.a.m: He undertakes the rite beginning with the clenching of the fists.

16.11.11.a.s: yadyukhye bhriyamāṇe 'yaṃ devaḥ prajā abhimanyetāgneyībhirbhiṣagvatībhistisṛbhistisraḥ samidha ādadhyāt //
16.11.11.a.d: यद्युख्ये भ्रियमाणे ऽयं देवः प्रजा अभिमन्येताग्नेयीभिर्भिषग्वतीभिस्तिसृभिस्तिस्रः समिध आदध्यात् ॥
16.11.11.a.m: If while [the fire] is being carried in the pot, this god should rage against creatures, he should put on three firewood sticks with three verses addressed to Agni containing the word 'physician':

16.11.11.b.m: 'Bring us your own form as a physician, O Agni of black course;

16.11.11.d.s: tvaṃ no agne bhiṣagbhava deveṣu havyavāhanaḥ /
16.11.11.d.d: त्वं नो अग्ने भिषग्भव देवेषु हव्यवाहनः ।
16.11.11.d.m: Be thou our physician, O Agni, carrying the oblation among the gods;

16.11.11.f.m: We invoke thee as physician, as physician may we kindle thee;

16.11.11.g.m: be a physician for us among the gods.'

16.11.12.a.s: yadi kāmayeta varṣediti yāḥ saurī raśmivatīstābhistisṛbhistisraḥ samidha ādadhyāt //
16.11.12.a.d: यदि कामयेत वर्षेदिति याः सौरी रश्मिवतीस्ताभिस्तिसृभिस्तिस्रः समिध आदध्यात् ॥
16.11.12.a.m: If he desires, 'May it rain,' he should put on three firewood sticks with three verses addressed to Sūrya containing the word 'ray':

16.11.12.b.m: 'Sūrya plunges into the waters with his rays, best winner of booty;

16.11.12.c.m: be attentive to the singer, thou that increasest vitality!

16.11.12.d.d: परि यो रश्मिना दिवो ऽन्तान्ममे पृथिव्याः ।
16.11.12.d.m: He who with his ray measured the ends of heaven and earth,

16.11.12.e.m: filled both world-halves with his greatness.

16.11.12.f.m: Traversing, O god, thou spreadest the black thread of wealth without unravelling it,

16.11.12.g.m: the brandishing rays of Sūrya have set the darkness within the waters like a skin.'

16.11.13.a.s: yadi kāmayeta na varṣediti yāḥ saurīrbhrājasvatīstābhistisṛbhistisraḥ samidha ādadhyāt
16.11.13.a.d: यदि कामयेत न वर्षेदिति याः सौरीर्भ्राजस्वतीस्ताभिस्तिसृभिस्तिस्रः समिध आदध्यात्
16.11.13.a.m: If he desires, 'May it not rain,' he should put on three firewood sticks with three verses addressed to Sūrya containing the word 'bright':

16.12.1.a.s: adṛśvamasya ketavo vi raśmayo janām̐ anu /
16.12.1.a.d: अदृश्वमस्य केतवो वि रश्मयो जनाम्̐ अनु ।
16.12.1.a.m: 'Visible were his banners, his rays among the peoples,

16.12.1.d.s: divo rukma urucakṣā udeti dūre arthastaraṇirbhrājamānaḥ /
16.12.1.d.d: दिवो रुक्म उरुचक्षा उदेति दूरे अर्थस्तरणिर्भ्राजमानः ।
16.12.1.d.m: 'The golden disc of heaven, wide-seeing, rises, its goal far off, swift, shining;

16.12.1.e.s: nūnaṃ jaṇāḥ sūryeṇa prasūtā āyannarthāni kṛṇavannapāṃsīti
16.12.1.e.d: नूनं जणाः सूर्येण प्रसूता आयन्नर्थानि कृणवन्नपांसीति
16.12.1.e.m: Now may people, impelled by the sun, go to their pursuits and perform their works.'

16.12.2.a.s: yadyukhye bhriyamāṇe yajamānasya naśyedagne 'bhyāvartinnagne aṅgiraḥ punarūrjā saha rayyetyetābhiścatasṛbhirupatiṣṭheta
16.12.2.a.d: यद्युख्ये भ्रियमाणे यजमानस्य नश्येदग्ने ऽभ्यावर्तिन्नग्ने अङ्गिरः पुनरूर्जा सह रय्येत्येताभिश्चतसृभिरुपतिष्ठेत
16.12.2.a.m: If, while the fire in the pan is being carried, something of the sacrificer is lost, he should revere [the fire] with these four verses: 'O Agni, turning back…', 'O Agni, Aṅgiras…', 'Again with strength…', and 'Together with wealth…'

16.12.3.a.m: 'He surely finds it,' so it is taught.

16.12.4.a.s: yadahaḥ prayāyādudu tvā viśve devā ityukhyamudyamya sīda tvaṃ māturasyā upastha iti catasṛbhirdvīṣe śakaṭe prauga ukhyamāsādayati
16.12.4.a.d: यदहः प्रयायादुदु त्वा विश्वे देवा इत्युख्यमुद्यम्य सीद त्वं मातुरस्या उपस्थ इति चतसृभिर्द्वीषे शकटे प्रौग उख्यमासादयति
16.12.4.a.m: On whichever day he would set out, having raised the fire in the pan with [the verse] 'Up may all the gods [bear] you…', he sets down the fire in the pan in the front-part of a two-poled cart with four [verses beginning]: 'Sit you in the lap of this mother…'

16.12.5.b.m: Some say he reveres it with the Haṃsavatī verse.

16.12.6.a.m: Having united the other two fires, having caused them to ascend [into fire-sticks], he sets out with [the formula]: 'March forth, O Agni, possessing light…'

16.12.7.a.m: He addresses the creaking of the axle with: 'Agni has cried out…'

16.12.8.a.m: Having settled [at a new dwelling place], he puts on a firewood stick smeared with ghee when he has halted, with [the verse]: 'Tend the fire with firewood…'

16.12.9.a.m: With the subsequent Triṣṭubh verse for a Rājanya;

16.12.10.a.m: When the kindling of the fire, the vow-meal, and the settling coincide, he places the [stick] smeared with ghee first.

16.12.11.a.s: yadyukhāṃ bhasmābhiniṣīdedukhyamādāyodakāntaṃ gatvemaṃ suyoniṃ suvṛtaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ sahasrabhṛṣṭiṃ mahiṣāvaroha /
16.12.11.a.d: यद्युखां भस्माभिनिषीदेदुख्यमादायोदकान्तं गत्वेमं सुयोनिं सुवृतं हिरण्मयं सहस्रभृष्टिं महिषावरोह ।
16.12.11.a.m: If ash settles down into the pan, having taken the fire in the pan and gone to the edge of the water, [with the two verses]: 'Descend, O mighty one, into this good womb, well-turned, golden, thousand-pointed;

16.12.11.b.m: Enjoy the sweet spring, enter into the oceanic dwelling;'

16.12.11.c.s: imaṃ stanaṃ madhumantaṃ dhyāpāṃ prapyātamagne sarirasya madhe /
16.12.11.c.d: इमं स्तनं मधुमन्तं ध्यापां प्रप्यातमग्ने सरिरस्य मधे ।
16.12.11.c.m: 'This sweet breast of the waters, swollen in the midst of the ocean, O Agni;

16.12.11.d.s: utsaṃ juṣasva madhumantamūrva samudriyaṃ sadanamāviśasvetyetābhyāmukhāyā agnimddhṛtyānirūhañchikyādukhāmāpo devīḥ prati gṛhṇīta bhasmaitaditi tisṛbhirapsu bhasma praveśayati
16.12.11.d.d: उत्सं जुषस्व मधुमन्तमूर्व समुद्रियं सदनमाविशस्वेत्येताभ्यामुखाया अग्निम्द्धृत्यानिरूहञ्छिक्यादुखामापो देवीः प्रति गृह्णीत भस्मैतदिति तिसृभिरप्सु भस्म प्रवेशयति
16.12.11.d.m: Enjoy the sweet spring, enter into the oceanic dwelling'—having raised the fire from the pan with these two [verses], without removing the pan from the halter, he introduces the ash into the waters with three [verses beginning]: 'O divine waters, receive this ash…'

16.12.12.a.s: bhasmano 'pādāya prapīḍya prasadya bhasmaneti dvābhyāmukhāyāṃ pratyavadhāya punarūrjā saha rayyeti punarudaiti
16.12.12.a.d: भस्मनो ऽपादाय प्रपीड्य प्रसद्य भस्मनेति द्वाभ्यामुखायां प्रत्यवधाय पुनरूर्जा सह रय्येति पुनरुदैति
16.12.12.a.m: Having taken [a portion] of the ash, squeezed it, and placed it back into the pan with two [verses beginning]: 'Settling with the ash…', he steps out [of the water] with: 'Again with strength, together with wealth…'

16.12.13.a.m: He kindles the fire in the pan again with: 'Again may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle you…'

16.13.1.a.m: He reveres [the fire] with the two Bodhavatī verses: 'Wake…', 'Be awake…'

16.13.2.a.m: The introduction of the ash into the waters is obligatory for a consecrated [sacrificer] when the bricks have been made.

16.13.2.b.m: When they have not been made, it serves the purpose of mixture [with the clay].

16.13.3.a.m: One who desires cattle should place it into the loose soil.

16.13.4.a.m: A wandering mendicant should cast it into the waters.

16.13.5.a.m: He makes the bricks for a consecrated [sacrificer] in the consecration procedures lasting a month or more; before [the consecration] for an unconsecrated one in other cases; [or] after the Prājāpatya animal sacrifice.

16.13.6.a.s: mṛnmayīriṣṭakāḥ karoti pādamātryo 'ratnimātrya ūrvasthimātry 'ṇūkamātrya ṛjulekhā dakṣiṇāvṛtaḥ savyāvṛtastryālikhitāśca
16.13.6.a.d: मृन्मयीरिष्टकाः करोति पादमात्र्यो ऽरत्निमात्र्य ऊर्वस्थिमात्र्य् ऽणूकमात्र्य ऋजुलेखा दक्षिणावृतः सव्यावृतस्त्र्यालिखिताश्च
16.13.6.a.m: He makes the earthen bricks: of the measure of a foot, of the measure of a cubit, of the measure of a thigh-bone, of the measure of an ankle-bone, straight-lined, turned to the right, turned to the left, and marked with three lines.

16.13.7.a.m: They bake them red with churned-out fire.

16.13.9.a.m: He should not lay one that is broken, black, or spotted.

16.13.10.a.s: puṣkaraparṇaṃ rukmo hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ srucau sapta svayamātṛṇāḥ śarkarā hiraṇyeṣṭakāḥ pañca ghṛteṣṭakā dūrvāstambaḥ kūrma ulūkhalaṃ musalaṃ śūrpamaśmānaḥ paśuśirāṃsi sarpaśiraścāmṛnmayīriṣṭakāḥ
16.13.10.a.d: पुष्करपर्णं रुक्मो हिरण्मयः पुरुषः स्रुचौ सप्त स्वयमातृणाः शर्करा हिरण्येष्टकाः पञ्च घृतेष्टका दूर्वास्तम्बः कूर्म उलूखलं मुसलं शूर्पमश्मानः पशुशिरांसि सर्पशिरश्चामृन्मयीरिष्टकाः
16.13.10.a.m: A lotus leaf, a golden disc, a golden man, two ladles, seven naturally perforated [stones], pebbles, golden bricks, five ghee bricks, a clump of dūrvā grass, a tortoise, a mortar, a pestle, a winnowing basket, stones, heads of animals, and a head of a serpent are the non-earthen bricks.

16.13.11.a.m: One who piles [the altar] for the first time should pile [it] knee-deep, of a thousand [bricks];

16.13.11.b.m: Navel-deep, of two thousand [bricks], for the second;

16.13.11.c.m: Mouth-deep, of three thousand [bricks], for the third;

16.13.12.a.m: 'One who desires heaven should pile it great, lofty, unmeasured,' so says the Vājasaneyaka.

16.14.1.a.s: apavṛtte dīkṣāparimāṇe 'peta vīteti gārhapatyaciterāyatanaṃ vyāyāmamātraṃ caturasraṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ voddhatya hariṇyā palāśaśākhayā śamīśākhayā vā saṃmṛjya prācīmudīcīṃ vā śākhāmudasitvā śaṃ no devīrabhiṣṭaya ityadbhiravokṣyāgnerbhasmāsīti sikatā nivapati
16.14.1.a.d: अपवृत्ते दीक्षापरिमाणे ऽपेत वीतेति गार्हपत्यचितेरायतनं व्यायाममात्रं चतुरस्रं परिमण्डलं वोद्धत्य हरिण्या पलाशशाखया शमीशाखया वा संमृज्य प्राचीमुदीचीं वा शाखामुदसित्वा शं नो देवीरभिष्टय इत्यद्भिरवोक्ष्याग्नेर्भस्मासीति सिकता निवपति
16.14.1.a.m: When the measure of the consecration has passed, having dug up the site of the gārhapatya piling measuring a fathom, square or round, with [the formula] 'Begone! Depart…', having swept it with a leafy branch of palāśa or a branch of śamī, having cast away the branch toward the east or the north, and having sprinkled it with water with 'May the divine waters be for our aid…', he pours out sand with 'You are the ash of Agni…'

16.14.3.a.m: While pouring them out, he meditates in mind: 'What is black yonder in the moon, let that be here.'

16.14.4.a.s: saṃ yā vaḥ priyāstanuva ityūṣānsikatāśca saṃsṛjya cita stha paricita ityekaviṃśatyā śarkarābhirgārhapatyaciterāyatanaṃ pariśrayati /
16.14.4.a.d: सं या वः प्रियास्तनुव इत्यूषान्सिकताश्च संसृज्य चित स्थ परिचित इत्येकविंशत्या शर्कराभिर्गार्हपत्यचितेरायतनं परिश्रयति ।
16.14.4.a.m: Having mixed the saline earth and the sand with 'Together your dear bodies…', he encloses the site of the gārhapatya piling with twenty-one pebbles, [reciting]: 'You are piled, you are enclosed…';

16.14.5.a.s: vrajaṃ kṛṇudhvaṃ sa hi vo nṛpāṇo varma sīvyadhvaṃ bahulā pṛthūni /
16.14.5.a.d: व्रजं कृणुध्वं स हि वो नृपाणो वर्म सीव्यध्वं बहुला पृथूनि ।
16.14.5.a.m: 'Make an enclosure, for it is your protection for men; sew armor thick and wide;

16.14.5.b.s: puraḥ kṛṇudhvamāyasīradhṛṣṭā mā vaḥ susroccamaso dṛṃhatā tamiti śarkarā abhimantryāyaṃ so agniriti catasro madhye prācīriṣṭakā gārhapatyacitāvupadadhāti
16.14.5.b.d: पुरः कृणुध्वमायसीरधृष्टा मा वः सुस्रोच्चमसो दृंहता तमिति शर्करा अभिमन्त्र्यायं सो अग्निरिति चतस्रो मध्ये प्राचीरिष्टका गार्हपत्यचितावुपदधाति
16.14.5.b.m: Make forts of iron, unassailable; let not your goblet leak, make it firm'—having addressed the pebbles with this [verse], he places four bricks facing east in the middle on the gārhapatya piling, with: 'This is that Agni…'

16.14.6.a.s: iḍāmagne 'yaṃ te yonirṛtviya iti dve purastātsamīcī tiraścī vā
16.14.6.a.d: इडामग्ने ऽयं ते योनिरृत्विय इति द्वे पुरस्तात्समीची तिरश्ची वा
16.14.6.a.m: [He places] two in front, turned toward each other or across, with: 'Refreshment, O Agni…' and 'This is your seasonal womb…'

16.14.7.a.m: In the same way [two] behind, with: 'You are piled,' and 'You are enclosed.'

16.14.8.a.m: He covers the remaining [space] with thirteen space-filler [bricks].

16.14.9.a.s: lokaṃ pṛṇa tā asya sūdadohasa iti dvābhyāṃdvābhyām mantrābhyāmekaikāṃ lokaṃpṛṇāmupadadhāti
16.14.9.a.d: लोकं पृण ता अस्य सूददोहस इति द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्याम् मन्त्राभ्यामेकैकां लोकंपृणामुपदधाति
16.14.9.a.m: He places each space-filler [brick] with two formulas each: 'Fill the space…' and 'These, his milking draughts…'

16.14.10.a.m: Over all the bricks, he continuously places [the formula]: 'By that deity…'

16.15.1.a.m: Having brought loose soil from the pit-mound, he scatters it over the piling with the Vaiśvānara verse: 'Revered in heaven…'

16.15.3.a.m: One who piles for the first time should pile [an altar] of five layers;

16.15.4.a.m: From then on, he should pile only one-layered ones.

16.15.5.a.s: ajījanannamṛtaṃ martyāsa iti gārhapatyacitimabhimṛśya samitamiti tasyāṃ catasṛbhirukhyaṃ saṃnivapati
16.15.5.a.d: अजीजनन्नमृतं मर्त्यास इति गार्हपत्यचितिमभिमृश्य समितमिति तस्यां चतसृभिरुख्यं संनिवपति
16.15.5.a.m: Having touched the gārhapatya piling with 'Mortals have begotten the immortal…', he pours out together the fire in the pan onto it with four [formulas beginning]: 'Together…'

16.15.6.a.s: vijñāyate ca vi vā etau dviṣāte yaścokhāyāṃ yaśca cīyate /
16.15.6.a.d: विज्ञायते च वि वा एतौ द्विषाते यश्चोखायां यश्च चीयते ।
16.15.6.a.m: And it is taught: 'These two surely hate each other: the one in the pan and the one that is piled.

16.15.6.c.m: When he distributes [the fire] having poured them together, he pacifies them with the holy power alone.'

16.15.7.a.s: sākaṃ hi śucinā śuciḥ praśāstā kratunājani /
16.15.7.a.d: साकं हि शुचिना शुचिः प्रशास्ता क्रतुनाजनि ।
16.15.7.a.m: 'For together with the pure one the pure ruler was born through wisdom;

16.15.7.b.s: vidvām̐ asya vratā ghruvā vayā ivānu rohata iti saṃnyuptāvabhimantrya mateva putramiti śikyādukhāṃ nirūhya yadasya pāre rajasa iti vaiśvānaryā śikyamādatte
16.15.7.b.d: विद्वाम्̐ अस्य व्रता घ्रुवा वया इवानु रोहत इति संन्युप्तावभिमन्त्र्य मतेव पुत्रमिति शिक्यादुखां निरूह्य यदस्य पारे रजस इति वैश्वानर्या शिक्यमादत्ते
16.15.7.b.m: Knowing his fixed ordinances, they grow up like branches'—having addressed the two [fires] poured together with this [verse], having removed the pan from the halter with 'Like a mother her son…', he takes the halter with the Vaiśvānara verse: 'What is on the other side of this space…'

16.15.8.a.s: nairṛtīriṣṭakāḥ kṛṣṇāstisrastuṣapakvāstāḥ śikyaṃ rukmasūtramāsandīṃ cādāya dakṣiṇamaparamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvā namaḥ su te nirṛta iti svakṛta iriṇe pradare vā śikyaṃ nidhāya tasyeṣṭakābhiḥ pāśamabhyupadadhāti
16.15.8.a.d: नैरृतीरिष्टकाः कृष्णास्तिस्रस्तुषपक्वास्ताः शिक्यं रुक्मसूत्रमासन्दीं चादाय दक्षिणमपरमवान्तरदेशं गत्वा नमः सु ते निरृत इति स्वकृत इरिणे प्रदरे वा शिक्यं निधाय तस्येष्टकाभिः पाशमभ्युपदधाति
16.15.8.a.m: Having taken the bricks of Nirṛti—three black ones, baked with chaff—as well as the sling, the gold ornament's cord, and the stool, and having gone to the south-western intermediate quarter, having placed the sling in a natural cleft or in a chasm with the verse: “Homage indeed to you, O Nirṛti,” he sets down [the bricks] upon its noose.

16.15.9.a.s: yasyāste asyāḥ krūra āsañjuhomītyetābhistisṛbhiḥ parācīrasaṃspṛṣṭā dakṣiṇāpavargam
16.15.9.a.d: यस्यास्ते अस्याः क्रूर आसञ्जुहोमीत्येताभिस्तिसृभिः पराचीरसंस्पृष्टा दक्षिणापवर्गम्
16.15.9.a.m: With these three [formulas]: “In whose cruel mouth I sacrifice...”, [he sets down the bricks] facing away, touching each other, ending towards the south.

16.16.1.a.s: yatte devī nirṛtirābabandheti śikyajālenaināḥ pracchādya rukmasūtramāsandīṃ ca parastānnidhāyāpāsmadetu nirṛtirnehāsyā api kiṃcana /
16.16.1.a.d: यत्ते देवी निरृतिराबबन्धेति शिक्यजालेनैनाः प्रच्छाद्य रुक्मसूत्रमासन्दीं च परस्तान्निधायापास्मदेतु निरृतिर्नेहास्या अपि किंचन ।
16.16.1.a.m: Having covered them with the netting of the sling with: “What the goddess Nirṛti has bound...”, and having placed the gold ornament's cord and the stool beyond, [with the verses]: “May Nirṛti go away from us; may not even a little of her remain here;

16.16.1.b.m: Lack of cattle, destruction, evil—all that we drive away.

16.16.1.c.m: Away from us the nooses of Nirṛti, and the hundred and one deaths, which [she brings],

16.16.1.d.s: apāsya ye sināḥ pāśā mṛtyūnekaśataṃ suve //
16.16.1.d.d: अपास्य ये सिनाः पाशा मृत्यूनेकशतं सुवे ॥
16.16.1.d.m: Away from him whatever binding nooses, the hundred and one deaths, I dispel.

16.16.1.e.s: ye te pāśā ekaśataṃ mṛtyo martyāya hantave /
16.16.1.e.d: ये ते पाशा एकशतं मृत्यो मर्त्याय हन्तवे ।
16.16.1.e.m: Whatever hundred and one nooses are yours, O Death, to kill mortal man,

16.16.1.f.m: All of them through the power of the sacrifice we appease through sacrifice.

16.16.1.g.s: devīmahaṃ nirṛtiṃ bādhamānaḥ piteva putraṃ dasaye vacobhiḥ /
16.16.1.g.d: देवीमहं निरृतिं बाधमानः पितेव पुत्रं दसये वचोभिः ।
16.16.1.g.m: Repelling the goddess Nirṛti, as a father wearying his son with words,

16.16.1.h.s: viśvasya yā jāyamānasya veda śiraḥśiraḥ prati sūrī vicaṣṭa ityetābhiścatasṛbhirupahitā abhimantrya yadasya pāre rajasa iti vaiśvānaryā pariṣicya bhūtyai nama ityupasthāyāpratīkṣamāyanti
16.16.1.h.d: विश्वस्य या जायमानस्य वेद शिरःशिरः प्रति सूरी विचष्ट इत्येताभिश्चतसृभिरुपहिता अभिमन्त्र्य यदस्य पारे रजस इति वैश्वानर्या परिषिच्य भूत्यै नम इत्युपस्थायाप्रतीक्षमायन्ति
16.16.1.h.m: Who knows of every creature being born, wise, she surveys head by head”—having addressed [the bricks] thus placed with these four [verses], having poured water around with the Vaiśvānara verse: “What is on the other side of this space...”, having reverenced them with: “Homage to prosperity,” they return without looking back.

16.16.2.a.m: “For the concealment of Nirṛti,” so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

16.16.3.a.m: They cleanse themselves with water with: “May the divine waters be for our welfare...”

16.16.4.a.s: ūrjaṃ bibhradvasumanāḥ sumedhā gṛhānaimi manasā modamānaḥ suvarcāḥ /
16.16.4.a.d: ऊर्जं बिभ्रद्वसुमनाः सुमेधा गृहानैमि मनसा मोदमानः सुवर्चाः ।
16.16.4.a.m: “Bearing nourishment, well-minded, wise, of goodly splendor, I enter the house, rejoicing in mind;

16.16.4.b.s: aghoreṇa cakṣuṣāhaṃ śivena gṛhāṇāṃ paśyanvaya uttirāṇi //
16.16.4.b.d: अघोरेण चक्षुषाहं शिवेन गृहाणां पश्यन्वय उत्तिराणि ॥
16.16.4.b.m: With an unfeared, auspicious eye, looking at the houses, may I prolong life.

16.16.4.c.s: gṛhāṇāmāyuḥ pra vayaṃ tirāmo gṛhā asmākaṃ pra tirantvāyuḥ /
16.16.4.c.d: गृहाणामायुः प्र वयं तिरामो गृहा अस्माकं प्र तिरन्त्वायुः ।
16.16.4.c.m: We prolong the life of the houses; may the houses prolong our life;

16.16.4.d.s: gṝnahaṃ sumanasaḥ prapadye 'vīraghno vīravataḥ suvīrāniti gṛhānabheti
16.16.4.d.d: गॄनहं सुमनसः प्रपद्ये ऽवीरघ्नो वीरवतः सुवीरानिति गृहानभेति
16.16.4.d.m: I enter the houses, well-disposed, not slaying our men, full of heroes, possessed of noble men”—with this [verse] he approaches the houses.

16.16.5.a.m: They worship the āhavanīya or the gārhapatya with: “The resting place, the assembler of wealth...”

16.17.1.a.m: He undertakes the rite beginning with the measuring out of the king [Soma].

16.17.2.a.m: Having performed the prāyaṇīyā offering, he measures out the altar ground.

16.17.3.a.m: “Having released speech with [the call to] the maker of the oblation,” according to the Vājasaneyaka.

16.17.4.a.m: He undertakes the rite beginning with taking [ghee] from the dhruvā ladle for the prāyaṇīyā.

16.17.5.a.m: Having performed the ātithyā offering, he measures out the fire [altar].

16.17.6.a.m: “Having released speech with [the call to] the maker of the oblation,” according to the Vājasaneyaka.

16.17.7.a.s: samūlaṃ haritaṃ darbhastambamāhṛtya madhye 'gnernikhāya juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sajūrabdo 'yāvabhiriti darbhastambe pañcāhutīrjuhoti
16.17.7.a.d: समूलं हरितं दर्भस्तम्बमाहृत्य मध्ये ऽग्नेर्निखाय जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा सजूरब्दो ऽयावभिरिति दर्भस्तम्बे पञ्चाहुतीर्जुहोति
16.17.7.a.m: Having brought a green clump of darbha grass along with its roots, having buried it in the middle of the fire [altar], having taken five ladlings into the juhū ladle, he offers five oblations on the clump of darbha grass with: “The year in union with the unassailable...”

16.17.8.a.m: He measures out the fire [altar] with a bamboo rod as long as the sacrificer with his arms raised upward:

16.17.9.a.m: Three [bamboo rods] to the east, four to the north.

16.17.10.a.m: The wings and the tail are one puruṣa in size [each].

16.17.12.a.m: He lengthens the right wing to the south by a cubit.

16.17.14.a.m: The tail to the west by a span or a vitasti.

16.17.15.a.m: The first fire [altar] has a single measure [of one puruṣa];

16.17.15.d.m: They rise in this manner up to one of a hundred and one measures.

16.17.16.a.s: tadu ha vai saptavidhameva cinvīta saptavidho vāva prākṛto 'gnistata ūrdhvamekottarāniti vājasaneyakam
16.17.16.a.d: तदु ह वै सप्तविधमेव चिन्वीत सप्तविधो वाव प्राकृतो ऽग्निस्तत ऊर्ध्वमेकोत्तरानिति वाजसनेयकम्
16.17.16.a.m: “Now, he should build only a sevenfold one; indeed the basic fire [altar] is sevenfold; beyond that, they increase by one,” according to the Vājasaneyaka.

16.17.17.a.m: “Be pleasant, O earth, thornless, a resting place;

16.17.17.c.m: With these two verses: [“Be pleasant, O earth...” and] “Truly of the mountains...”, they step upon the measured fire [altar ground].

16.18.1.a.m: He issues the call: “Fasten the straps together!”

16.18.2.a.m: With: “The pit whose trough is prepared...”, he pours water from the pit into the troughs.

16.18.3.a.m: They water the oxen at them.

16.18.4.a.m: “The yoking-loop, the inner pole-pin, the shaft, the axle-peg, the hoof,

16.18.4.b.s: aṣṭrāṃ tālaṃ pratīnāhamubhe maṇḍūkyau yujāviti yugalāṅgalaṃ saṃprasārayati
16.18.4.b.d: अष्ट्रां तालं प्रतीनाहमुभे मण्डूक्यौ युजाविति युगलाङ्गलं संप्रसारयति
16.18.4.b.m: The goad, the palm, the outer band, both frog-pieces joined together”—with this formula, he lays out the yoke and the plough.

16.18.5.a.s: sīrā yuñjantīti dvābhyāṃ sīraṃ yunakti ṣaḍgavaṃ dvādaśagavaṃ caturviṃśatigavaṃ vā
16.18.5.a.d: सीरा युञ्जन्तीति द्वाभ्यां सीरं युनक्ति षड्गवं द्वादशगवं चतुर्विंशतिगवं वा
16.18.5.a.m: With the two verses: “They yoke the ploughs...”, he yokes the plough with a team of six oxen, twelve oxen, or twenty-four oxen.

16.18.6.a.m: “Of the two draft-oxen, of the two quick ones, and of the two to be bound,

16.18.6.b.s: sarveṣāṃ vidma vo nāma vāhāḥ kīlālapeśasa iti yuktānabhimantryodasthādhojiddhanajidaśvajiddhiraṇyajitsūnṛtayā parīvṛtaḥ /
16.18.6.b.d: सर्वेषां विद्म वो नाम वाहाः कीलालपेशस इति युक्तानभिमन्त्र्योदस्थाधोजिद्धनजिदश्वजिद्धिरण्यजित्सूनृतया परीवृतः ।
16.18.6.b.m: We know the name of all of you, draft-animals adorned with drink”—having addressed the yoked [oxen] with this verse, [and then reciting]: “The winner of food, winner of wealth, winner of horses, winner of gold has arisen, encompassed by gracious speech;

16.18.6.c.s: ekacakreṇa savitā rathenorjo bhāgaṃ pṛthivīmetvāpṛṇanniti lāṅgalamucchrayati
16.18.6.c.d: एकचक्रेण सविता रथेनोर्जो भागं पृथिवीमेत्वापृणन्निति लाङ्गलमुच्छ्रयति
16.18.6.c.m: May Savitṛ with his one-wheeled chariot come to the earth, filling the portion of nourishment”—he raises the plough.

16.18.7.a.m: This is [the verse]: “The prayer born first...”

16.18.7.b.s: anāptā yā vaḥ prathamā yasyāṃ karmāṇi kṛṇvate /
16.18.7.b.d: अनाप्ता या वः प्रथमा यस्यां कर्माणि कृण्वते ।
16.18.7.b.m: “The first [abode] of yours that is unreached, upon which they perform rites,

16.18.7.c.s: vīrānno atra mā dabhaṃstadva etatpuro dadhe //
16.18.7.c.d: वीरान्नो अत्र मा दभंस्तद्व एतत्पुरो दधे ॥
16.18.7.c.m: May they not harm our heroes here; this of yours I place before you.

16.18.7.d.s: paryū ṣu pra dhanva vājasātaye pari vṛtrāṇi sakṣaṇiḥ /
16.18.7.d.d: पर्यू षु प्र धन्व वाजसातये परि वृत्राणि सक्षणिः ।
16.18.7.d.m: Flow forward well for the winning of prize, overcoming the foes;

16.18.7.e.m: Like an exacter of debts to overcome the haters, you speed.

16.18.7.f.s: sahasradhāre 'va te samasvarandivo nāke madhujihvā asaścataḥ /
16.18.7.f.d: सहस्रधारे ऽव ते समस्वरन्दिवो नाके मधुजिह्वा असश्चतः ।
16.18.7.f.m: In a thousand streams they sounded down to you, honey-tongued, untiring in the vault of heaven;

16.18.7.g.s: asya spaśo na ni miṣanti bhūrṇayaḥ padepade pāśinaḥ santi setava iti brahmavarmāṇi juhoti
16.18.7.g.d: अस्य स्पशो न नि मिषन्ति भूर्णयः पदेपदे पाशिनः सन्ति सेतव इति ब्रह्मवर्माणि जुहोति
16.18.7.g.m: His watchers do not close their eyes, eager; at every step there are snare-holders, binding cords”—with these [formulas] he offers the brahmavarmā oblations.

16.18.8.a.s: malimluco nāmāsi trayodaśo māsa indrasya varmāsīndrasya śarmāsīndrasya varūthamasi taṃ tvā prapadye
16.18.8.a.d: मलिम्लुचो नामासि त्रयोदशो मास इन्द्रस्य वर्मासीन्द्रस्य शर्मासीन्द्रस्य वरूथमसि तं त्वा प्रपद्ये
16.18.8.a.m: With 'You are named the robber (Malimluca), the thirteenth month; you are Indra's armour, you are Indra's shelter, you are Indra's protection; I take refuge in you,'

16.19.1.a.m: 'I enter the gāyatrī with my body hairs;

16.19.1.b.m: I enter the triṣṭubh with my skin;

16.19.1.c.m: I enter the jagatī with my flesh;

16.19.1.d.m: I enter the anuṣṭubh with my bones;

16.19.1.e.m: I enter the paṅkti with my marrow;

16.19.1.f.s: aindrāgnaṃ varma bahulaṃ yadugraṃ viśve devā nātividhyanti sūrāḥ /
16.19.1.f.d: ऐन्द्राग्नं वर्म बहुलं यदुग्रं विश्वे देवा नातिविध्यन्ति सूराः ।
16.19.1.f.m: The armour of Indra and Agni, which is thick and formidable, which all the gods, the heroes, cannot pierce through:

16.19.1.g.s: tannastrāyatāṃ tanno viśvato mahadāyuṣmanto jarāmupagacchema devā iti vimitamagnimākrmante
16.19.1.g.d: तन्नस्त्रायतां तन्नो विश्वतो महदायुष्मन्तो जरामुपगच्छेम देवा इति विमितमग्निमाक्र्मन्ते
16.19.1.g.m: May that protect us, may that great [armour] protect us from all sides; endowed with long life, may we attain old age, O gods'—with [these formulas] they step into the measured shed of the fire.

16.19.2.a.m: With the two verses beginning 'The plough equipped with a lance…', he ploughs.

16.19.4.a.m: He ploughs from the tail to the head.

16.19.5.a.s: kāmaṃ kāmadugho dhukṣveti pradakṣiṇamāvartayaṃstisrastisraḥ sītāḥ saṃhitāḥ kṛṣati
16.19.5.a.d: कामं कामदुघो धुक्ष्वेति प्रदक्षिणमावर्तयंस्तिस्रस्तिस्रः सीताः संहिताः कृषति
16.19.5.a.m: Saying, 'Yield desire, yielding wishes,' turning in a sunwise direction, he ploughs sets of three furrows joined together.

16.19.7.a.m: From the southern wing to the northern wing;

16.19.7.c.m: From the southern hip to the northern shoulder;

16.19.8.a.m: 'Be unyoked, O unslayable cows, moving on the path of the gods; we have crossed to the other side of this darkness;

16.19.8.b.s: jyotirāpāma suvaraganmeti dakṣiṇe 'ṃsa uttare vā balīvardānvimucya tānudīcaḥ prāco votsṛjyādhvaryave dadāti
16.19.8.b.d: ज्योतिरापाम सुवरगन्मेति दक्षिणे ऽंस उत्तरे वा बलीवर्दान्विमुच्य तानुदीचः प्राचो वोत्सृज्याध्वर्यवे ददाति
16.19.8.b.m: We have attained the light, we have gone to heaven'—having unyoked the oxen at the southern or northern shoulder, having released them towards the north or the east, he gives them to the adhvaryu.

16.19.9.a.m: The Vājasaneyins prescribe a four-cornered [ploughing], not crossing in the middle, having sixteen furrows.

16.19.10.a.m: He pours out fifteen vessels of water:

16.19.10.b.m: Twelve on the ploughed [ground], three on the unploughed.

16.19.11.a.m: With the fourteen verses beginning 'The plants which were born…', he sows seeds of plants.

16.19.13.a.s: tilamāṣā vrīhiyavāḥ priyaṅgvaṇavo godhūmā veṇuśyāmākanīvārā jartilaśca gavīdhukā āraṇyajā markaṭakā vijñeyāḥ
16.19.13.a.d: तिलमाषा व्रीहियवाः प्रियङ्ग्वणवो गोधूमा वेणुश्यामाकनीवारा जर्तिलश्च गवीधुका आरण्यजा मर्कटका विज्ञेयाः
16.19.13.a.m: Sesame, black gram, rice, barley, foxtail millet, panic seed, wheat, wild panic, wild rice, wild sesame, and Coix lacryma-jobi, and wild Markaṭaka-grains are to be known [as the seeds].

16.19.14.a.s: gārmutasaptamāḥ kulatthasaptamā vā sapta grāmyāḥ kṛṣṭe /
16.19.14.a.d: गार्मुतसप्तमाः कुलत्थसप्तमा वा सप्त ग्राम्याः कृष्टे ।
16.19.14.a.m: Seven cultivated seeds, with Gārmuta as the seventh or with horsegram as the seventh, [he sows] on the ploughed ground;

16.20.1.a.m: Whichsoever plant he may not obtain, in its place he should sow barley mixed with honey;

16.20.2.a.d: उप्ता मे ऽसीति वा मनसा ध्यायेत्
16.20.2.a.m: Or he should meditate in mind: 'You are sown by me.'

16.20.3.a.m: When it is obtained, he should bind it up onto whichever firewood comes first.

16.20.4.a.m: Those trees which bear fruit—having bound them onto the firewood, he should sprinkle them.

16.20.5.a.s: mā no hiṃsījjanitā yaḥ pṛthivyā iti catasṛbhirdigbhyo loṣṭānsamasyati ye 'ntarvidhādbahirvidhamāpannā bhavanti
16.20.5.a.d: मा नो हिंसीज्जनिता यः पृथिव्या इति चतसृभिर्दिग्भ्यो लोष्टान्समस्यति ये ऽन्तर्विधाद्बहिर्विधमापन्ना भवन्ति
16.20.5.a.m: With the four verses beginning 'May he not harm us who is the creator of the earth…', he gathers from the directions the clods of earth that have fallen outside the perimeter from inside the perimeter.

16.20.6.a.s: yaṃ dviṣyādyatra sa syāttasyai diśo jaghanyaṃ loṣṭamāharediṣamūrjamahamita ādada iti
16.20.6.a.d: यं द्विष्याद्यत्र स स्यात्तस्यै दिशो जघन्यं लोष्टमाहरेदिषमूर्जमहमित आदद इति
16.20.6.a.m: Whomever he might hate, from whichever direction that man might be, from that direction he should fetch the last clod with the formula: 'Here I take sap and nourishment.'

16.20.7.a.m: With the verse 'Furrow, with ghee…', he touches the spaces between the furrows,

16.20.8.a.m: He strews the high altar to the size of the fire-altar.

16.20.9.a.s: vyāghāraṇāntāṃ kṛtvāgne tava śravo vaya iti ṣaḍbhiḥ sikatā nyupya cita stha paricita ityaparimitābhiḥ śarkarābhirāhavanīyaciterāyatanaṃ pariśrayati yathā gārhapatyasyaivam
16.20.9.a.d: व्याघारणान्तां कृत्वाग्ने तव श्रवो वय इति षड्भिः सिकता न्युप्य चित स्थ परिचित इत्यपरिमिताभिः शर्कराभिराहवनीयचितेरायतनं परिश्रयति यथा गार्हपत्यस्यैवम्
16.20.9.a.m: Having made it end with libation-streaks, having scattered sand with the six verses beginning 'O Agni, your fame, vigor…', he surrounds the seat of the āhavanīya-pile with an unlimited number of pebbles with the formula: 'You are piled, you are enclosed,' just as [was done] for the gārhapatya.

16.20.10.a.m: With three times seven [pebbles] for one desiring cattle;

16.20.10.b.m: With three times nine for one who has a rival;

16.20.10.c.m: With tens for one desiring food;

16.20.10.d.m: With an unlimited number for one who has unlimited desire.

16.20.11.a.m: For one whom he wishes should be without cattle, 'without measuring for him' has been stated.

16.20.12.a.s: āpyāyasva sametu ta iti sikatā vyūhati
16.20.12.a.d: आप्यायस्व समेतु त इति सिकता व्यूहति
16.20.12.a.m: With the verse 'Swell, let [vigor] gather to you…', he levels the sand.

16.20.13.a.m: With the subsequent triṣṭubh verse for a rājanya:

16.20.14.a.s: asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā harī rajeva dasmo abhi gā acikradat /
16.20.14.a.d: असावि सोमो अरुषो वृषा हरी रजेव दस्मो अभि गा अचिक्रदत् ।
16.20.14.a.m: 'Soma, ruddy, a bull, tawny, has been pressed out; like a king, wonder-working, he roared towards the cows;

16.20.14.b.s: punāno vāraṃ paryetyavyayaṃ śyeno na yoniṃ ghṛtavantamāsadamiti jagatyā vaiśayasya
16.20.14.b.d: पुनानो वारं पर्येत्यव्ययं श्येनो न योनिं घृतवन्तमासदमिति जगत्या वैशयस्य
16.20.14.b.m: Purifying himself, he passes through the sheep's wool filter, to sit, like an eagle, in his ghee-abounding home'—with this jagatī verse for a vaiśya.

16.21.1.a.m: Starting from 'From the steady [ladle] of the Ātithyā…', he undertakes this rite.

16.21.2.a.s: paurvāhṇikībhyāṃ pracaryāgreṇa prāgvaṃśaṃ lohite carmaṇyānaḍuhe prācīnagrīva uttaralomni prathamasyāściteriṣṭakāḥ saṃsādayati /
16.21.2.a.d: पौर्वाह्णिकीभ्यां प्रचर्याग्रेण प्राग्वंशं लोहिते चर्मण्यानडुहे प्राचीनग्रीव उत्तरलोम्नि प्रथमस्याश्चितेरिष्टकाः संसादयति ।
16.21.2.a.m: Having performed the two morning offerings, in front of the eastern hall, on a red ox-hide with the neck turned to the east and the hair side turned upwards, he places together the bricks of the first layer,

16.21.2.b.m: Or three naturally perforated bricks and three Viśvajyotis bricks.

16.21.3.a.s: tā darbhāgramuṣṭinājyena vyavokṣya samudyamya cityagnibhyaḥ praṇīyamānebhyo 'nubrūhīti saṃpreṣyati /
16.21.3.a.d: ता दर्भाग्रमुष्टिनाज्येन व्यवोक्ष्य समुद्यम्य चित्यग्निभ्यः प्रणीयमानेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहीति संप्रेष्यति ।
16.21.3.a.m:
Having sprinkled them with clarified butter with a handful of darbha tops, having lifted them up, he issues the command: 'Recite for the fires of the pile being brought forward!'

Or: 'Recite for [the fires] being brought forward!'

16.21.4.a.s: prathamāyāṃ triranūktāyāṃ hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti prāñco 'śvaprathamā abhipravrajanti
16.21.4.a.d: प्रथमायां त्रिरनूक्तायां हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति प्राञ्चो ऽश्वप्रथमा अभिप्रव्रजन्ति
16.21.4.a.m: When the first [verse] has been recited three times, with the verse 'The golden embryo arose in the beginning…', they advance towards the east, led by a horse.

16.21.5.a.m: They lead a white horse in front.

16.21.6.a.s: prajāpatistvā sādayatu tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdetyuttaravedimabhimṛśya mayi gṛhṇāmyagre agniṃ yo no agniḥ pitara iti dvābhyāmātmannagniṃ gṛhītvā yāste agne samidha iti svayaṃcityābhimṛśati
16.21.6.a.d: प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेत्युत्तरवेदिमभिमृश्य मयि गृह्णाम्यग्रे अग्निं यो नो अग्निः पितर इति द्वाभ्यामात्मन्नग्निं गृहीत्वा यास्ते अग्ने समिध इति स्वयंचित्याभिमृशति
16.21.6.a.m: Having touched the high altar with 'May Prajāpati seat you; by that deity, firm in the manner of the Aṅgirases, sit firm,' having taken the fire into himself with the two verses 'I take Agni into myself in the beginning…' and 'The fire which is our fathers'…', he touches [the bricks] with the Svayaṃciti formula: 'Whatever firewood is yours, O Agni…'

16.21.7.a.m: The adhvaryu or the sacrificer piles the fire with the bricks.

16.21.8.a.m: Piling it himself, he does not take the fire into himself nor does he touch it with the Svayaṃciti formula.

16.21.9.a.m: 'He places [them] facing east, he places [them] facing west' refers to the lines of bricks in groups.

16.21.10.a.m: 'He places [it] facing east, he places [it] facing west' refers to the face of the performer.

16.21.11.a.m: The white horse stands to the south.

16.21.12.a.s: tamālabhyendraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhannityuttareṇa pucchāpyayamantarvidha ākramaṇaṃ pratīṣṭakāmupadadhyāt
16.21.12.a.d: तमालभ्येन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्नित्युत्तरेण पुच्छाप्ययमन्तर्विध आक्रमणं प्रतीष्टकामुपदध्यात्
16.21.12.a.m: Having touched it, with the verse: “All songs have magnified Indra...”, he should set down a brick to face the approach to the north of the tail's junction, within the measurement [of the altar].

16.21.13.a.m: The approach to the fire [altar] is from the north or from the west.

16.21.14.a.m: Every time he ascends and descends, he mutters: “Speech in my mouth...”;

16.22.1.a.s: tattvā yāmi brahmaṇā vandamāna iti śālāmukhīye hutvā prāñcamaśvamabhyasthādviśvā iti dakṣiṇena padā darbhastambamākramayya pradakṣiṇamāvartayitvā yadakranda iti punarevākramayati
16.22.1.a.d: तत्त्वा यामि ब्रह्मणा वन्दमान इति शालामुखीये हुत्वा प्राञ्चमश्वमभ्यस्थाद्विश्वा इति दक्षिणेन पदा दर्भस्तम्बमाक्रमय्य प्रदक्षिणमावर्तयित्वा यदक्रन्द इति पुनरेवाक्रमयति
16.22.1.a.m: Having offered [a libation] in the śālāmukhīya fire with, 'Seeking that, I approach you with a prayer…', having made the horse, facing east, step with its right foot upon a bunch of darbha grass with, 'He has overcome all [adversaries]…', and having made it turn clockwise, he makes it step again with, 'When you first whinnied…'.

16.22.2.a.s: apāṃ pṛṣṭhamasītyaśvasya pade puṣkaraparṇamuttānamupadhāyāpāṃ nidhiṃ gāyeti saṃpreṣyati
16.22.2.a.d: अपां पृष्ठमसीत्यश्वस्य पदे पुष्करपर्णमुत्तानमुपधायापां निधिं गायेति संप्रेष्यति
16.22.2.a.m: Having laid down a lotus leaf turned upwards in the footprint of the horse with, 'You are the back of the waters…', he gives the ritual call: 'Sing the Apāṃ nidhi chant!'

16.22.3.a.s: brahma jajñānamiti puṣkaraparṇa upariṣṭānnirbādhaṃ rukmamupadhāya hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti tasminhiraṇmayaṃ puruṣaṃ prācīnamuttānaṃ dakṣiṇenātṛṇaṃ prāṅmukha upadhāya puruṣasāma gāyeti saṃpreṣyati
16.22.3.a.d: ब्रह्म जज्ञानमिति पुष्करपर्ण उपरिष्टान्निर्बाधं रुक्ममुपधाय हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति तस्मिन्हिरण्मयं पुरुषं प्राचीनमुत्तानं दक्षिणेनातृणं प्राङ्मुख उपधाय पुरुषसाम गायेति संप्रेष्यति
16.22.3.a.m: Having laid a golden disk with protruding points upon the lotus leaf with, 'The prayer born first…', and facing east, having laid upon it a golden man facing east, turned upwards, south of the naturally perforated brick with, 'The Golden Embryo arose in the beginning…', he gives the ritual call: 'Sing the Puruṣasāma chant!'

16.22.4.a.s: drapsaścaskandeti puruṣamabhimṛśya namo astu sarpebhya iti tisṛbhirabhimantrya kṛṇuṣva pāja iti pañcabhiruttaravedivatpuruṣaṃ vyāghārya srucāvupadadhātītyuktam
16.22.4.a.d: द्रप्सश्चस्कन्देति पुरुषमभिमृश्य नमो अस्तु सर्पेभ्य इति तिसृभिरभिमन्त्र्य कृणुष्व पाज इति पञ्चभिरुत्तरवेदिवत्पुरुषं व्याघार्य स्रुचावुपदधातीत्युक्तम्
16.22.4.a.m: Having touched the man with, 'The drop has fallen…', and having consecrated him with the three [verses], 'Homage be to the serpents…', and having anointed the man with ghee like the uttaravedī with the five [verses], 'Put forth your power…', he lays down the two ladles—this has been taught.

16.22.5.a.s: api vāgnestvā tejasā sādayāmītyājyasya pūrṇāṃ kārṣmaryamayīṃ dakṣiṇena puruṣam /
16.22.5.a.d: अपि वाग्नेस्त्वा तेजसा सादयामीत्याज्यस्य पूर्णां कार्ष्मर्यमयीं दक्षिणेन पुरुषम् ।
16.22.5.a.m: Or rather, [he lays down] the one made of kārṣmarya wood, full of clarified butter, to the south of the man with, 'With the splendour of Agni I set you down…';

16.22.5.b.s: indrasya tvaujasā sādayāmīti dadhnaḥ pūrṇāmaudumbarīmuttareṇa puruṣam
16.22.5.b.d: इन्द्रस्य त्वौजसा सादयामीति दध्नः पूर्णामौदुम्बरीमुत्तरेण पुरुषम्
16.22.5.b.m: the one made of udumbara wood, full of curd, to the north of the man with, 'With the power of Indra I set you down…'.

16.22.6.a.m: He attends upon the one made of kārṣmarya wood with, 'Agni is the head…';

16.22.6.b.m: upon the one made of udumbara wood with, 'You are the [protector] of the sacrifice…'.

16.22.7.a.m: Some say: he lays them down with the two verses containing the word mūrdhan, and attends upon them with the two yajus formulas.

16.22.8.a.m: Here, having anointed the golden disk as [he did] the man,

16.23.1.a.s: dhruvāsi dharuṇāstṛteti svayamatṛṇāmabhimṛśyāśvenopaghrāpya prajāpatistvā sādayatu pṛthivyāḥ pṛṣṭha ityaviduṣā brāhmaṇena saha madhye 'gnerupadadhāti /
16.23.1.a.d: ध्रुवासि धरुणास्तृतेति स्वयमतृणामभिमृश्याश्वेनोपघ्राप्य प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु पृथिव्याः पृष्ठ इत्यविदुषा ब्राह्मणेन सह मध्ये ऽग्नेरुपदधाति ।
16.23.1.a.m: having touched the naturally perforated brick with, 'You are firm, a foundation, spread out…', having made the horse smell it, he lays it down in the middle of the fire altar together with an unlearned brahmin with, 'May Prajāpati set you down on the back of the earth…'

16.23.2.a.m: Having offered in the naturally perforated brick with, 'I offer consciousness…', he breathes out.

16.23.3.a.m: He gives a choice gift—one, two, or three—to the unlearned brahmin.

16.23.4.a.m: Seated, he lays down the first naturally perforated brick;

16.23.5.a.m: He gives the ritual call: 'Sing a chant upon the naturally perforated brick!'

16.23.6.a.m: In the same manner, having laid down the second and the third, he gives the ritual call.

16.23.7.a.s: yadi manyeta yajamānaḥ pūrvo mātikrānto bhrātṛvya iti pratho 'sītyupahitāṃ prācīmudūhet /
16.23.7.a.d: यदि मन्येत यजमानः पूर्वो मातिक्रान्तो भ्रातृव्य इति प्रथो ऽसीत्युपहितां प्राचीमुदूहेत् ।
16.23.7.a.m: If the sacrificer should think, 'My rival has preceded me,' he should push forward towards the east the laid brick with, 'You are broad…';

16.23.7.b.m: or if [he should think], 'He is behind,' [he should push it] towards the west with, 'You are the earth…';

16.23.7.c.m: if [he should think], 'He is equal to me,' he should shake it with, 'You are being, you are creation…'.

16.23.8.a.d: तेजो ऽसि तेजो मे यच्छेति हिरण्येष्टकाम्
16.23.8.a.m: [He lays down] the gold-brick with, 'You are radiance, bestow radiance upon me…';

16.23.9.a.m: the round brick with, 'The earth [as a stronghold] of water, with food…'.

16.23.10.a.m: 'You are being, the seed of creation.

16.23.10.d.m: Agni is light, light is Agni.

16.23.10.e.m: With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm!'

16.23.10.f.m: 'You are the sun, the seed of generation.

16.23.10.i.m: Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya.

16.23.10.j.m: With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm!'—[with these] two ascending bricks [are laid].

16.24.1.a.s: kāṇḍātkāṇḍātprarohantīti dvābhyāṃ dūrveṣṭakāṃ saloṣṭaṃ haritaṃ dūrvāstambamapracchinnāgraṃ yathāsyopahitasya svayamātṛṇāyāmagraṃ prāpnuyāditi
16.24.1.a.d: काण्डात्काण्डात्प्ररोहन्तीति द्वाभ्यां दूर्वेष्टकां सलोष्टं हरितं दूर्वास्तम्बमप्रच्छिन्नाग्रं यथास्योपहितस्य स्वयमातृणायामग्रं प्राप्नुयादिति
16.24.1.a.m: With the two [verses], 'Sprouting shoot from shoot…', [he lays down] the dūrvā-brick: a green clump of dūrvā grass with its clod of earth, its tip uncut, in such a way that its tip reaches the naturally perforated brick when laid down.

16.24.2.a.s: prabāhugiṣṭakāyāṃ hiraṇyaśakalāvadhyūhya yāste agne sūrye ruca iti dvābhyāṃ vāmabhṛtam
16.24.2.a.d: प्रबाहुगिष्टकायां हिरण्यशकलावध्यूह्य यास्ते अग्ने सूर्ये रुच इति द्वाभ्यां वामभृतम्
16.24.2.a.m: Having placed two chips of gold facing outwards on the brick, [he lays down] the vāmabhṛt brick with the two [verses], 'The lights that are yours, O Agni, in the sun…'.

16.24.3.a.m: [He lays down] the three retaḥsic bricks with, 'The shining ruler is light…'.

16.24.4.a.s: tāsāṃ dve prathamāyāṃ cityāṃ yūna upadadhyāt /
16.24.4.a.d: तासां द्वे प्रथमायां चित्यां यून उपदध्यात् ।
16.24.4.a.m: Of these, he should lay down two in the first layer for a young man;

16.24.4.b.m: all of them in the middle layer for a middle-aged man;

16.24.4.c.m: one in the first layer and one in the top layer for an old man.

16.24.5.a.m: He should lay down either of them for one who is hated.

16.24.6.a.m: He lays down this one and that one with a yajus formula;

16.24.7.a.s: bṛhaspatistvā sādayatu pṛthivyāḥ pṛṣṭhe jyotiṣmatīmiti viśvajyotiṣam
16.24.7.a.d: बृहस्पतिस्त्वा सादयतु पृथिव्याः पृष्ठे ज्योतिष्मतीमिति विश्वज्योतिषम्
16.24.7.a.m: [He lays down] the viśvajyotis brick with, 'May Bṛhaspati set you down, full of light, on the back of the earth…'.

16.24.8.a.m: [He lays down] the two saṃyānī bricks with, 'You are the chariot of Agni…'.

16.24.9.a.m: [He lays down] the two seasonal bricks, having the same deity formula, with, 'Madhu and Mādhava…'.

16.24.10.a.m: Along with all the seasonal bricks, he lays down avakā plants.

16.24.11.a.m: Some say: he sets them down on avakā plants.

16.24.12.a.m: With the two [verses], 'You are the unconquered…', [he lays down] the aṣāḍhā brick, with its mark on top.

16.24.13.a.m: For one whom he desires to be wealthier, it has its mark on top—so it has been said.

16.24.14.a.m: Having laid down the gharma-brick, [he lays down] the kulāyinī brick.

16.24.15.a.m: The two mantras for these two are in the Pravargya.

16.25.1.a.s: madhu vātā ṛtāyata iti tisṛbhirdadhnā madhumiśreṇa kūrmamabhyajya mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti purastātsvayamātṛṇāyāḥ pratyañcaṃ jīvantaṃ prāṅmukha upadadhāti
16.25.1.a.d: मधु वाता ऋतायत इति तिसृभिर्दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण कूर्ममभ्यज्य मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति पुरस्तात्स्वयमातृणायाः प्रत्यञ्चं जीवन्तं प्राङ्मुख उपदधाति
16.25.1.a.m: Having smeared a tortoise with curd mixed with honey with the three [verses], 'The winds blow honey for the righteous…', and facing east, he lays it down alive to the east of the naturally perforated brick, facing west, with, 'Wide heaven and earth [protect] us…'.

16.25.2.a.s: catasra āśāḥ pracarantvagnaya iti vopadhāyāvakābhiḥ parītaṃsya jālena pracchādya śaṅkubhiḥ pariṇihatyāpāṃ gambhīraṃ gaccha mā tvā sūryaḥ parītāpsīnmo agnirvaiśvānaraḥ /
16.25.2.a.d: चतस्र आशाः प्रचरन्त्वग्नय इति वोपधायावकाभिः परीतंस्य जालेन प्रच्छाद्य शङ्कुभिः परिणिहत्यापां गम्भीरं गच्छ मा त्वा सूर्यः परीताप्सीन्मो अग्निर्वैश्वानरः ।
16.25.2.a.m: Or having laid it down with, 'May the fires move along the four quarters…', having surrounded it with avakā plants, covered it with a net, and fastened it around with pegs, [he addresses it with:] 'Go into the deep of the waters; may Sūrya not scorch you, nor Agni Vaiśvānara;

16.25.2.b.s: aghoraḥ prajā abhivipaśyānu tvā divyā vṛṣṭiḥ sacatām //
16.25.2.b.d: अघोरः प्रजा अभिविपश्यानु त्वा दिव्या वृष्टिः सचताम् ॥
16.25.2.b.m: not terrible, look upon the creatures; may heavenly rain follow you!

16.25.2.c.m: Glide through the three oceans, the heavenly worlds, the lord of waters, the bull among the bricks!

16.25.2.d.s: tatra gaccha yatra pūrve paretāḥ purīṣaṃ vasānaḥ svāṃ yoniṃ yathāyathamityupahitamabhimantrayate
16.25.2.d.d: तत्र गच्छ यत्र पूर्वे परेताः पुरीषं वसानः स्वां योनिं यथायथमित्युपहितमभिमन्त्रयते
16.25.2.d.m: Go thither where the ancients have passed away, wearing loose soil, to your proper place of origin.'—thus he addresses [the tortoise] once laid down.

16.26.1.a.m: 'Since you, O mortar, are employed in house after house,

16.26.1.b.s: iha dyumattamaṃ vada jayatāmiva dundubhiriti prādeśamātraṃ catuḥsraktyaudumbaramulūkhalamuttare 'ṃse prayunakti
16.26.1.b.d: इह द्युमत्तमं वद जयतामिव दुन्दुभिरिति प्रादेशमात्रं चतुःस्रक्त्यौदुम्बरमुलूखलमुत्तरे ऽंसे प्रयुनक्ति
16.26.1.b.m: sound here most splendidly like the drum of victors'—with [this verse] he places a mortar of udumbara wood, a span in size and four-cornered, in the northern shoulder [of the altar].

16.26.3.a.s: uta sma te vanaspate vāto vi vātyagramit /
16.26.3.a.d: उत स्म ते वनस्पते वातो वि वात्यग्रमित् ।
16.26.3.a.m: “And surely, O tree, the wind blows upon your crown;

16.26.3.b.s: atho indrāya pātave sunu somamulūkhaleti sarvauṣadhasya pūrayitvāvahatyedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama iti madhye 'gnerupadadhāti
16.26.3.b.d: अथो इन्द्राय पातवे सुनु सोममुलूखलेति सर्वौषधस्य पूरयित्वावहत्येदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इति मध्ये ऽग्नेरुपदधाति
16.26.3.b.m: then press Soma for Indra to drink, O mortar!”—having filled [the mortar] with all herbs and pounded them, with “Here Viṣṇu strode,” he places it in the middle of the fire [site].

16.26.4.a.m: With “That highest step of Viṣṇu,” [he places] the pestle.

16.26.5.a.m: With “From heaven or, O Viṣṇu,” [he places] the winnowing basket.

16.26.6.a.m: “Sewn by the two [hands], with immortality she has come; the ukhā-pot has mounted her sister upon the altar ground.

16.26.6.b.s: satyaṃ pūrvairṛṣibhiścākupāno 'gniḥ pravidvāniha tatkarotviti ghṛtenokhāṃ pūrayati /
16.26.6.b.d: सत्यं पूर्वैरृषिभिश्चाकुपानो ऽग्निः प्रविद्वानिह तत्करोत्विति घृतेनोखां पूरयति ।
16.26.6.b.m: Finding truth through the ancient seers, may Agni, knowing well, accomplish it here,”—with this he fills the ukhā-pot with ghee;

16.26.6.c.m: or with curd, with honey, or with sand, or with all of them.

16.26.7.a.m: Having poured it in, he should not look into it when empty;

16.26.9.a.m: Some teachers teach that it is filled after having poured [the milk] down.

16.26.10.a.m: “He whom he might wish, ‘May he become hungry,’ for him deficient [filling]”—thus it has been declared.

16.26.11.a.m: With “You are the firm earth,” he places [the ukhā-pot] in the middle of the fire [site].

16.26.12.a.s: pṛthivi pṛthivyāṃ sīda mātā mātari mātā syonā syonāyāmukhāṃ svasāramadhi vedimasthāt /
16.26.12.a.d: पृथिवि पृथिव्यां सीद माता मातरि माता स्योना स्योनायामुखां स्वसारमधि वेदिमस्थात् ।
16.26.12.a.m: “O earth, sit upon the earth, mother upon mother, mother, gentle upon the gentle; the ukhā-pot has mounted her sister upon the altar ground.

16.26.12.b.s: satyaṃ pūrvairṛṣibhiścākupāno 'gniḥ pravidvāniha taddadhātviti volūkhalmupadadhātīti vājasaneyakam
16.26.12.b.d: सत्यं पूर्वैरृषिभिश्चाकुपानो ऽग्निः प्रविद्वानिह तद्दधात्विति वोलूखल्मुपदधातीति वाजसनेयकम्
16.26.12.b.m: Finding truth through the ancient seers, may Agni, knowing well, place it here,”—or he places the mortar [with this formula]; thus the Vājasaneyaka [holds].

16.26.13.a.s: agne yukṣvā hi ye tava yukṣvā hi devahūtamāniti dvābhyāmukhāyāṃ hutvā puruṣaśirasi hiraṇyaśalkānpratyasyati
16.26.13.a.d: अग्ने युक्ष्वा हि ये तव युक्ष्वा हि देवहूतमानिति द्वाभ्यामुखायां हुत्वा पुरुषशिरसि हिरण्यशल्कान्प्रत्यस्यति
16.26.13.a.m: Having made an offering into the ukhā-pot with the two [formulas], “Agni, yoke indeed those that are yours,” [and] “Yoke indeed those most invoking the gods,” he throws gold chips into the human head.

16.27.1.a.m: With “The drop fell,” [he throws one] into the mouth;

16.27.1.b.m: or with “This has become of the entire world.”

16.27.2.a.m: With “To the ṛc, you,” [he throws one] into the right eye-socket;

16.27.4.a.m: with “To the brilliance, you,” into the right nostril;

16.27.4.b.m: with “To the light, you,” into the northern [i.e., left] one.

16.27.5.a.s: samitsravantīti śṛtātaṅkyena dadhnā madhumiśreṇa puruṣaśiraḥ pūrayati
16.27.5.a.d: समित्स्रवन्तीति शृतातङ्क्येन दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण पुरुषशिरः पूरयति
16.27.5.a.m: With “The firewood sticks flowing,” he fills the human head with curd that has been coagulated with boiled [milk] and mixed with honey.

16.27.6.a.s: sarveṣāṃ paśuśirasāṃ pūraṇaṃ ca vājasaneyinaḥ samāmananti
16.27.6.a.d: सर्वेषां पशुशिरसां पूरणं च वाजसनेयिनः समामनन्ति
16.27.6.a.m: And the Vājasaneyins teach the filling of all the animal heads.

16.27.7.a.s: tasmintsuparṇo madhukṛtkulāyīti puruṣaśira ādāyādityaṃ garbhamityukhāyāṃ purastāccubukaṃ prācīnamuttānaṃ prāṅmukha upadhāya citraṃ devānāmityardharcābhyāmakṣikaṭayorhutvā paśuśīrṣāṇyupadadhāti
16.27.7.a.d: तस्मिन्त्सुपर्णो मधुकृत्कुलायीति पुरुषशिर आदायादित्यं गर्भमित्युखायां पुरस्ताच्चुबुकं प्राचीनमुत्तानं प्राङ्मुख उपधाय चित्रं देवानामित्यर्धर्चाभ्यामक्षिकटयोर्हुत्वा पशुशीर्षाण्युपदधाति
16.27.7.a.m: Taking the human head with “In it the well-winged maker of honey has its nest,” and having set it down in the ukhā-pot facing east, chin to the front, face upwards, facing east with “The sun, the embryo,” having made an offering into the two eye-sockets with the two half-verses of “The bright [face] of the gods,” he places the animal heads.

16.27.8.a.m: “He whom he might wish, ‘May he be without cattle,’ for him [turned] away in opposite directions”—thus it has been declared.

16.27.9.a.m: With “The rush of the wind,” [he places the head] of the horse to the east, turned westward.

16.27.10.a.m: With “The unceasing drop,” [he places that] of the bull to the west, turned eastward.

16.27.11.a.m: With “The female protector of Tvaṣṭṛ,” [he places that] of the ram to the south, turned northward.

16.27.12.a.m: With “Which fire among the fires,” [he places that] of the he-goat to the north, [turned] southward.

16.27.13.a.m: He attends upon them without interruption with the dismissal [formulas].

16.27.14.a.m: With “Do not harm this two-footed one,” [he attends upon the head] of the human.

16.27.15.a.m: With “Do not harm this single-hoofed one,” [that] of the horse.

16.27.17.a.m: With “This woolly one,” [that] of the ram.

16.27.18.a.m: With “For the she-goat is Agni's,” [that] of the he-goat.

16.27.19.a.s: yadi vāyavyasya syānmukhyasya sthāne sarveṣāmupadhānairupadhāya sarveṣāmutsargairupatiṣṭheta
16.27.19.a.d: यदि वायव्यस्य स्यान्मुख्यस्य स्थाने सर्वेषामुपधानैरुपधाय सर्वेषामुत्सर्गैरुपतिष्ठेत
16.27.19.a.m: If [the animal sacrifice] belongs to Vāyu, having placed [the other heads] in the place of the chief one with the placing [formulas] of all, he should attend upon [them] with the dismissal [formulas] of all;

16.27.20.a.s: api vā tasyatasya sthāna upadhāya tasyatasyotsargeṇopatiṣthate
16.27.20.a.d: अपि वा तस्यतस्य स्थान उपधाय तस्यतस्योत्सर्गेणोपतिष्थते
16.27.20.a.m: or having placed each in its respective place, he attends upon it with its respective dismissal [formula].

16.27.21.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta kanīyo 'syānnaṃ syāditi saṃtarāṃ tasyetyuktam
16.27.21.a.d: यं कामयेत कनीयो ऽस्यान्नं स्यादिति संतरां तस्येत्युक्तम्
16.27.21.a.m: “He whom he might wish, ‘May food be smaller for him,’ for him [placed] more closely together”—thus it has been declared.

16.27.22.a.s: nomo astu sarpebhya iti dakṣiṇe 'ṃse sarpaśira upadadhyādviṣūcīnaṃ paśuśīrṣaiḥ
16.27.22.a.d: नोमो अस्तु सर्पेभ्य इति दक्षिणे ऽंसे सर्पशिर उपदध्याद्विषूचीनं पशुशीर्षैः
16.27.22.a.m: With “Homage be to the snakes,” he should place a snake head in the southern corner, facing away from the animal heads.

16.27.23.a.m: Or he may only utter the yajus-formula and not place [it].

16.28.1.a.s: mā chandastatpṛthivyagnirdevatā tenarṣiṇā tena brahmaṇā tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīda /
16.28.1.a.d: मा छन्दस्तत्पृथिव्यग्निर्देवता तेनर्षिणा तेन ब्रह्मणा तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीद ।
16.28.1.a.m: “Mā is the metre; that is the earth; Agni is the deity; with that seer, with that sacred word, with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

16.28.1.b.m: Pramā is the metre; that is the atmosphere; Vāta is the deity.

16.28.1.c.m: Pratimā is the metre; that is the sky; Sūrya is the deity.

16.28.1.d.m: Asrīviṣ is the metre; that is the directions; Soma is the deity.

16.28.1.e.m: Virāj is the metre; that is speech; Varuṇa is the deity.

16.28.1.f.m: Gāyatrī is the metre; that is the she-goat; Bṛhaspati is the deity.

16.28.1.g.m: Triṣṭubh is the metre; that is gold; Indra is the deity.

16.28.1.h.m: Jagatī is the metre; that is the cow; Prajāpati is the deity.

16.28.1.i.m: Anuṣṭubh is the metre; that is the wind; Mitra is the deity.

16.28.1.j.m: Uṣṇih is the metre; that is the eye; Pūṣan is the deity.

16.28.1.k.m: Paṅkti is the metre; that is agriculture; Parjanya is the deity.

16.28.1.l.s: bṛhatī chandastadaśvaḥ parameṣṭhī devatā tenarṣiṇā tena brahmaṇā tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdetyetābhirdvādaśabhistrirabhyāsaṃ purastātpratīcīṃ puruṣātkṛtiṃ cinoti
16.28.1.l.d: बृहती छन्दस्तदश्वः परमेष्ठी देवता तेनर्षिणा तेन ब्रह्मणा तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेत्येताभिर्द्वादशभिस्त्रिरभ्यासं पुरस्तात्प्रतीचीं पुरुषात्कृतिं चिनोति
16.28.1.l.m: Bṛhatī is the metre; that is the horse; Parameṣṭhin is the deity; with that seer, with that sacred word, with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras,”—with these twelve [formulas], recited three times, he piles a human-shaped [layer] from the east turned towards the west.

16.28.2.a.m: The human head becomes its head.

16.28.3.a.s: sahasraśīrṣā puruṣa ityupahitāṃ puruṣeṇa nārāyaṇena yajamāna upatiṣṭhate
16.28.3.a.d: सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुष इत्युपहितां पुरुषेण नारायणेन यजमान उपतिष्ठते
16.28.3.a.m: The sacrificer reveres [the layer] when it is laid down with the Puruṣasūkta [beginning with] 'A thousand-headed is the Puruṣa'.

16.28.4.b.m: Five [pointing] from east to west with 'I settle you in the courses of waters';

16.28.4.c.s: arṇave sadane sīdeti pañca dakṣiṇata udīcīḥ /
16.28.4.c.d: अर्णवे सदने सीदेति पञ्च दक्षिणत उदीचीः ।
16.28.4.c.m: Five [pointing] from south to north with 'Sit in the surge of the ocean';

16.28.4.d.s: apāṃ tvā sadane sādayāmīti pañca paścātprācīḥ /
16.28.4.d.d: अपां त्वा सदने सादयामीति पञ्च पश्चात्प्राचीः ।
16.28.4.d.m: Five [pointing] from west to east with 'I settle you in the seat of waters';

16.28.4.e.m: Five [pointing] from north to south with 'The gāyatrī metre'.

16.29.1.a.m: "The gods who grasped the sacrifice from around the gods,

16.29.1.b.s: tāngāyatrī nayatu prajānatī svarge loke amṛtaṃ duhānā //
16.29.1.b.d: तान्गायत्री नयतु प्रजानती स्वर्गे लोके अमृतं दुहाना ॥
16.29.1.b.m: May the knowing gāyatrī lead them, milking immortality in the heavenly world.

16.29.1.c.s: ye jyotīṃṣi saṃdadhati svarārohanto amṛtasya lokam /
16.29.1.c.d: ये ज्योतींषि संदधति स्वरारोहन्तो अमृतस्य लोकम् ।
16.29.1.c.m: Those who unite the lights, ascending to heaven, to the world of immortality,

16.29.1.d.s: te yantu prajānanto yajñaṃ vidānāḥ sukṛtasya loke //
16.29.1.d.d: ते यन्तु प्रजानन्तो यज्ञं विदानाः सुकृतस्य लोके ॥
16.29.1.d.m: May they go knowing, recognizing the sacrifice in the world of the well-done.

16.29.1.e.m: The animals fit for sacrifice who were produced toward the womb of the sacrifice,

16.29.1.f.s: tāndadante kavayo vipaścito yajñaṃ vidānāḥ sukṛtasya loke //
16.29.1.f.d: तान्ददन्ते कवयो विपश्चितो यज्ञं विदानाः सुकृतस्य लोके ॥
16.29.1.f.m: The wise, inspired poets offer them, recognizing the sacrifice in the world of the well-done.

16.29.1.g.m: The path that is stretched out, going to the gods, proceeds distributed by metres;

16.29.1.h.m: By that path he has reached heaven and the intermediate space, having seized the sacrifice, into the world of the well-done.

16.29.1.i.m: The sacrifice of a thousand streams, built up above heaven and earth,

16.29.1.j.s: tenaitu yajamānaḥ svastyā divo 'dhi pṛṣṭhamasthāditi pañca hiraṇyeṣṭakāḥ pratidiśam /
16.29.1.j.d: तेनैतु यजमानः स्वस्त्या दिवो ऽधि पृष्ठमस्थादिति पञ्च हिरण्येष्टकाः प्रतिदिशम् ।
16.29.1.j.m: By that may the sacrificer go to well-being; he has stood upon the back of heaven" — [with these verses] five gold bricks [are laid down], one in each direction;

16.29.2.a.s: āyave svāhāyoṣkṛte svāhāyoṣpatvane svāhā viṣṇave svāhā bṛhapsataye svāheti pañcopadhāyādbhyaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ pṛthivyai rasācca viśvakramaṇaḥ samavartatādhi /
16.29.2.a.d: आयवे स्वाहायोष्कृते स्वाहायोष्पत्वने स्वाहा विष्णवे स्वाहा बृहप्सतये स्वाहेति पञ्चोपधायाद्भ्यः संभूतः पृथिव्यै रसाच्च विश्वक्रमणः समवर्तताधि ।
16.29.2.a.m: Having laid down five with 'Svāhā to the quick one, svāhā to the fashioner of quickness, svāhā to the flier of quickness, svāhā to Viṣṇu, svāhā to Bṛhaspati', and having laid down this [brick] with 'Formed from the waters, the sap of earth, and Viśvakarman, he arose over [all]; / Fashioning his form, Tvaṣṭṛ approaches; that was the complete birth of the Puruṣa in the beginning', [he lays down bricks with:] 'You are the seat of truth, the seat of reality, the seat of brilliance, the seat of splendour, the seat of fame, you are praised.

16.29.2.b.s: tasya tvaṣṭā vidadhadrūpameti tatpuruṣasya viśvamājānamagra ityetāmupadhāyartasadasi satyasadasi tejaḥsadasi varcaḥsadasi yaśaḥsadasi gṛṇānāsi /
16.29.2.b.d: तस्य त्वष्टा विदधद्रूपमेति तत्पुरुषस्य विश्वमाजानमग्र इत्येतामुपधायर्तसदसि सत्यसदसि तेजःसदसि वर्चःसदसि यशःसदसि गृणानासि ।
16.29.2.b.m: You are the abode; to the abode I [offer] you, to the abodes I [offer] you; sit in the abodes.

16.29.2.c.s: dhāmāsi dhāmyai tvā dhāmabhyastvā dhāmasu sīda /
16.29.2.c.d: धामासि धाम्यै त्वा धामभ्यस्त्वा धामसु सीद ।
16.29.2.c.m: You are acquisition; to acquisition I [offer] you; may I acquire.

16.29.2.d.m: You are finding; to finding I [offer] you; may I find.

16.29.2.e.m: You are ability; to ability I [offer] you; may I be able.

16.29.2.f.m: You are prosperity; to prosperity I [offer] you; may I prosper.

16.29.2.g.m: You are ritual action; to ritual action I [offer] you; may I perform.

16.29.2.h.m: You are the jump; to the jump I [offer] you, to the jumps I [offer] you; sit in the jump.

16.30.1.a.s: gūrdo 'si gūrdāya tvā gūrdebhyastvā gūrde sīda /
16.30.1.a.d: गूर्दो ऽसि गूर्दाय त्वा गूर्देभ्यस्त्वा गूर्दे सीद ।
16.30.1.a.m: Protect dominion, nourish dominion, animate dominion, bestow dominion, strengthen dominion. You are dominion; to dominion I [offer] you, to dominions I [offer] you; sit in dominion.

16.30.1.b.s: kṣatraṃ pāhi kṣatraṃ pinva kṣatraṃ jinva kṣatraṃ yaccha kṣatraṃ dṛṃha kṣatramasi kṣatrāya tvā kṣatrebhyastvā kṣatre sīda /
16.30.1.b.d: क्षत्रं पाहि क्षत्रं पिन्व क्षत्रं जिन्व क्षत्रं यच्छ क्षत्रं दृंह क्षत्रमसि क्षत्राय त्वा क्षत्रेभ्यस्त्वा क्षत्रे सीद ।
16.30.1.b.m: I settle you in all earthly things.

16.30.1.c.m: I settle you in all intermediate things.

16.30.1.d.m: I settle you in all heavenly things.

16.30.1.e.m: I settle you in all gods.

16.30.1.f.m: I settle you in all waters.

16.30.1.g.m: I settle you in all plants.

16.30.1.h.m: I settle you in all trees.

16.30.1.i.m: I settle you in all quarters.

16.30.1.l.s: svarjidasi pṛtanājidasi bhūrijidasyabhijidasi viśvajidasi sarvajidasi satrājidasi dhanajidasi bhrāḍasi vibhrāḍasi prabhrāḍasi /
16.30.1.l.d: स्वर्जिदसि पृतनाजिदसि भूरिजिदस्यभिजिदसि विश्वजिदसि सर्वजिदसि सत्राजिदसि धनजिदसि भ्राडसि विभ्राडसि प्रभ्राडसि ।
16.30.1.l.m: I settle you, a thunderbolt striking rivals.

16.30.1.m.m: I settle you, a thunderbolt striking enemies.

16.30.1.n.m: I settle you, a thunderbolt striking ill-will.

16.30.1.o.m: I settle you, a thunderbolt striking sorcerers.

16.30.1.p.m: I settle you, a thunderbolt striking piśācas.

16.30.1.q.m: I settle you, a thunderbolt striking rakṣases.

16.30.1.r.m: I settle you, Indra's thunderbolt, striking foes, striking unfriendly ones, striking adversaries, striking asuras.

16.30.1.s.m: You are the high-speaker, you are rising, you are surging, you are approaching, you are advancing, you are conquest, you are stepping over, you are crossing, you are transition, you lead to heaven, you are heaven.

16.30.1.t.m: Sit in nourishment, sit in strength, sit in good fortune, sit in wealth, sit in well-being, sit in the sacrificial [seat] of earth, sit on the back of Viṣṇu, sit in the place of iḍā, sit in ghee, sit in abundance.

16.30.1.u.s: iṣi sīdorji sīda bhage sīda draviṇe sīda subhūte sīda pṛthivyā yajñiye sīda viṣṇoḥ pṛṣṭhe sīdeḍāyāḥ pade sīda ghṛtavati sīda pinvamāne sīda
16.30.1.u.d: इषि सीदोर्जि सीद भगे सीद द्रविणे सीद सुभूते सीद पृथिव्या यज्ञिये सीद विष्णोः पृष्ठे सीदेडायाः पदे सीद घृतवति सीद पिन्वमाने सीद
16.30.1.u.m: Sit in the saṃvatsara-year, sit in the parivatsara-year, sit in the idāvatsara-year, sit in the iduvatsara-year, sit in the idvatsara-year, sit in the vatsara-year.

16.31.1.a.s: saṃvatsare sīda parivatsare sīdedāvatsare sīdeduvatsare sīdedvatsare sīda vatsare sīda /
16.31.1.a.d: संवत्सरे सीद परिवत्सरे सीदेदावत्सरे सीदेदुवत्सरे सीदेद्वत्सरे सीद वत्सरे सीद ।
16.31.1.a.m: Sit in one, sit in ten, sit in a hundred, sit in a thousand, sit in ten thousand, sit in a hundred thousand, sit in a million, sit in ten million, sit in a hundred million, sit in a billion, sit in the middle, sit in ten billion, sit at the end, sit in the highest number.

16.31.1.b.s: ekasyāṃ sīda daśasu sīda śate sīda sahasre sīdāyute sīda niyute sīda prayute sīdārbude sīda nyarbude sīda samudre sīda madhye sīda padme sīdānte sīda parārdhe sīda /
16.31.1.b.d: एकस्यां सीद दशसु सीद शते सीद सहस्रे सीदायुते सीद नियुते सीद प्रयुते सीदार्बुदे सीद न्यर्बुदे सीद समुद्रे सीद मध्ये सीद पद्मे सीदान्ते सीद परार्धे सीद ।
16.31.1.b.m: You are swelling; to the swelling I [offer] you, to the swelling ones I [offer] you; sit in the swelling.

16.31.1.c.s: pinvamānāsi pinvamānāya tvā pinvamānebhyastvā pinvamāne sīda /
16.31.1.c.d: पिन्वमानासि पिन्वमानाय त्वा पिन्वमानेभ्यस्त्वा पिन्वमाने सीद ।
16.31.1.c.m: You are truth; to truth I [offer] you, to the true I [offer] you; sit in truth.

16.31.1.d.m: You are reality; to reality I [offer] you, to the real I [offer] you; sit in reality.

16.31.1.e.s: satyamasi satyāya tvā satyebhyastvā satye sīda /
16.31.1.e.d: सत्यमसि सत्याय त्वा सत्येभ्यस्त्वा सत्ये सीद ।
16.31.1.e.m: You are junction; to junction I [offer] you, to junctions I [offer] you; sit in junctions.

16.31.1.f.s: saṃdhirasi saṃdhaye tvā saṃdhibhyastvā saṃdhiṣu sīda /
16.31.1.f.d: संधिरसि संधये त्वा संधिभ्यस्त्वा संधिषु सीद ।
16.31.1.f.m: You are close adherence; to close adherence I [offer] you, to the adhering ones I [offer] you; sit in adherence.

16.31.1.g.s: saṃśliḍasi saṃśliṣe tvā saṃśliḍbhyastvā saṃśliṭsu sīda /
16.31.1.g.d: संश्लिडसि संश्लिषे त्वा संश्लिड्भ्यस्त्वा संश्लिट्सु सीद ।
16.31.1.g.m: You are attainment; to attainment I [offer] you, to attainments I [offer] you; sit in attainments' — with these two anuvākas, verse by verse, [he lays down] the seer-bricks [ṛṣīṣṭakāḥ] and with the rounds expressing settling.

16.31.1.h.s: saṃpadasi saṃpade tvā saṃpadbhyastvā saṃpatsu sīdetyetābhyāmanuvākābhyāṃ pratimantramṛṣīṣṭakāḥ sādanapravādaiśca paryāyaiḥ
16.31.1.h.d: संपदसि संपदे त्वा संपद्भ्यस्त्वा संपत्सु सीदेत्येताभ्यामनुवाकाभ्यां प्रतिमन्त्रमृषीष्टकाः सादनप्रवादैश्च पर्यायैः
16.31.1.h.m: [With] 'This one in front is being', [he lays down] fifty breath-holding bricks [prāṇabhṛtaḥ]:

16.32.1.a.s: ayaṃ puro bhuva iti pañcāśataṃ prāṇabhṛtaḥ /
16.32.1.a.d: अयं पुरो भुव इति पञ्चाशतं प्राणभृतः ।
16.32.1.a.m: Ten in each quarter, [and] diagonally ten;

16.32.1.b.m: Having laid down the inner one in the middle, [he lays down] each outer one.

16.32.1.c.m: [With] 'The eastern of the directions', [he lays down] fifty out-breath-holding bricks [apānabhṛtaḥ] in the same manner as the breath-holding bricks,

16.32.2.a.m: Having laid down the outer one, [then] each inner one.

16.32.3.j.m: "Extend the intermediate region from the earth;"

16.32.3.l.m: "Extend light from heaven"—[with these mantras he sets down] the twelve continuity bricks.

16.32.4.a.s: pṛthivī vaśāmāvāsyā garbho vanaspatayo jarāyvagnirvatso 'gnihotraṃ pīyuṣaḥ /
16.32.4.a.d: पृथिवी वशामावास्या गर्भो वनस्पतयो जराय्वग्निर्वत्सो ऽग्निहोत्रं पीयुषः ।
16.32.4.a.m: "The earth is the barren cow, the new moon day is the fetus, the trees are the placenta, Agni is the calf, the agnihotra is the colostrum;"

16.32.4.b.s: antarikṣaṃ vaśā dhātā garbho rudro jarāyu vāyurvatso ghrmaḥ pīyūṣaḥ /
16.32.4.b.d: अन्तरिक्षं वशा धाता गर्भो रुद्रो जरायु वायुर्वत्सो घ्र्मः पीयूषः ।
16.32.4.b.m: "The intermediate region is the barren cow, Dhātṛ is the fetus, Rudra is the placenta, Vāyu is the calf, the summer heat is the colostrum;"

16.32.4.c.s: dyaurvaśā stanayitnurgarbho nakṣatrāṇi jarāyu sūryo vatso vṛṣṭiḥ pīyūṣaḥ /
16.32.4.c.d: द्यौर्वशा स्तनयित्नुर्गर्भो नक्षत्राणि जरायु सूर्यो वत्सो वृष्टिः पीयूषः ।
16.32.4.c.m: "Heaven is the barren cow, the thunder is the fetus, the lunar mansions are the placenta, the sun is the calf, the rain is the colostrum;"

16.32.4.d.s: ṛgvaśā bṛhadrathaṃtare garbhaḥ praiṣanivido jarāyu yajño vatso dakṣiṇāḥ pīyūṣaḥ /
16.32.4.d.d: ऋग्वशा बृहद्रथंतरे गर्भः प्रैषनिविदो जरायु यज्ञो वत्सो दक्षिणाः पीयूषः ।
16.32.4.d.m: "The Ṛgveda is the barren cow, the Bṛhat and Rathantara [sāmans] are the fetus, the ritual calls and nivids are the placenta, the sacrifice is the calf, the sacrificial gifts are the colostrum;"

16.32.4.e.s: viḍvaśā rājanyo garbhaḥ paśavo jarāyu rājā vatso baliḥ pīyūṣa iti pañca vaśā
16.32.4.e.d: विड्वशा राजन्यो गर्भः पशवो जरायु राजा वत्सो बलिः पीयूष इति पञ्च वशा
16.32.4.e.m: "The commonalty is the barren cow, the nobleman is the fetus, the animals are the placenta, the king is the calf, the tribute is the colostrum"—[these are] the five barren cow [bricks].

16.32.5.a.s: artheta sthādhvagato 'gnirvastejiṣṭhena tejasā devatābhirgṛhṇāmīti kumbhaṃ kumbhīṃ cādbhiḥ pūrayitvā śarma ca stha varma ca stha devasya vaḥ savituḥ prasave madhumatīḥ sādayāmīti purastādanusītamupadhāya jyotiṣe vāmiti hiraṇyaśalkau pratyasyati
16.32.5.a.d: अर्थेत स्थाध्वगतो ऽग्निर्वस्तेजिष्ठेन तेजसा देवताभिर्गृह्णामीति कुम्भं कुम्भीं चाद्भिः पूरयित्वा शर्म च स्थ वर्म च स्थ देवस्य वः सवितुः प्रसवे मधुमतीः सादयामीति पुरस्तादनुसीतमुपधाय ज्योतिषे वामिति हिरण्यशल्कौ प्रत्यस्यति
16.32.5.a.m: Having filled a jar and a small jar with water with "You are meant for a purpose, on the journey; with Agni's most brilliant radiance, through the deities I draw you," having placed them in the east along the furrow with "You are protection, you are armor; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, sweet I seat you," he tosses into each a gold flake with "For luster to you both."

16.32.6.a.m: In this same way [he places] the subsequent ones with the subsequent mantras in each direction along the furrow;

16.32.7.a.s: śukrā stha vīryāvatīrindrasya va indriyāvato devatābhirgṛhṇāmi
16.32.7.a.d: शुक्रा स्थ वीर्यावतीरिन्द्रस्य व इन्द्रियावतो देवताभिर्गृह्णामि
16.32.7.a.m: "You are bright, full of virility; of Indra who possesses virility, through the deities I draw you;"

16.33.1.a.s: ṛtaṃ ca stha satyaṃ ca stha devasya vaḥ savituḥ prasave madhumatīḥ sādayāmi /
16.33.1.a.d: ऋतं च स्थ सत्यं च स्थ देवस्य वः सवितुः प्रसवे मधुमतीः सादयामि ।
16.33.1.a.m: "You are order and you are truth; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, sweet I seat you;"

16.33.1.c.s: mandarā sthābhibhuvo viśveṣāṃ vo devānāṃ devatābhirgṛhṇāmi /
16.33.1.c.d: मन्दरा स्थाभिभुवो विश्वेषां वो देवानां देवताभिर्गृह्णामि ।
16.33.1.c.m: "You are gladdening, overpowering; through the deities of the All-gods I draw you;"

16.33.1.d.s: sapatnaghnīśca sthābhimātighnīśca stha devasya vaḥ savituḥ prasave madhumatīḥ sādayāmi /
16.33.1.d.d: सपत्नघ्नीश्च स्थाभिमातिघ्नीश्च स्थ देवस्य वः सवितुः प्रसवे मधुमतीः सादयामि ।
16.33.1.d.m: "You are slayers of rivals and slayers of assailants; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, sweet I seat you;"

16.33.1.f.m: "You are the sovereign, mighty; through the deities of the Ādityas I draw you;"

16.33.1.g.s: rakṣoghnīśca sthārātighnīśca stha devasya vaḥ savituḥ prasave madhumatīḥ sādayāmi /
16.33.1.g.d: रक्षोघ्नीश्च स्थारातिघ्नीश्च स्थ देवस्य वः सवितुः प्रसवे मधुमतीः सादयामि ।
16.33.1.g.m: "You are slayers of demons and slayers of malicious foes; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, sweet I seat you;"

16.33.1.i.m: "You are holders of dominion, mighty; with the sacred word of Mitra and Varuṇa, through the deities I draw you;"

16.33.1.j.s: vasu ca stha vāmaṃ ca stha devasya vaḥ savituḥ prasave madhumatīḥ sādayāmi /
16.33.1.j.d: वसु च स्थ वामं च स्थ देवस्य वः सवितुः प्रसवे मधुमतीः सादयामि ।
16.33.1.j.m: "You are wealth and you are what is desirable; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, sweet I seat you;"

16.33.1.l.m: "You are dwelling in the pen, looking upward; with the sacred word of Bṛhaspati, through the deities I draw you;"

16.33.1.m.s: bhūtaṃ ca stha bhavyaṃ ca stha devasya vaḥ savituḥ prasave madhumatīḥ sādayāmi /
16.33.1.m.d: भूतं च स्थ भव्यं च स्थ देवस्य वः सवितुः प्रसवे मधुमतीः सादयामि ।
16.33.1.m.m: "You are what has been and you are what is to be; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, sweet I seat you;"

16.33.1.n.m: "For radiance to you both"—these are the drawing, seating, and tossing mantras of the pot-bricks.

16.33.2.a.m: He addresses them once laid with "Golden of hue..."

16.33.3.a.s: divi śrayasveti bārhaspatyaṃ naivāraṃ payasi caruṃ madhye kumbheṣṭakānāmupadadhāti
16.33.3.a.d: दिवि श्रयस्वेति बार्हस्पत्यं नैवारं पयसि चरुं मध्ये कुम्भेष्टकानामुपदधाति
16.33.3.a.m: With "Rest in heaven," he sets down in the middle of the pot-bricks a wild rice caru cooked in milk for Bṛhaspati;

16.33.4.b.s: hiraṇyavarṇaḥ sa hiraṇyasaṃdṛgapāṃ patiḥ sedu hiraṇyavarṇaḥ /
16.33.4.b.d: हिरण्यवर्णः स हिरण्यसंदृगपां पतिः सेदु हिरण्यवर्णः ।
16.33.4.b.m: "Golden-colored is he, golden of aspect, the lord of waters; he indeed is golden-colored;

16.33.4.c.s: hirṇyayātpari yonerniṣadyā hiraṇyadā dadatyannamasmā ityetābhyāṃ ca naivāram
16.33.4.c.d: हिर्ण्ययात्परि योनेर्निषद्या हिरण्यदा ददत्यन्नमस्मा इत्येताभ्यां च नैवारम्
16.33.4.c.m: sitting down from the golden womb, the givers of gold give food to him"—and with these two [verses he sets down] the wild rice [caru].

16.33.5.a.m: "The threefold chant is your head, O Agni; that is my head, O Agni;"

16.33.5.b.s: pañcadaśau te agne bāhū tau me agne bāhū /
16.33.5.b.d: पञ्चदशौ ते अग्ने बाहू तौ मे अग्ने बाहू ।
16.33.5.b.m: "The fifteenfold chants are your two arms, O Agni; those are my two arms, O Agni;"

16.33.5.c.s: saptadaśaste agna ātmā sa me agna ātmā /
16.33.5.c.d: सप्तदशस्ते अग्न आत्मा स मे अग्न आत्मा ।
16.33.5.c.m: "The seventeenfold chant is your body, O Agni; that is my body, O Agni;"

16.33.5.d.s: ekaviṃśau te agne ūrū tau me agne ūrū /
16.33.5.d.d: एकविंशौ ते अग्ने ऊरू तौ मे अग्ने ऊरू ।
16.33.5.d.m: "The twenty-onefold chants are your two thighs, O Agni; those are my two thighs, O Agni;"

16.33.5.e.s: triṇavau te agne aṣṭhīvantau tau me agne aṣṭhīvantau /
16.33.5.e.d: त्रिणवौ ते अग्ने अष्ठीवन्तौ तौ मे अग्ने अष्ठीवन्तौ ।
