16.33.5.e.m: "The thrice-ninefold chants are your two knee-caps, O Agni; those are my two knee-caps, O Agni;"

16.33.5.f.s: trayastriṃśaṃ te agne pratiṣṭhānaṃ tanme agne pratiṣṭhānamityetāḥ śirasi pakṣayormadhye pucche vopadadhāti
16.33.5.f.d: त्रयस्त्रिंशं ते अग्ने प्रतिष्ठानं तन्मे अग्ने प्रतिष्ठानमित्येताः शिरसि पक्षयोर्मध्ये पुच्छे वोपदधाति
16.33.5.f.m: "The thirty-threefold chant is your foundation, O Agni; that is my foundation, O Agni"—these he places on the head, on the two wings, in the middle, and on the tail.

16.33.6.a.s: trivṛtte agne śirastena mā pāhīti saṃnamayaṃstāṃtāmupatiṣṭhate yajamānaḥ
16.33.6.a.d: त्रिवृत्ते अग्ने शिरस्तेन मा पाहीति संनमयंस्तांतामुपतिष्ठते यजमानः
16.33.6.a.m: Modifying [the mantras] with "The threefold chant is your head, O Agni; protect me with it," the sacrificer reveres each of them.

16.33.7.a.s: tvāmagne vṛṣabhamityṛṣabhamupadhāya lokaṃ pṛṇa tā asya sūdadohasa ityaviśiṣṭamaparimitābhirlokaṃpṛṇābhiḥ pracchādayati
16.33.7.a.d: त्वामग्ने वृषभमित्यृषभमुपधाय लोकं पृण ता अस्य सूददोहस इत्यविशिष्टमपरिमिताभिर्लोकंपृणाभिः प्रच्छादयति
16.33.7.a.m: Having placed the bull-brick with "You, O Agni, the bull...," with "Fill the space...," and "Those milk-givers of his...," he covers the remainder [of the layer] with an unlimited number of space-filler bricks.

16.33.8.a.m: He should make the marks of the bricks of all varieties.

16.34.1.a.m: There is an authoritative instruction on the lines, and it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]:

16.34.2.a.m: "Those that turn to the right he should place on the south;

16.34.2.c.m: those with straight lines, in the west and in the east;

16.34.3.a.m: Having placed gold upon the layer, he touches it with the layer-arrangement [mantra]: "The known and the unknown..."

16.34.4.a.s: yatte 'citaṃ yadu citaṃ te agne yadūnaṃ yadvātrātiriktam /
16.34.4.a.d: यत्ते ऽचितं यदु चितं ते अग्ने यदूनं यद्वात्रातिरिक्तम् ।
16.34.4.a.m: "Whatever is unpiled of you, and whatever is piled of you, O Agni, whatever is deficient or whatever here is redundant,

16.34.4.b.m: may the All-gods and the Aṅgirases pile it, may the Ādityas fill up your layer.

16.34.4.e.m: "May we, O Agni, possess wealth, sufficient for the sacrifice and for the sacrificial gift;

16.34.4.f.m: may the pressing stone speak facing the stalk of Soma; may we serve Indra with the pressed juice."

16.34.4.g.s: rāyaspoṣaṃ no dhehi jātaveda ūrjo bhāgaṃ madhumatsūnṛtāvat /
16.34.4.g.d: रायस्पोषं नो धेहि जातवेद ऊर्जो भागं मधुमत्सूनृतावत् ।
16.34.4.g.m: Bestow on us prosperity of wealth, O Jātavedas, a portion of vigour, sweet and pleasant;

16.34.4.h.s: dadhāma yajñaṃ sunavāma somaṃ yajñena tvāmupaśikṣema śakra //
16.34.4.h.d: दधाम यज्ञं सुनवाम सोमं यज्ञेन त्वामुपशिक्षेम शक्र ॥
16.34.4.h.m: May we establish the sacrifice, may we press soma; by the sacrifice may we serve you, O mighty one!

16.34.4.i.s: īśānaṃ tvā śuśrumo vayaṃ dhanānāṃ dhanapate gomadagne /
16.34.4.i.d: ईशानं त्वा शुश्रुमो वयं धनानां धनपते गोमदग्ने ।
16.34.4.i.m: We have heard of you as the master of riches, O lord of wealth, rich in cattle, O Agni;

16.34.4.j.m: Bestow upon me abundant, rich nourishment with horses and with gold!

16.34.4.k.s: duhāṃ te dyauḥ pṛthivī payo 'jagarastvā sodako visarpatu /
16.34.4.k.d: दुहां ते द्यौः पृथिवी पयो ऽजगरस्त्वा सोदको विसर्पतु ।
16.34.4.k.m: May heaven and earth yield milk for you; may the water-python glide away from you;

16.34.4.l.m: With Prajāpati I fill myself; empty is my self.

16.34.4.m.s: yo rudro agnau yo apsu ya oṣadhīṣu yo rudro viśvā bhuvanāviveśa /
16.34.4.m.d: यो रुद्रो अग्नौ यो अप्सु य ओषधीषु यो रुद्रो विश्वा भुवनाविवेश ।
16.34.4.m.m: The Rudra who is in the fire, who is in the waters, who is in the plants, the Rudra who entered into all beings—

16.34.4.n.s: tasmai rudrāya namo astu devā ityetābhiḥ svayaṃcityābhimṛśati
16.34.4.n.d: तस्मै रुद्राय नमो अस्तु देवा इत्येताभिः स्वयंचित्याभिमृशति
16.34.4.n.m: To that Rudra be homage, O gods!"—with these [verses] he touches the self-built [layer].

16.34.5.a.m: To the north stands a black horse,

16.34.6.a.s: tamālabhya cātvālātpurīṣmāhṛtya pṛṣṭo divīti vaiśvānaryarcā citāvanubyūhati
16.34.6.a.d: तमालभ्य चात्वालात्पुरीष्माहृत्य पृष्टो दिवीति वैश्वानर्यर्चा चितावनुब्यूहति
16.34.6.a.m: Touching it, having brought loose earth from the cātvāla pit, he scatters it along the layer with the Vaiśvānara verse: "Set on the back of heaven..."

16.35.1.a.s: yo apsvantaragniryo vṛtre yaḥ puruṣe yo aśmani /
16.35.1.a.d: यो अप्स्वन्तरग्निर्यो वृत्रे यः पुरुषे यो अश्मनि ।
16.35.1.a.m: "The fire which is within the waters, which is in Vṛtra, which is in man, which is in the rock,

16.35.1.b.s: ya āviveśa bhuvanāni viśvā tebhyo agnibhyo hutamastvetat //
16.35.1.b.d: य आविवेश भुवनानि विश्वा तेभ्यो अग्निभ्यो हुतमस्त्वेतत् ॥
16.35.1.b.m: Which entered into all beings—to those fires be this offered!

16.35.1.c.s: yaḥ some antaryo goṣvantarvayāṃsi ya āviveśa yo mṛgeṣu /
16.35.1.c.d: यः सोमे अन्तर्यो गोष्वन्तर्वयांसि य आविवेश यो मृगेषु ।
16.35.1.c.m: The one which is within soma, which is within cattle, which entered the birds, which is in beasts,

16.35.1.d.s: ya āviveśa dvipado yaścatuṣpadastebhyo agnibhyo hutamastvetat //
16.35.1.d.d: य आविवेश द्विपदो यश्चतुष्पदस्तेभ्यो अग्निभ्यो हुतमस्त्वेतत् ॥
16.35.1.d.m: Which entered two-footed [creatures], which entered four-footed—to those fires be this offered!

16.35.1.f.s: yenendrasya rathaṃ saṃbabhūvuryo vaiśvānara uta vaiśvadevyaḥ /
16.35.1.f.d: येनेन्द्रस्य रथं संबभूवुर्यो वैश्वानर उत वैश्वदेव्यः ।
16.35.1.f.m: With which they joined Indra's chariot, which is Vaiśvānara and also belonging to all the gods,

16.35.1.g.s: dhīro yaḥ śakraḥ paribhūradābhyastebhyo agnibhyo hutamastvetat //
16.35.1.g.d: धीरो यः शक्रः परिभूरदाभ्यस्तेभ्यो अग्निभ्यो हुतमस्त्वेतत् ॥
16.35.1.g.m: Wise, powerful, surrounding, undecaying—to those fires be this offered!

16.35.1.h.s: yaṃ hutādamagniṃ yamu kāmamāhuryaṃ dātāraṃ pratigrahītāramāhuḥ /
16.35.1.h.d: यं हुतादमग्निं यमु काममाहुर्यं दातारं प्रतिग्रहीतारमाहुः ।
16.35.1.h.m: [and] “Which Agni the consumer of the oblation, and which they call desire, whom they call the giver, the receiver,” [he attends upon it].

16.35.1.i.m: Who is the most divine of gods, born of heat—to those fires be this offered!"

16.35.1.j.m: With these six [verses], having placed layer upon layer, he makes an offering over each [with the verses beginning] "For the bull-eater, for the barren-cow-eater..."

16.35.2.a.m: With an Agni-verse, with a dhāmacchad verse: "Agni, many...", having placed layer upon layer, he makes an offering over [it].

16.35.4.a.m: It is stated: "He should touch the first layer with an Agni-verse in the gāyatrī metre."

16.35.5.a.s: agne devām̐ ihā vaha jajñāno vṛktabarhiṣe /
16.35.5.a.d: अग्ने देवाम्̐ इहा वह जज्ञानो वृक्तबर्हिषे ।
16.35.5.a.m: "O Agni, bring the gods hither, being born for him who has trimmed the sacrificial grass;

16.35.5.c.s: aganma mahā manasā yaviṣṭhaṃ yo dīdāya samiddhaḥ sve duroṇe /
16.35.5.c.d: अगन्म महा मनसा यविष्ठं यो दीदाय समिद्धः स्वे दुरोणे ।
16.35.5.c.m: We have approached with great mind the youngest, who shines kindled in his own abode,

16.35.5.d.s: citrabhānū rodasī antarurvī svāhutaṃ viśvataḥ pratyañcam //
16.35.5.d.d: चित्रभानू रोदसी अन्तरुर्वी स्वाहुतं विश्वतः प्रत्यञ्चम् ॥
16.35.5.d.m: Shining wonderfully between the two wide heaven and earth, well-sacrificed, facing all directions.

16.35.5.e.s: medhākāraṃ vidathasya prasādhanamagniṃ hotāraṃ paribhūtamaṃ matim /
16.35.5.e.d: मेधाकारं विदथस्य प्रसाधनमग्निं होतारं परिभूतमं मतिम् ।
16.35.5.e.m: The creator of wisdom, the accomplisher of the sacred assembly, Agni the hotṛ, most comprehensive, the thought;

16.35.5.f.s: tvāmarbhasya haviṣaḥ samānamittvā maho vṛṇate naro nānyaṃ tvat //
16.35.5.f.d: त्वामर्भस्य हविषः समानमित्त्वा महो वृणते नरो नान्यं त्वत् ॥
16.35.5.f.m: You for a small offering, just the same for a great one, do men choose, none other than you.

16.35.5.g.m: Like Manu we set you down, like Manu we kindle you;

16.35.5.h.m: O Agni, like Manu, O Aṅgiras, sacrifice to the gods on behalf of him who seeks the gods!

16.35.5.i.m: For Agni, dwelling among all men, gives a steed to the clan;

16.35.5.j.s: agnī rāye svābhuvaṃ sa prīto yāti vāryamiṣaṃ stotṛbhya ā bharetyetā āmnātā bhavanti
16.35.5.j.d: अग्नी राये स्वाभुवं स प्रीतो याति वार्यमिषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भरेत्येता आम्नाता भवन्ति
16.35.5.j.m: Agni, pleasing to riches, approaches; may he, being pleased, bring desirable food to the praisers"—these are handed down by tradition.

16.35.7.a.m: For two days each, he offers with one Upasad mantra.

16.35.8.a.m: Following each Upasad, he piles the fire for two days.

16.35.11.a.s: āparāhṇikībhyāṃ pracarya śvetamaśvaṃ pariṇīya vasanti vasanti
16.35.11.a.d: आपराह्णिकीभ्यां प्रचर्य श्वेतमश्वं परिणीय वसन्ति वसन्ति
16.35.11.a.m: Having performed [the rites] with the two afternoon [offerings] and having led the white horse around, they dwell for each night.

17.1.1.a.s: śvo bhūte paurvāhṇikībhyāṃ pracarya dvitīyāṃ citiṃ cinoti
17.1.1.a.d: श्वो भूते पौर्वाह्णिकीभ्यां प्रचर्य द्वितीयां चितिं चिनोति
17.1.1.a.m: On the next day, having performed [the rites] with the two morning [offerings], he piles the second layer.

17.1.2.a.m: With "Steadfast dwelling..." he places the five Āśvinī bricks.

17.1.3.a.m: With "United with the seasons..." having placed the five seasonal bricks following the Āśvinī bricks;

17.1.4.a.s: prāṇaṃ me pāhīti pañca prāṇabhṛta ṛtavyā anūpadhāya
17.1.4.a.d: प्राणं मे पाहीति पञ्च प्राणभृत ऋतव्या अनूपधाय
17.1.4.a.m: With "Protect my breath..." having placed the five vital-breath-supporting bricks following the seasonal bricks;

17.1.5.a.m: With "Swell the waters..." [he places] the five water-bricks, moving all around.

17.1.6.a.m: With "You are Vāyu's vehicle..." [he places] two Saṃyānī bricks.

17.1.7.a.m: With "Bright and clear..." [he places] two seasonal bricks having the same deity and placement.

17.1.8.a.m: With "The three-year-old steer is strength..." [he places] five [bricks] on the southern buttock;

17.1.8.b.m: With "The four-year-old ox is strength..." [he places] five on the northern;

17.1.8.c.m: With "The he-goat is strength..." [he places bricks] on the right shoulder;

17.1.8.e.m: With "The tiger is strength..." on the right wing;

17.1.8.i.s: viṣṭambho vaya iti catasro vayasyāḥ purastātpratīcīḥ
17.1.8.i.d: विष्टम्भो वय इति चतस्रो वयस्याः पुरस्तात्प्रतीचीः
17.1.8.i.m: With "Support is strength..." [he places] four Vayasyā bricks in the front, facing west.

17.1.9.a.m: “He whom he might wish, ‘May he be without cattle,’ for him the [bricks] belonging to various ages”—thus it has been declared.

17.1.11.a.s: śvo bhūte paurvāhṇikībhyāṃ pracarya tṛtīyāṃ citiṃ cinoti
17.1.11.a.d: श्वो भूते पौर्वाह्णिकीभ्यां प्रचर्य तृतीयां चितिं चिनोति
17.1.11.a.m: On the next day, having performed the two morning rituals, he builds the third layer.

17.1.12.a.s: indrāgnī avyathamānāmiti svayamātṛṇāmabhimṛśyāśvenopaghrāpya viśvakarmā tvā sādayatvantarikṣasya pṛṣṭha ityaviduṣā brāhmaṇena saha madhye 'gnerupadadhāti /
17.1.12.a.d: इन्द्राग्नी अव्यथमानामिति स्वयमातृणामभिमृश्याश्वेनोपघ्राप्य विश्वकर्मा त्वा सादयत्वन्तरिक्षस्य पृष्ठ इत्यविदुषा ब्राह्मणेन सह मध्ये ऽग्नेरुपदधाति ।
17.1.12.a.m: Having touched the naturally perforated [brick] with 'Indra and Agni, not trembling...', and having made a horse sniff it, he lays it down in the center of the Agni with 'May Viśvakarman seat you on the back of the intermediate space...', together with an unlearned brāhmaṇa;

17.1.13.a.m: Having offered into the naturally perforated [brick] with 'I offer insight...', he breathes out.

17.1.14.a.m: [He lays] a gold brick with 'You are light; give me light.'

17.1.16.a.s: viśvakarmā tvā sādayatvantarikṣasya pṛṣṭhe jyotiṣmatīmiti viśvajyotiṣam
17.1.16.a.d: विश्वकर्मा त्वा सादयत्वन्तरिक्षस्य पृष्ठे ज्योतिष्मतीमिति विश्वज्योतिषम्
17.1.16.a.m: A Viśvajyotis brick with 'May Viśvakarman seat you on the back of the intermediate space, full of light.'

17.1.17.a.m: Two Saṃyānī bricks with 'You are that which goes to the intermediate space...'

17.2.1.a.m: Four seasonal bricks with 'Nabhas and Nabhasya...'

17.2.1.b.m: Two each, sharing the same deity-formula.

17.2.2.a.s: rājñyasi prācī digiti pañca diśyāḥ pratidiśamekāṃ madhye
17.2.2.a.d: राज्ञ्यसि प्राची दिगिति पञ्च दिश्याः प्रतिदिशमेकां मध्ये
17.2.2.a.m: Five directional bricks with 'You are the queen, the eastern direction...', one in each direction and one in the center.

17.2.3.a.m: Having laid down ten Prāṇabhṛt bricks in the east with 'Protect my life...',

17.2.4.b.m: twelve to the south with 'Mā meter...';

17.2.4.c.m: twelve to the west with 'Earth meter...';

17.2.4.d.m: twelve to the north with 'Agni is deity...'

17.2.5.a.m: Seven Vālakhilyā [bricks] facing west in the east with 'You are head, ruler...';

17.2.5.b.m: seven facing east in the west with 'Controller, ruler...'

17.2.6.a.s: akṣṇayā dveṣyasya prasavāya tvopayāmāya tvā kāṭāya tvārṇavāya tvā dharṇasāya tvā draviṇāya tvā sindhave tvā samudrāya tvā sarasvate tvā viśvavyacase tvā subhūtāya tvāntarikṣāya tveti dvādaśa bhūteṣṭakāḥ
17.2.6.a.d: अक्ष्णया द्वेष्यस्य प्रसवाय त्वोपयामाय त्वा काटाय त्वार्णवाय त्वा धर्णसाय त्वा द्रविणाय त्वा सिन्धवे त्वा समुद्राय त्वा सरस्वते त्वा विश्वव्यचसे त्वा सुभूताय त्वान्तरिक्षाय त्वेति द्वादश भूतेष्टकाः
17.2.6.a.m: Diagonally, for the enemy, twelve Bhūteṣṭakā bricks with 'To impulse you, to Upayāma you, to Kāṭa you, to the flood you, to Dharnas you, to wealth you, to the stream you, to the ocean you, to Sarasvat you, to the all-encompassing you, to well-being you, to the intermediate space you.'

17.2.8.a.s: śvo bhūte paurvāhṇikībhyāṃ pracarya caturthīṃ citiṃ cinoti
17.2.8.a.d: श्वो भूते पौर्वाह्णिकीभ्यां प्रचर्य चतुर्थीं चितिं चिनोति
17.2.8.a.m: On the next day, having performed the two morning rituals, he builds the fourth layer.

17.2.9.a.d: आशुस्त्रिवृदग्नेर्भागो ऽसीत्येताभ्यामनुवाकाभ्यां यथाब्राह्मणमुपधायान्तरिक्षमस्यन्तरिक्षाय त्वेति द्वे संयान्यौ
17.2.9.a.m: Having laid [bricks] down according to the Brāhmaṇa with the two anuvākas 'Swift, threefold...' and 'You are the portion of Agni...', [he lays down] two Saṃyānī bricks with 'You are the intermediate space, to the intermediate space you.'

17.2.10.a.m: Two seasonal bricks with 'Sahas and Sahasya...', sharing the same deity-formula.

17.2.11.a.m: Seventeen Sṛṣṭi bricks with 'They praised with one...'

17.2.12.a.s: iyameva sā yā prathamā vyaucchaditi ṣoḍaśa vyuṣṭīḥ
17.2.12.a.d: इयमेव सा या प्रथमा व्यौच्छदिति षोडश व्युष्टीः
17.2.12.a.m: Sixteen Vyuṣṭi bricks with 'This indeed is she who shone forth first...'

17.3.1.a.s: śvo bhūte paurvāhṇikībhyāṃ pracarya pañcamīṃ catiṃ cinoti
17.3.1.a.d: श्वो भूते पौर्वाह्णिकीभ्यां प्रचर्य पञ्चमीं चतिं चिनोति
17.3.1.a.m: On the next day, having performed the two morning rituals, he builds the fifth layer.

17.3.2.a.s: agne jātānpra ṇudā naḥ sapatnāniti purastādupadadhāti /
17.3.2.a.d: अग्ने जातान्प्र णुदा नः सपत्नानिति पुरस्तादुपदधाति ।
17.3.2.a.m: He lays [bricks] in the east with 'O Agni, dispel our enemies born...';

17.3.2.b.m: in the west with 'Those born with force...';

17.3.3.a.s: iṣṭakāyāṃ purīṣamadhyūhya pṛthivyāḥ purīṣamasīti madhye 'gneḥ purīṣavatīm
17.3.3.a.d: इष्टकायां पुरीषमध्यूह्य पृथिव्याः पुरीषमसीति मध्ये ऽग्नेः पुरीषवतीम्
17.3.3.a.m: Having scattered loose earth over the brick, [he lays] the loose-earth brick in the center of the Agni with 'You are the loose earth of the earth.'

17.3.4.a.s: evaśchando varivaśchanda iti catvāriṃśataṃ virājo daśadaśa pratidiśamakṣṇayā
17.3.4.a.d: एवश्छन्दो वरिवश्छन्द इति चत्वारिंशतं विराजो दशदश प्रतिदिशमक्ष्णया
17.3.4.a.m: Forty Virāj [bricks] with 'Eva meter, Varivas meter...', ten in each direction, diagonally.

17.3.5.a.s: raśmirasi kṣayāya tvā kṣayaṃ jinveti stomabhāgāḥ /
17.3.5.a.d: रश्मिरसि क्षयाय त्वा क्षयं जिन्वेति स्तोमभागाः ।
17.3.5.a.m: Stomabhāga bricks with 'You are a ray; for dwelling you, quicken the dwelling...':

17.3.6.a.s: rājñyasi prācī digiti pañca nāksadaḥ pratidiśamekāṃ madhye
17.3.6.a.d: राज्ञ्यसि प्राची दिगिति पञ्च नाक्सदः प्रतिदिशमेकां मध्ये
17.3.6.a.m: Five Nākasad bricks with 'You are the queen, the eastern direction...', one in each direction and one in the center.

17.3.7.a.s: tāsu purīṣamadhyūhyāyaṃ puro harikeśa iti pañcacoḍā abhyupadadhāti /
17.3.7.a.d: तासु पुरीषमध्यूह्यायं पुरो हरिकेश इति पञ्चचोडा अभ्युपदधाति ।
17.3.7.a.m: Having scattered loose earth over them, he places five Cūḍā bricks upon them with 'This one in front, yellow-haired...';

17.3.7.b.m: meditating in mind on the enemy, [he places] the last one facing east in the west.

17.3.8.a.s: āyostvā sadane sādayāmīti svayamātṛṇāmabhimṛśyāśvenopaghrāpya parameṣṭhī tvā sādayatu divaḥ pṛṣṭha ityaviduṣā brāhmaṇena saha madhye 'gnerupadadhāti /
17.3.8.a.d: आयोस्त्वा सदने सादयामीति स्वयमातृणामभिमृश्याश्वेनोपघ्राप्य परमेष्ठी त्वा सादयतु दिवः पृष्ठ इत्यविदुषा ब्राह्मणेन सह मध्ये ऽग्नेरुपदधाति ।
17.3.8.a.m: Having touched the naturally perforated [brick] with 'In the seat of Āyu I place you...', and having made a horse sniff it, he lays it down in the center of the Agni with 'May Parameṣṭhin seat you on the back of heaven...', together with an unlearned brāhmaṇa;

17.3.9.a.s: cittiṃ juhomīti svayamātṛṇāyāṃ hutvāpānya prothadaśva ityuttare 'ṃse vikarṇīm
17.3.9.a.d: चित्तिं जुहोमीति स्वयमातृणायां हुत्वापान्य प्रोथदश्व इत्युत्तरे ऽंसे विकर्णीम्
17.3.9.a.m: Having offered into the naturally perforated [brick] with 'I offer insight...', having inhaled, [he lays] the Vikarṇī brick on the northern shoulder with 'Snorting, the horse...'

17.3.10.a.m: He places [them] over them with other bricks.

17.4.1.a.m: A gold brick with 'You are light; give me light.'

17.4.2.a.m: A round brick with 'Heaven is unconquered...'

17.4.3.a.m: Here [he places] one seed-pouring brick for an old man.

17.4.4.a.s: prajāpatistvā sādayatu divaḥ pṛṣṭhe jyotiṣmatīmiti viśvajyotiṣam
17.4.4.a.d: प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु दिवः पृष्ठे ज्योतिष्मतीमिति विश्वज्योतिषम्
17.4.4.a.m: A Viśvajyotis brick with 'May Prajāpati seat you on the back of heaven, full of light.'

17.4.5.a.m: Two seasonal bricks with 'Tapas and Tapasya...', sharing the same deity-formula.

17.4.6.a.s: devānāṃ yānyasi devānāṃ devayānyasīti dve saṃyānyau
17.4.6.a.d: देवानां यान्यसि देवानां देवयान्यसीति द्वे संयान्यौ
17.4.6.a.m: Two Saṃyānī bricks with 'You are that which goes to the gods; you are that which goes on the path of the gods to the gods.'

17.4.7.a.s: saṃyānyāvṛtavye viśvajyotiṣaṃ retaḥsicaṃ hiraṇyeṣṭakāṃ maṇḍaleṣṭakāṃ vikarṇīṃ svayamātṛṇāmityevamanupūrvā eke samāmananti
17.4.7.a.d: संयान्यावृतव्ये विश्वज्योतिषं रेतःसिचं हिरण्येष्टकां मण्डलेष्टकां विकर्णीं स्वयमातृणामित्येवमनुपूर्वा एके समामनन्ति
17.4.7.a.m: Some teach them in this order: the two Saṃyānīs, the two seasonal, the Viśvajyotis, the seed-pouring, the gold brick, the round brick, the Vikarṇī, the naturally perforated.

17.4.8.a.m: Having performed the two afternoon rituals, he steeps udumbara kindling-sticks in ghee.

17.4.9.a.s: śvo bhūte paurvāhṇikībhyāṃ pracarya pañcamyāściteḥ śeṣaṃ yājñasenīṃ citiṃ cinoti
17.4.9.a.d: श्वो भूते पौर्वाह्णिकीभ्यां प्रचर्य पञ्चम्याश्चितेः शेषं याज्ञसेनीं चितिं चिनोति
17.4.9.a.m: On the next day, having performed the two morning rituals, he builds the remainder of the fifth layer, the Yājñasenī layer.

17.4.10.a.m: He lays three Gāyatrī [bricks] in the east with 'Agni is the head...';

17.4.10.b.m: likewise the subsequent sets of three:

17.4.10.f.m: Bṛhatīs, Uṣṇihs, Paṅktis, and Akṣarapaṅktis, [namely] the various meters, in the available spaces;

17.4.11.a.m: Elsewhere than in the thousand-brick piling, for one who desires cattle he piles the cattle-layer (gociti).

17.4.13.a.m: He should place them in the first layer, in the middle, or in the highest.

17.5.1.a.s: agne gobhirna ā gahītyanuvākena pratimantraṃ punaḥ punarabhyāsam
17.5.1.a.d: अग्ने गोभिर्न आ गहीत्यनुवाकेन प्रतिमन्त्रं पुनः पुनरभ्यासम्
17.5.1.a.m: Repeating again and again with each formula of the anuvāka: "Agni, come to us with cattle..."

17.5.2.a.s: indrāgnibhyāṃ tvā sayujā yujā yunajmītyaṣṭau sayujaḥ
17.5.2.a.d: इन्द्राग्निभ्यां त्वा सयुजा युजा युनज्मीत्यष्टौ सयुजः
17.5.2.a.m: With "For Indra and Agni I yoke you, yoke-mate with yoke-mate...", eight yoke-mate bricks (sayuj).

17.5.3.a.s: rohiteṣu tvā jīmūteṣu sādayāmyaruṇeṣu tvā kṛṣṇeṣu tvā nīleṣu tvā siteṣu tvā jīmūteṣu sādayāmīti pañca jīmūtāḥ
17.5.3.a.d: रोहितेषु त्वा जीमूतेषु सादयाम्यरुणेषु त्वा कृष्णेषु त्वा नीलेषु त्वा सितेषु त्वा जीमूतेषु सादयामीति पञ्च जीमूताः
17.5.3.a.m: With "I place you in the red clouds; I place you in the ruddy clouds; I place you in the black clouds; I place you in the dark-blue clouds; I place you in the white clouds...", five cloud bricks (jīmūta).

17.5.4.a.m: With "Ambā by name are you...", seven Kṛttikā bricks.

17.5.5.a.m: With "You are the winner of the east wind...", five rain-winning bricks, placing them around continuously.

17.5.6.a.m: With "For the ocean, you...", eight Āditya bricks.

17.5.7.a.s: ṛce tvā ruce tveti pañca ghṛteṣṭakā anuparihāram
17.5.7.a.d: ऋचे त्वा रुचे त्वेति पञ्च घृतेष्टका अनुपरिहारम्
17.5.7.a.m: With "For the Ṛc, you; for splendour, you...", five ghee bricks, placing them around continuously.

17.5.8.a.m: "Balls of ghee should be placed interwoven with the Āditya bricks," says the Vājasaneyaka.

17.5.9.a.m: With "You that give glory...", five glory-giving bricks (yaśodā).

17.5.10.a.m: With "You are the increaser...", five increasing bricks (bhūyaskṛt).

17.5.11.a.m: With "You that sit in the waters...", five forms of Agni (agnirūpa).

17.5.12.a.m: With "I place you in the wealth of the earth...", five wealth-giving bricks (draviṇodā).

17.5.13.a.m: With "Protect my breath...", six life-prolonging bricks (āyuṣyā).

17.5.14.a.m: With "O Agni, what is your supreme name, the heart...", the heart of Agni (agner hṛdaya).

17.5.16.a.m: "What divine brick you are, life-giving, lying near,

17.5.16.b.m: lie by me, as a wife ever by her husband;

17.5.16.c.s: yā devyasīṣṭake prāṇadā apānadā vyānadāścakṣurdā śrotradā vāgdā ātmadāḥ pṛthividā antarikṣadā dyaurdā svardāḥ kumārīdāḥ prapharvidāḥ prathamaupaśadā yuvatidā upaśīvarī /
17.5.16.c.d: या देव्यसीष्टके प्राणदा अपानदा व्यानदाश्चक्षुर्दा श्रोत्रदा वाग्दा आत्मदाः पृथिविदा अन्तरिक्षदा द्यौर्दा स्वर्दाः कुमारीदाः प्रफर्विदाः प्रथमौपशदा युवतिदा उपशीवरी ।
17.5.16.c.m: what divine bricks you are, giving out-breath, giving in-breath, giving diffused breath, giving sight, giving hearing, giving speech, giving self, giving earth, giving intermediate space, giving heaven, giving the sun-world, giving young maidens, giving lively women, giving the first head-ornament, giving youthful women, lying near,

17.5.16.d.m: lie by me, as a wife ever by her husband"—thus sixteen lying-near bricks (upaśīvarī).

17.6.1.a.s: abhīṣāccābhiṣavī cābhivayāścordhvavayāśca bṛhadvayāśca savayāśca sahvāṃśca sahamānaśca sahasvāṃsca sahīyāṃśceti daśendranāmāni
17.6.1.a.d: अभीषाच्चाभिषवी चाभिवयाश्चोर्ध्ववयाश्च बृहद्वयाश्च सवयाश्च सह्वांश्च सहमानश्च सहस्वांस्च सहीयांश्चेति दशेन्द्रनामानि
17.6.1.a.m: With "Abhīṣāh, and Abhiṣavī, and Abhivayas, and Ūrdhvavayas, and Bṛhadvayas, and Savayas, and Sahvan, and Sahamāna, and Sahasvan, and Sahīyas...", ten Indra names.

17.6.2.a.m: With "With Agni, the all-conquering...", twenty-two Indra bodies (indratanū).

17.6.3.a.m: With "Prajāpati with his mind reached out to the soma...", thirty-three sacrifice bodies (yajñatanū).

17.6.4.a.m: With "I place you, the luminous...", twelve luminous bricks (jyotiṣmatī).

17.6.5.a.s: pūrṇā paścāditi paurṇamāsīṃ purastādupadhāya kṛttikā nakṣatramiti nakṣatreṣṭakāḥ purastātpratīcīrasaṃspṛṣṭāḥ
17.6.5.a.d: पूर्णा पश्चादिति पौर्णमासीं पुरस्तादुपधाय कृत्तिका नक्षत्रमिति नक्षत्रेष्टकाः पुरस्तात्प्रतीचीरसंस्पृष्टाः
17.6.5.a.m: Having placed the full moon brick in front with "Full in the west...", he places the constellation bricks (nakṣatreṣṭakā) with "The Kṛttikās are the constellation...", running from east to west without touching [each other].

17.6.6.a.m: Having placed the previous one, [he places] the subsequent one and the subsequent one, up to the Viśākhās.

17.6.7.a.m: To the south of the naturally perforated brick (svayamātṛṇā), he carries forward the line.

17.6.8.a.m: Having placed the new moon brick in the west with "What the gods deposited...", of the remaining [constellations, he places] the previous and the previous one, up to the Apabharaṇīs.

17.6.9.a.m: To the north of the naturally perforated brick, he carries forward the line.

17.6.11.a.s: ṛce tvā ruce tveti sarvāsu nakṣatreṣṭakāsvanuṣajati
17.6.11.a.d: ऋचे त्वा रुचे त्वेति सर्वासु नक्षत्रेष्टकास्वनुषजति
17.6.11.a.m: With "For the Ṛc, you; for splendour, you...", he attaches [this mantra] to all the constellation bricks.

17.7.1.a.m: With "Hiranyagarbha came into being in the beginning...", eight river bricks (sarit).

17.7.2.a.s: viśvakarmā diśāṃ patiriti pañca hiraṇyeṣṭakāḥ pratidiśamekāṃ madhye
17.7.2.a.d: विश्वकर्मा दिशां पतिरिति पञ्च हिरण्येष्टकाः प्रतिदिशमेकां मध्ये
17.7.2.a.m: With "Viśvakarman, lord of the quarters...", five gold bricks (hiraṇyeṣṭakā): one in each direction and one in the middle.

17.7.3.a.s: prāṇāya tvā cakṣuṣe tveti catasraḥ svayamātṛṇāḥ pratidiśam
17.7.3.a.d: प्राणाय त्वा चक्षुषे त्वेति चतस्रः स्वयमातृणाः प्रतिदिशम्
17.7.3.a.m: With "For breath, you; for sight, you...", four naturally perforated bricks (svayamātṛṇā), one in each direction.

17.7.4.e.m: Agni, we think on a hymn of praise, successful today, touching heaven,

17.7.4.f.m: desirous of the god's wealth"—thus five forms of the days (ahar-rūpa).

17.7.5.a.m: Then he places the vow brick (vrata).

17.7.6.a.s: prācyā tvā diśā sādayāmīti pañcātmeṣṭakāḥ pratidiśamekāṃ madhye
17.7.6.a.d: प्राच्या त्वा दिशा सादयामीति पञ्चात्मेष्टकाः प्रतिदिशमेकां मध्ये
17.7.6.a.m: With "With the eastern direction I place you...", five body bricks (ātmeṣṭakā): one in each direction and one in the middle.

17.7.7.a.s: saṃyacca pracetāśceti pañca vaiśvadevīrātmani dveṣyaṃ manasā dhyāyan
17.7.7.a.d: संयच्च प्रचेताश्चेति पञ्च वैश्वदेवीरात्मनि द्वेष्यं मनसा ध्यायन्
17.7.7.a.m: With "Saṃyac and Pracetas...", [he places] five all-god bricks (vaiśvadevī) on the body [of the altar], contemplating in mind the person he hates.

17.7.8.a.s: kayā naścitra ā bhuvadūtī sadāvṛdhaḥ sakhā /
17.7.8.a.d: कया नश्चित्र आ भुवदूती सदावृधः सखा ।
17.7.8.a.m: "With what help will the wonderful one be present to us, the ever-increasing friend,

17.7.8.c.m: What true, most generous exhilaration of the drinks will gladden you with the draught,

17.7.8.e.m: Do protect us well, your friends, your praisers;

17.7.8.f.m: be present with a hundred aids"—thus the Vāmadevya [hymn].

17.8.2.a.m: "Indra, with the bones of Dadhīca, unresisted,

17.8.2.b.m: grew mighty, fierce, undefeated, slaying the obstacles"—thus the Atharvaśiras, ten [bricks] interlinked.

17.8.3.a.m: "In the eastern half there is the drawing out of the head;

17.8.4.a.s: abhi tvā śūra nonumo 'dugdhā iva dhenavaḥ /
17.8.4.a.d: अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमो ऽदुग्धा इव धेनवः ।
17.8.4.a.m: "Unto you, O hero, we roar aloud like unmilked cows,

17.8.4.b.m: to the lord of this moving world, beholding the sun, the lord, O Indra, of what stands still,

17.8.4.d.s: na tvāvām̐ anyo divyo na pārthivaḥ /
17.8.4.d.d: न त्वावाम्̐ अन्यो दिव्यो न पार्थिवः ।
17.8.4.d.m: None like you, neither celestial nor earthly,

17.8.4.e.s: na jāto na janiṣyate aśvāyanto maghavannindra vājinaḥ /
17.8.4.e.d: न जातो न जनिष्यते अश्वायन्तो मघवन्निन्द्र वाजिनः ।
17.8.4.e.m: “None has been born, nor will be born, equal to you. Desiring horses, bountiful Indra, rich in spoils,

17.8.4.f.s: gavyantastvā havāmaha iti rathaṃtaraṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣe 'dhyātmannapavargaḥ
17.8.4.f.d: गव्यन्तस्त्वा हवामह इति रथंतरं दक्षिणे पक्षे ऽध्यात्मन्नपवर्गः
17.8.4.f.m: desiring cattle, we call upon you”—with these words [he places the bricks of] the Rathaṃtara on the southern wing; the conclusion is on the body [of the altar].

17.8.5.a.m: Having placed the first, then the second, [he places] the viśayā brick:

17.8.6.a.m: half on the body, half on the wing.

17.8.7.a.m: “You indeed we call upon, the poets, in the winning of booty;

17.8.7.b.m: you, Indra, true lord amidst the foes, men [call upon] you in the racecourses, swift horse;

17.8.7.d.m: So, wonderful one, bolt in hand, boldly,

17.8.7.g.m: scatter cow, horse, chariot-horse, O Indra;

17.8.7.h.s: satrā vājaṃ na jigyuṣa iti bṛhaduttare pakṣe
17.8.7.h.d: सत्रा वाजं न जिग्युष इति बृहदुत्तरे पक्षे
17.8.7.h.m: bestow booty at once upon the winner”—with these words [he places the bricks of] the Bṛhat on the northern wing.

17.8.8.a.m: Its procedure is like that of the Rathaṃtara.

17.9.1.a.s: yajñāyajñā vo agnaye girāgirā ca dakṣase /
17.9.1.a.d: यज्ञायज्ञा वो अग्नये गिरागिरा च दक्षसे ।
17.9.1.a.m: “At every sacrifice for your Agni, with song after song for the capable,

17.9.1.b.s: prapra vayamamṛtaṃ jātavedasaṃ priyaṃ mitraṃ na śamsiṣam /
17.9.1.b.d: प्रप्र वयममृतं जातवेदसं प्रियं मित्रं न शम्सिषम् ।
17.9.1.b.m:
forth we sing the immortal Jātavedas, like a dear friend;

like a dear friend.

17.9.1.d.m: He, the child of strength, being well disposed toward us,

17.9.1.g.m: May he be our helper in battles, may he be our increaser,

17.9.1.h.m: and the protector of our bodies”—with these words [he places the bricks of] the Yajñāyajñīya on the tail.

17.9.2.a.m: Its procedure is like that of the Rathaṃtara.

17.9.3.a.m: Having placed the bull brick with “You, Agni, the bull...”, [he places] the Prājāpatyā brick with “Image of the year...”.

17.9.4.a.m: With “For him who has a hundred weapons, a hundred strengths...”, [he places] five Ājyānī bricks, one in each quarter and one in the middle.

17.9.5.a.s: indrasya vajro 'sīti catasro vajriṇīḥ pratidiśamaśmana iṣuhasta upadadhāti
17.9.5.a.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति चतस्रो वज्रिणीः प्रतिदिशमश्मन इषुहस्त उपदधाति
17.9.5.a.m: With “You are Indra's bolt...”, holding an arrow in his hand, he places four Vajriṇī stones in each quarter.

17.9.6.a.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसि वार्त्रघ्नस्तनूपा नः प्रतिस्पशः ।
17.9.6.a.m: “You are Indra’s bolt, slayer of Vṛtra, protector of our bodies, confronting spies.

17.9.6.b.s: yo na upariṣṭādaghāyurabhidāsatyetaṃ so 'śmānamṛcchatviti madhye pañcamīmeke samāmananti
17.9.6.b.d: यो न उपरिष्टादघायुरभिदासत्येतं सो ऽश्मानमृच्छत्विति मध्ये पञ्चमीमेके समामनन्ति
17.9.6.b.m: Whoever attacks us from above with evil intent, may he meet this stone”—with these words some teach a fifth in the middle.

17.9.7.a.s: pṛthivyai tvāntarikṣāya tvā dive tveti tisro lokeṣṭakāḥ
17.9.7.a.d: पृथिव्यै त्वान्तरिक्षाय त्वा दिवे त्वेति तिस्रो लोकेष्टकाः
17.9.7.a.m: With “To the earth you, to the atmosphere you, to heaven you”, [he places] three Lokeṣṭakā bricks.

17.9.8.a.s: agnaye tvā pavamānāyāgnaye tvā pāvakāyāgnaye tvā śucaya iti tisraḥ pāvamānīḥ
17.9.8.a.d: अग्नये त्वा पवमानायाग्नये त्वा पावकायाग्नये त्वा शुचय इति तिस्रः पावमानीः
17.9.8.a.m: With “To Agni Pavamāna you, to Agni Pāvaka you, to Agni Śuci you”, [he places] three Pāvamānī bricks.

17.10.1.a.s: ṛcā tvā chandasā sādayāmi vaṣaṭkāreṇa tvā chandasā sādayāmi hiṅkāreṇa tvā chandasā sādayāmi prastāvena tvā chandasā sādayāmi pratihāreṇa tvā chandasā sādayāmyudgīthena tvā chandasā sādayāmi nidhanena tvā chandasā sādayāmīti sapta cchandasyāḥ
17.10.1.a.d: ऋचा त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि वषट्कारेण त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि हिङ्कारेण त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि प्रस्तावेन त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि प्रतिहारेण त्वा छन्दसा सादयाम्युद्गीथेन त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि निधनेन त्वा छन्दसा सादयामीति सप्त च्छन्दस्याः
17.10.1.a.m: “With the ṛc metre I settle you; with the vaṣaṭ-call metre I settle you; with the hiṅ-sound metre I settle you; with the prastāva metre I settle you; with the pratihāra metre I settle you; with the udgītha metre I settle you; with the nidhana metre I settle you”—thus [he places] the seven Chandasyā bricks.

17.10.2.a.s: ange yaśasvinniti catasro rāṣṭrabhṛtaḥ purastādupadhāya hiraṇyeṣṭakābhiḥ sarvato mukhamupadadhāti
17.10.2.a.d: अन्गे यशस्विन्निति चतस्रो राष्ट्रभृतः पुरस्तादुपधाय हिरण्येष्टकाभिः सर्वतो मुखमुपदधाति
17.10.2.a.m: Having placed the four Rāṣṭrabhṛt bricks in front with “O body, glorious...”, he places [the layer] facing in all directions with gold bricks.

17.10.3.a.m: It has been said: “He places the Gāyatrī in front”.

17.10.4.b.s: gāyatrīṃ purastādupadadhāti triṣṭubhaṃ dakṣiṇato jagatīṃ paścādanuṣṭubhamuttarataḥ paṅktiṃ madhye /
17.10.4.b.d: गायत्रीं पुरस्तादुपदधाति त्रिष्टुभं दक्षिणतो जगतीं पश्चादनुष्टुभमुत्तरतः पङ्क्तिं मध्ये ।
17.10.4.b.m: “He places the Gāyatrī in front, the Triṣṭubh in the south, the Jagatī in the west, the Anuṣṭubh in the north, the Paṅkti in the middle”—

17.10.4.c.m: with all of these he places [the layer] facing in all directions.

17.10.5.a.m: They begin with the Gāyatrī and end with the Paṅkti.

17.10.7.a.s: agna ā yāhi vītaya iti caitābhiḥ sarvato mukhamupadadhāti
17.10.7.a.d: अग्न आ याहि वीतय इति चैताभिः सर्वतो मुखमुपदधाति
17.10.7.a.m: And with these [verses beginning with] “Come, Agni, to the feast...”, he places [bricks] facing in all directions.

17.10.9.a.m: Or here he may place the Vikarṇī and the Svayamātṛṇā.

17.10.10.a.m: The end of the layer is with Lokaṃpṛṇā [bricks] and the like.
